The second man said: No, I am its owner, for I massaged its bearer and kneaded its joints. The bath-keeper said: Bring me the owner of the head so I may ask him: Does this head belong to you or to him? They brought me and said: We have a testimony for you to give, so appear. I stood up and came, whether I wished or not. The bath-keeper said: Man, do not speak anything but the truth, do not testify to anything but what is right, and tell me: To which of these two does this head belong? I said: May God preserve you, this is my head. It has accompanied me on the road, it has circled the Ancient House <note>the Kaaba in Mecca</note> with me, and I have no doubt that it is mine. He said to me: Be quiet, you meddler. Then he leaned toward one of the claimants and said: Man, how long will this rivalry with people continue over this head? Turn away from its slight value, to the curse of God and the heat of His <term>Saqar</term> <gloss>Hellfire</gloss>. Suppose this head is not [yours], and I did not see this "not."

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us: I stood up from that place ashamed, my clothes in disarray, and I slipped out of the bath in haste. I cursed the boy with <term>ass</term> and <term>mass</term> <note>terms suggesting harsh reprimand or insults</note> and pushed him with the force of pounding gypsum. I said to another: Go and bring me a cupper who will remove this weight from me. He brought me a man of gentle build, beautiful adornment, in the image of a doll. I was comforted by him, and he entered and said: Peace be upon you, and from which country are you? I said: From Famm <note>possibly a pun on the city or literally "a mouth"</note>. He said: May God greet you from the land of grace and luxury, the land of the <term>Sunnah</term> <gloss>tradition of the Prophet</gloss> and the community. I attended its mosque in the month of Ramadan when the lamps were lit and the <term>Tarawih</term> <gloss>special nightly Ramadan prayers</gloss> were established. We did not notice until the night stretched out and overtook those lamps. But God worked for me with a shoe... <note>The text here becomes nonsensical and rambling, characteristic of the character's madness.</note> ...but how was your pilgrimage? Did you perform its rites as required, and did they cry "Wonder, wonder"? I looked at the minaret, and how easy is war for the spectators! I found the <term>Harisa</term> <gloss>a meat and wheat porridge</gloss> as it was, and I knew the matter was by the decree and destiny of God. Until when is this distress? Today and tomorrow, Saturday and Sunday. I will not lengthen this chatter, but I wanted you to know that the file in grammar is the sharpness of the razor, so do not busy yourself with the talk of the commoners. Had the ability existed before the act, you would have shaved your head. So, do you see that we should begin?

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us: I remained bewildered by his eloquence within his delirium. I feared his sitting would be long, so I said: Until tomorrow, God willing. I asked those present about him, and they said: This is a man from the lands of Alexandria. This water did not agree with him, so melancholy overcame him. He raves all day as you see, though he possesses much merit. I said: I have heard of him, and his madness burdened me, and I began to say:

# The Nahidiyya Maqama

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying:
I inclined with a group of my companions toward the courtyard of a tent, seeking hospitality from its people. A man came out to us, burning with intensity, and said: Who are you? We said: Guests who have not tasted anything for three days. He said: Move aside. Then he said: O youths, [how about] a <term>Nahida</term> <gloss>a thick porridge</gloss> made of milk, shimmering like the pate of a bald man, in a wide bowl, crowned with a drop of clarified butter from the regions of a giant? The bowl is full of the pleasure of the mouth, for a group of five, hungry and thirsty, in which the molar tooth disappears as if its kernels were the tongues of birds. They are ignoring the <term>Nahida</term> in it along with... <note>The text descends into highly stylized, obscure culinary descriptions of a feast.</note> ...do you desire it, O youths? We said: Yes, by God, we desire it. The old man laughed and said: Your uncle also desires it. Then he said: What is your opinion, O youths, in fine flour like pieces of bullion...? <note>The narrative continues with an elaborate, humorous description of the preparation of a feast, meant to tease the hungry guests.</note> ...We said: Yes, by God, we desire it. The old man laughed and said: Your uncle, by God, does not hate it! He then said: What is your opinion, O youths, in a Najdi she-goat...? <note>He continues describing a succulent roast in exquisite, flowery, and teasing detail.</note> ...We said: Yes, by God, we desire it. He said: And your uncle, by God, dances for it! Then some of us jumped at him with a sword and said: What...

text:
The second said: "Rather, I am its owner; for I rubbed its bearer, and kneaded his joints." The bathhouse keeper said: "Bring me the owner of the head, and I shall ask him. Is this head yours, or is it his?" They brought me to him and said: "We have a testimony from you, so appear." I stood up and came, whether I wanted to or not. The bathhouse keeper said: "O man, say nothing but the truth, and do not bear witness to anything but what is just. Tell me, to which of these two does this head belong?" I said: "May God grant you well-being, this is my head. It has accompanied me on the road, it has circled with me around the Ancient House <note>the Kaaba in Mecca</note>, and I have no doubt that it is mine." He said to me: "Be silent, you meddler!" Then he turned to one of the two disputants and said: "O man, how long will this competition over people continue with this head? Seek solace from its little worth, may you be cursed by God and the heat of His Sqar <note>a name for Hell</note>. Grant that this head is not, and that I have not seen this 'is not'."

Isa ibn Hisham said: I rose from that place ashamed, with my clothes in a state of agitation, and I slipped out of the bathhouse in a hurry. I cursed the youth with the <term>ass</term> <gloss>beating</gloss> and the <term>mass</term> <gloss>crushing</gloss>, and I pushed him with a blow like the pounding of gypsum. I said to another: "Go and bring me a cupper who will remove this burden from me." He brought me a man of fine build, handsome in attire, in the image of a doll. I felt at ease with him. He entered and said: "Peace be upon you, and from which land are you?" I said: "From Fars." He said: "May God revive you from the land of grace and prosperity, and the land of the <term>Sunnah</term> <gloss>Prophetic tradition</gloss> and the <term>Jama'ah</term> <gloss>community of believers</gloss>. I attended its congregational mosque in the month of Ramadan, when the lamps were lit and the <term>Tarawih</term> <gloss>extra evening prayers in Ramadan</gloss> were established. We did not notice until the night grew long and passed over those lanterns. But God worked for me with a light <note>referring to a shoe</note> whose tongue I had been, yet its laces did not reach its sleeve, and the boy returned to his mother after I had prayed the night prayer and the shadow had leveled. But how was your pilgrimage? Did you complete its rites as required, while they cried 'the wonder, the wonder'?" I looked at the minaret—and how easy war is for the spectators—and I found the <term>harisah</term> <gloss>a porridge dish made of meat and wheat</gloss> as it was, and I knew that the matter was by the decree and judgment of God. How long must this frustration last? Today and tomorrow, Saturday and Sunday—I shall not prolong this, and what is all this chatter? But I wanted you to know that the <term>Mubarrad</term> <gloss>a famous grammarian</gloss> regarding grammar is like the sharpness of a razor, so do not busy yourself with the talk of the commoners. If the capacity existed before the act, you would have already shaved your head. So, do you think we should begin?

Isa ibn Hisham said: I remained bewildered by his articulation within his delirium, and I feared that his sitting would be long. I said: "Until tomorrow, if God wills." I asked those present about him, and they said: "This is a man from the lands of Alexandria. This water did not agree with him, so melancholy has overcome him. He babbles all day as you see, and behind it is much virtue." I said: "I have heard of him, and his madness weighs heavy on me," and I began to recite:

I give a pledge to God
I will not shave my head while I live
Firm in my vow is the pact
Even if I encounter hardship

The Nahdiyya Maqama

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying:
I inclined with a group of my companions toward the courtyard of a tent, seeking hospitality from its people. A man of thin stature came out to us and said: "Who are you?" We said: "Guests who have not tasted food for three days, fleeing enemies." He said: "Then step aside." Then he said: "O youths, what of a <term>nahida</term> <gloss>a dish of curdled milk and honey</gloss> as delicate as the crown of a bald man, in a wide bowl, crowned with the fragrance of an expert from the regions of a giant, crouched in its unity, filled with the flavor of the mouth, from a group famished with five thirsts, where the molar disappears? As if its kernels were the tongues of birds, they neglect the <term>nahida</term> in it along with the deep containers from which they have milked the aged, fat, pyramid-like beasts. Do you desire it, O youths?" We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it." The old man chuckled and said: "And your uncle also desires it." Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of fine white flour as if it were pieces of ingots, kneaded on a platter that has the scent of acacia? A nimble, clever, and light youth leaps toward it, kneading it without trembling or rustling, making it soft as fine silk. Then he twists it with a pestle or a crusher in abundance, then intends to fold it and leave it in the corner of the cool place. When it has risen without cracking, he intends to seek the wood of the <term>ghada</term> <gloss>a type of desert tree</gloss> and ignites a fire in it. When the fire dims, he levels its embers, then turns to his dough and throws it after having well-colored it, then spreads it upon it, then covers it until it settles. He then turns upon it the heated stones until the heat meets from both sides. When he covers them on the ashes with a lid, and it emerges transparent, its crust resembling companions, and its redness the redness of the Hijazi <term>busr</term> <gloss>unripe dates</gloss> famous in the mother of lizards or the <term>adq</term> of Ibn Tab, he pours upon it a white dressing like snow until it settles into the crevices of the oil. The core of the fine flour drinks what is upon it of the dressing. I present it to you so you may take it in mouthfuls of enjoyment or delight. Do you desire it, O youths?" He said: Everyone among us stretched out toward his description, and our saliva flowed, and we smacked our lips and clicked our tongues. We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it." He said: The old man chuckled and said: "And your uncle, by God, does not despise it." Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of a Najdi female kid, highland and wild, that has eaten the bitter plants, the Najdi wormwood, the lavender, and the withered grass? It has quenched its thirst with warm water, and filled itself with the shirt <note>metaphor for rich grazing</note> while it was fresh. Its fat has spread, it trots in contentment, then is cast into a furnace until it is cooked without burning or finishing. Then we present it to you, its skin having covered a white fat upon a tray layered with thin breads like spread-out fine linen or dyed red fabric, and holes have been made in it containing juices and various seasonings. It is placed between you, sweating and smelling of broth, and smelling of broth. Do you desire it, O youths?" We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it." He said: "And your uncle, by God, dances for it." Then some of us leaped toward him with a sword and said: "What..."

<summary>Isa ibn Hisham reflects on a confusing barber in a bathhouse and later encounters an old man who describes elaborate, mouth-watering dishes with intense poetic detail.</summary>
<keywords>bathhouse, barber, melancholy, Alexandria, Nahdiyya Maqama, hospitality, food description</keywords>

And the second said: "Rather, I am its owner, for I massaged his carrier <note>his body</note> and kneaded his joints."

The bathhouse keeper said: "Bring me the owner of the head so I may ask him: is this head yours or his?"

So they both came to me and said: "We require your testimony, so present yourself." I stood up and came, whether I willed it or not. The bathhouse keeper said: "O man, speak nothing but the truth, and do not testify to anything but the right. Tell me: to which of these two does this head belong?"

I said: "May God grant you health! This is my head; it accompanied me on the road and circumambulated the Ancient House <note>the Kaaba in Mecca</note> with me, and I never doubted that it was mine."

He said to me: "Silence, you meddler!" Then he turned to one of the two litigants and said: "O you! How long will this rivalry with people over this head continue? Withdraw from its meager worth, lest you face the curse of God and the heat of <term>Saqar</term> <gloss>Hellfire</gloss>. Even if we suppose this head does not exist, I have not seen this non-existence."

Isa ibn Hisham said: I stood up from that place in shame, not wearing clothes out of fear, and I slipped out of the bath in haste. I cursed the servant with every insult and struck him like one pounding gypsum. Then I said to another: "Go and bring me a barber to relieve me of this weight <note>the hair on his head</note>."

He brought me a man of delicate build, handsome appearance, and looking like a statue. I felt at ease with him. He entered and said: "Peace be upon you. From which land are you?"

I said: "From Qumm."

He said: "May God give you life! From the land of bounty and prosperity, and the city of the <term>Sunnah</term> and the <term>Jama'ah</term> <gloss>the orthodox community</gloss>. I was present in its congregational mosque during the month of Ramadan when the lamps were lit and the <term>Tarawih</term> <gloss>nightly Ramadan prayers</gloss> were performed. We only felt the night lengthen when it reached those lamps; but God acted kindly toward me regarding a leather boot whose tongue was moist, yet its fringes did not get on its sleeve, and the boy returned to his mother after I prayed the late evening prayer and the shadow leveled out. But how was your pilgrimage? Did you perform its rituals as required, while they cried out in great wonder? I looked at the minaret—and how easy is war to the spectators! I found the <term>harisa</term> <gloss>a thick meat and wheat porridge</gloss> as it was, and I knew that the matter is by the decree of God and fate. How long shall this annoyance last? Today and tomorrow, Saturday and Sunday... I shall not be long, for what is all this talk? But I wanted you to know that <term>al-Mubarrad</term> <note>a famous grammarian</note> in grammar is like the iron of a razor, so do not occupy yourself with the talk of the commoners. If the capacity preceded the action, you would have already shaved your head! Do you think we should begin?"

Isa ibn Hisham said: I remained bewildered by the eloquence of his nonsense, and I feared his session would go on forever. I said: "Until tomorrow, God willing." I asked those present about him, and they said: "This is a man from the lands of Alexandria; this water did not agree with him, so <term>black bile</term> <gloss>melancholy/madness</gloss> overcame him. He raves all day as you see, though he possesses much hidden merit."

I said: "I have heard of him, and his madness grieves me." And I began to say:

->An oath firmly bound<-

# The Nahid Maqama

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying:
I turned with a group of my companions toward the courtyard of a tent to seek hospitality <note>food for guests</note> from its people. A scorched-looking man <note>likely sunburnt or weather-beaten</note> came out to us and said: "Who are you?"

We said: "Guests who have not tasted an enemy <note>meaning a meal, used ironically</note> for three days."

He said: "Move aside." Then he said: "O youths, what is your opinion of some <term>nahidah</term> <gloss>thick butter or cream mixed with flour</gloss>, trembling like the crown of a bald man's head, in a wide bowl, crowned with a choice date-paste from the sides of a great, sturdy palm tree, a single one of which fills the mouth, for a group of hungry and thirsty men? The tooth vanishes into it, and its pits are like the tongues of birds. They scoop the <term>nahidah</term> with cups of milk milked from old, sturdy, well-fed camels. Do you desire it, O youths?"

We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it!"

The old man laughed loudly and said: "And your uncle <note>meaning himself</note> also desires it!"

Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of fine white bread <note>original: <term>darmak</term></note> like pieces of silver ingots, arranged on a leather mat smelling of mimosa? Then a bright, clever, and light youth leaps to it and kneads it without shaking it or breaking it, making it smoother than a soft king. Then he mixes it with milk or a pestle until it is thick, then he turns it and leaves it in the corner of a stone oven until it is leavened without becoming dry. Then he turns to the wood of the <term>ghada</term> tree and lights the fire. When its flame dies down, he prepares its place in the hot ashes, then takes his dough and tosses it after perfecting its color. He spreads it over the embers, then covers it until it swells and rises. He heaps over it hot stones that meet with two glows, until when he covers them in the matching embers with a lid, it cracks open transparently, its crust resembling fine parchment and its redness like the famous red dates of the Hijaz known as <term>Umm al-Jirdan</term> or <term>Adh-dhiq ibn Tab</term>. Then he sprinkles over it something white as snow <note>sugar or fat</note> until it sinks into the crevices of the fat, and the heart of the bread drinks what is upon it. I present it to you and you swallow it in great gulps. Do you desire it, O youths?"

He said: Each of us craned his neck at his description, his mouth watering, smacking his lips and tasting the air. We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it!"

He said: The old man laughed and said: "And by God, your uncle does not hate it!" Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of a young she-goat from Najd, high-bred and wild, that has eaten the mimosa blossoms, the Najdi wormwood, the yarrow, and dry herbage? She has sipped the summer water and filled herself with the lush grass until her sides are bursting. She is slaughtered while in prime condition, then hung in a pit-oven until she is cooked through without being scorched or underdone. Then we present her to you, her skin covering white fat, on a table arranged with thin loaves like spread fine linens or dyed cloths. She is placed between you, dripping with fat and oozing with broth. Do you desire it, O youths?"

We said: "Yes, by God, we desire it!"

He said: "And by God, your uncle dances for it!"

Then one of us leaped toward him with a sword and said: "What—"

<meta>This page continues the legal discussion regarding who is eligible to bring the First Fruits (Bikkurim) and recite the accompanying declaration. It concludes Chapter 1 by clarifying land ownership requirements and begins Chapter 2, which uses a comparative legal framework to distinguish between First Fruits, the Priestly Heave-offering (Terumah), and the Tithe (Ma'aser).</meta>

->11<-
The one who buys three trees within the field of another person,
brings the fruits and recites the declaration. <note>In Jewish law, purchasing three trees traditionally includes ownership of the land surrounding them, which allows the buyer to truthfully recite the biblical verse: "the land which You, O Lord, have given me."</note>
**Rabbi Meir** says:
Even if he only bought two trees.
If he bought a single tree and the ground it sits on,
he brings the fruits and recites.
**Rabbi Yehuda** says:
Even sharecroppers and those who lease land bring the fruits and recite. <note>Rabbi Yehuda holds a more lenient view, allowing those who work the land but do not own it to still participate in the full ceremony.</note>

# Chapter 2

## Tractate Bikkurim Chapter 2 Mishnah 1
->1<-
The **Terumah** <term>Terumah: the "heave-offering" or portion of the harvest given to the Priest</term> and the **First Fruits**,
carry the liability of **death** <note>referring to "death by the hands of Heaven," a spiritual penalty for a non-priest who eats these items intentionally</note> and the **Fifth**, <term>Chomesh: a 20% penalty added to the principal value when someone unintentionally eats or uses holy items, which is then paid to the priest</term>
and they are forbidden to **strangers**, <note>original: "zarim"—referring to anyone who is not a Kohen (Priest)</note>
and they are the property of the **Priest**,
and they are neutralized in a mixture of **one hundred and one**, <note>If one part of these holy items accidentally mixes with one hundred parts of ordinary food, the holy status is "dissolved," and the mixture may be eaten by non-priests.</note>
and they require **washing of the hands** and **the setting of the sun**. <note>A priest who was ritually impure must immerse in a ritual bath and wait until sunset before he is permitted to eat these holy offerings.</note>
Behold, these laws apply to Terumah and First Fruits,
which is not the case for the **Tithe**. <term>Ma'aser: the "Second Tithe" (Ma'aser Sheni) which was brought to Jerusalem to be eaten by the owner</term>

## Tractate Bikkurim Chapter 2 Mishnah 2
->2<-
There are rules regarding the **Tithe** and **First Fruits** that do not apply to **Terumah**:
For the Tithe and the First Fruits require **being brought to the Place**, <note>referring to the Temple in Jerusalem</note>
and they require the **Confession**, <note>a formal declaration made at the Temple acknowledging that one has fulfilled all tithing obligations</note> and they are forbidden to a **mourner**; <term>Onen: a person in the intense first day of mourning before their deceased relative has been buried</term>
**Rabbi Shimon** permits a mourner to eat them.
And they are subject to the laws of **removal**. <note>Bi'ur: the requirement to clear all holy produce from one's home every three years</note>
**Rabbi Shimon** exempts them from removal.
And it is forbidden to eat even the smallest amount of them outside of **Jerusalem**,
and their **offshoots** <note>referring to crops grown from the seeds of these holy fruits</note> are forbidden to be eaten in Jerusalem,
even by non-priests or as animal feed.
**Rabbi Shimon** permits these.
Behold, these laws apply to the Tithe and First Fruits,
which is not the case for Terumah.

text:
no person is without, since belief in what one has been tasked with knowing is attained through them: namely, rhetorical, dialectical, and demonstrative evidence. So, one who is stubborn regarding such things, if it is a foundation of the foundations of the Law, is a disbeliever, either by his tongue while not in his heart, or by his negligence in failing to expose himself to learning its evidence. For if he were a person of <term>demonstration</term> <gloss>logical proof</gloss>, a way would have been made for him to believe in it through demonstration; if he were a person of dialectic, through dialectic; and if he were a person of exhortation, through exhortation. Therefore, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say 'There is no god but God' and believe in me," meaning by whatever path occurs to them among the three paths of faith. As for the things which, due to their hidden nature, are not known except by demonstration, God has been gentle to His servants who have no path to demonstration—either due to their natural disposition, their custom, or their lack of the means of learning—by setting for them parables and likenesses, and calling them to believe in those parables, since it is possible for belief to occur in those parables through the evidence common to all, namely the dialectical and the rhetorical. This is the reason why the Law is divided into apparent and hidden. The apparent is those parables set for those meanings, and the hidden is those meanings which do not manifest except to the people of demonstration. These are the types of those four or five existing things mentioned by <term>Abu Hamid</term> <gloss>Al-Ghazali</gloss> in his book *The Decisive Criterion* <note>original: "كتاب التفرقة"</note>. If it happens, as we said, that we know a thing by itself through the three methods, we do not need to set parables for it, and it would be according to its apparent meaning, not subject to interpretation. If this type of apparent [meaning] is in the foundations, then the one who interprets it is an infidel, like one who believes that there is no afterlife happiness or misery here, and that the only purpose of this statement is for people to be safe from one another in their bodies and senses, and that it is a trick, and that there is no end for man except his sensory existence only. If this is established,

<summary>Averroes explains the three types of evidence (rhetorical, dialectical, demonstrative) and argues that the Law contains apparent meanings for the masses and hidden meanings for the learned.</summary>
<keywords>demonstration, dialectic, exhortation, Abu Hamid, Al-Ghazali, interpretation, Law, apparent, hidden, afterlife</keywords>

...a part out of one hundred and nine parts of a share. So you make the share one hundred and nine parts, and multiply the thirteen by one hundred and nine parts, and add to that eighty parts, and it becomes one thousand four hundred and ninety-seven, and the husband's portion is three hundred and twenty-seven.

If you leave two sisters and a wife, and bequeath to a man the equivalent of a sister's portion minus one-eighth of what remains of the <term>mal</term> after the legacy, the method for that is to set the distribution of the estate at twelve shares for each sister, a third of what remains of the <term>mal</term> after the legacy. You know that one-eighth of what remains with the legacy equals a sister's portion. So one-eighth of what remains is one-eighth of a <term>mal</term> minus one-eighth of a legacy. So one-eighth of a <term>mal</term> minus one-eighth of a legacy plus a legacy equals a sister's portion, which is one-eighth of a <term>mal</term> plus seven-eighths of a legacy. The whole <term>mal</term> equals three-eighths of a <term>mal</term> plus one-third of a legacy and five-eighths of a legacy. Subtract three-eighths from the <term>mal</term>, and there remains five-eighths of the <term>mal</term> equaling three legacies and five-eighths of a legacy. The whole <term>mal</term> equals five legacies and four-fifths of a legacy. The <term>mal</term> is twenty-nine, the legacy is five, and the portion is eight.

In another method of legacies, a man died and left four sons and bequeathed to a man the equivalent of the portion of one of his sons and to another a quarter of what remains of the third. Know that the legacy is only from the third.

You multiply thirteen by one hundred and nine parts and add eighty parts to that, which results in one thousand four hundred and ninety-seven. The share of the husband is three hundred and twenty-seven.

If a woman leaves two sisters and a husband, and bequeaths to a man the equivalent of a sister's portion minus one-eighth of what remains of the estate after the legacy, the calculation is as follows: You establish the fixed shares of inheritance <note>original: "al-faridah"</note> from twelve shares. Each sister receives one-third of what remains of the estate after the legacy. This is the estate minus the legacy. You know that one-eighth of what remains plus the legacy equals a sister's portion. One-eighth of what remains is one-eighth of the estate minus one-eighth of the legacy. Thus, one-eighth of the estate minus one-eighth of the legacy plus the legacy equals a sister's portion. This is equal to one-eighth of the estate and seven-eighths of the legacy. The total estate then equals three-eighths of the estate plus three legacies and five-eighths of a legacy. Subtract three-eighths from the estate, and five-eighths of the estate remains, equaling three legacies and five-eighths of a legacy. The whole estate then equals five legacies and four-fifths of a legacy. Thus, the estate is twenty-nine, the legacy is five, and the portion is eight.

In another type of legacy, a man dies and leaves four sons. He bequeaths to a man the equivalent of one of his sons' portions, and to another man a quarter of what remains of the third. Know that this legacy is only taken from the third.

...its companion and its follower. Its names are also numerous. Among them is <term>Soma</term>, because it is auspicious, and auspicious [planets] are called <term>Soma-kara</term> <gloss>moon-doer/auspicious-doer</gloss>, while the malefics are called <term>Papa-kara</term> <gloss>evil-doer</gloss>. He also said in the <term>Gita</term>, "I am like the <term>Vasant</term>," that is, the equinox in the sixths of the year; this has testified to the correctness of what is at the beginning of the months, they participate in the names of the [lunar] mansions; each month is distinguished by a number of mansions, its name being derived from one of them.</meta>

Its companions and followers are numerous. Among them is <term>Soma</term> <gloss>Moon</gloss>, because he is a <term>Saumya</term> <gloss>benefic</gloss>, and the benefics are called <term>Saumya-Graha</term> <gloss>benefic planet</gloss>, while the malefics are called <term>Papa-Graha</term> <gloss>malefic planet</gloss>. Among them is <term>Nishisha</term> <gloss>Lord of the Night</gloss>, <term>Nakshatranatha</term> <gloss>Lord of the Mansions</gloss>, <term>Dvijeshvara</term> <gloss>Lord of the Twice-Born</gloss>, and <term>Shitanshu</term> <gloss>Cold-Rayed</gloss>, because his sphere is moist, and it contains <term>Hana</term> <gloss>dew/moisture</gloss>. When the rays fall upon him, they become cool, as is his own coolness, and reflect, illuminating the darkness, cooling the night, and extinguishing what the sun corrupted by its burning. For this reason, it is also called <term>Chandra</term>. It is the left eye of <term>Narayana</term> <gloss>the Supreme Being/Vishnu</gloss>, just as the sun is his right eye. # Portion of Re'eh - Torah Or - Gate
## Page 94b

As it is said: "You shall not work the firstborn of your ox" <note>original: *lo ta'avor bekhor shorekha*</note>. **484:** Not to shear the firstborn animal, and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it says: "You shall not shear the firstborn of your sheep" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. **485:** Not to eat leaven <term>Chametz; leavened grain products</term> on the 14th of Nisan after midday, as it says: "You shall not eat leaven with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>—meaning, during the time of the slaughtering of the Passover sacrifice, which begins after midday. **486:** Not to leave over the meat of the festival offering of the 14th until the third day, as it says: "Neither shall any of the meat... remain overnight" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. **487:** Not to offer the Passover sacrifice on a private altar <term>Bamat Yachid; a localized altar used before the central Temple was established</term>, as it says: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates." **488:** The commandment of rejoicing on the festivals, as it is said: "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God." **489:** The commandment of appearing [at the Temple], every male three times a year. **490:** That we should not go up to the Chosen House <term>Beit HaBechirah; the Holy Temple in Jerusalem</term> on a festival without a sacrifice, as it says: "And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed."

### **Torah Or**
The commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: **Torah, Service (Avodah), and Deeds of Loving-kindness.**

**Torah** consists of the commands "do not add" and "do not subtract," which demonstrate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is perfectly complete cannot be called "lacking" or "excessive." For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could accept an addition, it would mean it was not previously finished. Therefore, the definition of "perfection" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is linked to His Great Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>, as it is written: "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated on this in my commentary on Tractate Shevuot, in the chapter "Torah Or." As it is written in the Zohar regarding the verse "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters *Yod-He* (Y-H) together with "My Name" (*Shmi*) numerically equal 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>. The letters *Vav-He* (V-H) with "My Memorial" (*Zikhri*) equal 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. It is also written: "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>; He is the absolute Perfection, having no subtraction or addition. Regarding this, the warning comes: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>. This is a warning not to erase the Name of God or to destroy a stone from the Sanctuary. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the house in which the Blessed One dwells, and so too is the Sanctuary. It is written: "I am the Lord, that is My name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like a frame for the house, and His Name is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God."

**Service (Avodah)** comprises most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command was given to have a permanent location in the Chosen House <note>The Temple</note>. The Torah gives a reason for this: "To His dwelling you shall seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "His dwelling" hints at the *Shekhinah* <term>the Divine Presence</term>, which is the palace for the Name... as it is said, "Do not fear, for she dwells within me," for in the Sanctuary, the Glory <term>Tiferet; a divine attribute</term> is unified with His people. This is the meaning of "to place His name there," which the Targum <note>Aramaic translation</note> renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness, "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>, which refers to the *Kelipot* <term>husks; spiritual forces of impurity</term>. Therefore, "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes**
Sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them back inside. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the "branch" returns to its "root." It is written of them: "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an ascent <note>The word for 'offer,' *Ta'aleh*, shares a root with 'ascent'</note> and not outside. Since the holiness is found in the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, we are commanded to "turn away from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped [idols]. We must uproot and eradicate them. This was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this hints that the ten nations <note>the Canaanite tribes</note> were not merely idolaters; rather, the nations in the Land of Israel, being under the direct dominion of the Honorable Name, were "cutting the shoots" <note>a metaphor for heresy/spiritual sabotage</note> through their worship, which is true idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the dominion of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking even one stone of the Sanctuary, conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and lose an "Apostate City" <term>Ir HaNidachat; a city led astray to idolatry</term> and never to rebuild it, for its location is impure. Similarly, the "Enticer" <term>Mesit; one who misleads others to idolatry</term> must be uprooted and eradicated, for he stems from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One, Blessed be He, immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore we do not provide any relief to the forces of the "Sama-el" <note>an angelic name often associated with the accuser or serpent</note>. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, similar to what was said of the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman." A false prophet is also like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <term>Bikkurim</term>, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the First Fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness... therefore they must go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God and shall be eaten in Jerusalem. The secret of "minor" sacrifices and the "Second Tithe" <term>Ma'aser Sheni</term> is that they are eaten in Jerusalem. This is the "blessing of grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary sources of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat minor sacrifices until after the sprinkling of their blood. For the blood is the soul <note>Leviticus 17:11</note>, and only afterward is there permission to enjoy the physical benefit. Know that just as the Service—which is the sacrifice—is an offering to God, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the service is that a person offers himself, based on the secret of the verse: "When a man among you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2; implying 'from within yourselves'</note>. The burnt offering is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for spiritual thoughts... it is offered all night, and the serpent cannot hinder it. Minor sacrifices are for the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The Secret**
Of the firstborn: it is the secret that Israel is called "holy," as it is said, "Israel is My firstborn" <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. He has pity on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, [the firstborn animal] is eaten only by priests. The secret of eating sacrifices corresponds to... for Israel is holy, and Israel is called "Man" (*Adam*). He was originally a holy entity, but then a blemish fell upon him after he sinned, and he was clothed in "garments of skin" <note>Genesis 3:21</note>, but he has a redemption... "and I shall give a man in your place." This was the secret of the Scapegoat <term>Azazel</term>, "and it shall bear their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>... their iniquities fall upon its head and upon its people. But we are commanded not to cause a blemish in a sacrifice in order to eat it. For if one intentionally blemishes a sacrifice, [it is a grave sin]. There is also a prohibition against working or shearing consecrated animals, for even the "broken tablets" <note>of the Ten Commandments</note> remain holy.

### **The General Rule**
The upshot of the "Service" is the sacrifice, but the internal sacrifice is the person himself. Similarly, his soul is called [an offering] after his death on the Altar on High, and Michael [the Archangel] is the High Priest... for "in the image of God made He man." Therefore, the warning comes to be careful during one's life regarding damages to souls, not to kill a person except after thorough inquiry and investigation. Then, his death is "at the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the witness, He is the judge," for the Lord, Blessed be He, is a True Witness and a True Judge. So too must the Sanhedrin <term>the high court of Israel</term> be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that they must clarify the truth of the witnesses with absolute clarity—that is, through inquiry and investigation. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His pious ones]" <note>Psalm 116:15</note>.

### **And Since**
Death is precious in the eyes of the Lord—because Israel is holy from the perspective of their souls, for after death the souls cleave above—therefore the command comes: "You shall not gash yourselves, nor make any baldness [for the dead]... for you are children of the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. This is not the case for the [idolatrous] nations; gashing and baldness are their customs, which is appropriate for them since, upon their death, they go to perdition and have no portion in this world or the World to Come. We, however, are children of God. When one is absent from this world—which is a temporary dwelling—on the contrary, we have a permanent dwelling above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or to perform these [mutilating] acts.

### **Let us return**
To the matter: the person who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it says, "When a man among you brings an offering." There is another secret in this: for... even below the level of Man, namely in the secret of reincarnation <term>Gilgul</term>, "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even when eating non-sacred meat <term>Chullin; meat for pleasure</term>, we are commanded regarding ritual slaughter <term>Shechitah</term> with great care to avoid any "nick" in the blade. For then it becomes a carcass <term>Neveilah</term>, and "an atrocity is committed in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation is within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself"—choose for him a "beautiful death," namely, slaughter without a flaw. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity spreads and takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and if there is a spark of holiness in that animal or pure bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **And one who eats**
A "limb from a living animal" <term>Ever Min HaChai</term> is like eating the flesh of... when there is a reincarnation of a soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the meat" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Similarly, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all point to the "spark" spread within them—whether it is from the side of impurity or the side of holiness. I have elaborated on this in the portion of Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. For they themselves are the Tabernacle; for a man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Holy, and from the belly downward corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in the portion of Terumah. When one eats foods that are from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Now, a man's table atones for him," as I have explained in its place.

### **And the matter**
Of the commandments of the Festivals and their sacrifices, I have written about each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to go up for the pilgrimage: "Three times a year shall all your males appear." Just as one comes to "see," so too he comes to "be seen." Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Sanctuary where the Glory dwells, he must "turn away from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Otherwise, it is forbidden for a wicked person to enter the hall—how could he wish to be seen before the Blessed One while bringing a "burnt offering of appearance"? Then, he himself becomes a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. And it said: "Three times a year he shall appear"—Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering"...

***

<summary>This page analyzes the commandments in Parashat Re'eh through the lens of the "three pillars" of the world, emphasizing that the human body and soul are a microcosm of the Holy Temple. It explains the mystical reasons for dietary laws, ritual slaughter, and the prohibition of mourning rituals like self-mutilation, viewing them as essential to maintaining the holiness of the "human sanctuary."</summary>
<keywords>Mitzvot, Re'eh, Holy Temple (Beit HaBechirah), Shekhinah, Sparks of Holiness, Reincarnation (Gilgul), Ritual Slaughter (Shechitah), Human Body as Sanctuary, Sanhedrin, Festivals (Mo'edim)</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta> as it is written: You shall not work the firstling of your ox <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 484. Not to shear the firstling, and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: You shall not shear the firstling of your sheep <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 485. Not to eat leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: You shall not eat leavened bread with it <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, meaning during the time of the Passover sacrifice, whose time is after midday. 486. Not to leave over the festive offering of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said: Neither shall any of the meat remain <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. 487. Not to offer the Passover sacrifice on a private altar, as it is said: You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>. 488. The commandment of rejoicing on the festivals, as it is said: And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. 489. The commandment of appearing <note>Pilgrimage</note>, that every male appear three times a year. 490. That we should not ascend to the Chosen House <note>The Temple</note> on a festival without a sacrifice, as it is said: And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### **Torah** Or <gloss>Torah Light</gloss>. These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service, and Deeds of Loving-kindness. Torah refers to the prohibitions "do not add" and "do not subtract," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers say: a thing that is complete in the ultimate perfection cannot be said to be lacking or redundant. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could accept an addition, it follows that it was not previously perfect. Therefore, the definition of "perfect" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is dependent upon His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term> <gloss>The Tetragrammaton</gloss>, as in the verse "The Torah of the Lord <note>Y-H-V-H</note> is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my work on Tractate Shevuot, chapter "Torah Or." And as stated in the Zohar regarding the verse "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Yod-He</term> with "My name" <note>Sh-M-Y</note> equals 365 <note>the number of negative commandments</note>. The letters <term>Vav-He</term> with "My memorial" <note>Z-Ch-R-Y</note> equals 248 <note>the number of positive commandments</note>. And it is written: "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>; He is the absolute Perfection, containing no subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which is a warning against erasing the Name or breaking a stone from the Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the house in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; so too the Sanctuary. And it is written: "I am the Lord, that is My name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like the enclosure of a house, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." Service <gloss>Avodah</gloss> refers to the majority of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came for there to be a fixed place, in the Chosen House, and the Torah gave a reason: "To His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" alludes to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term>. As it is written: "Do not fear, for she shall dwell within me," for in the Temple, the Glory <note>Kavod/Tiferet</note> unites with His people. This is "to put His name there," as the Aramaic translation <note>Targum</note> renders it: "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness, "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>, which are the <term>Kelipot</term> <gloss>husks/forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore: "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstlings and sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written of them: "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an elevation <note>aliyah</note> and not outside. Since the holiness is in the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, we were commanded to "turn from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this alludes to the ten nations whose power is not from idols. The matter is that the nations in the Land of Israel, being under the direct rule of the Honorable Name, worship God through "cutting the plantings" <note>heresy/separation of divine attributes</note>, which is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the rule of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking a single stone of holiness, conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a "Subverted City" <note>Ir HaNidachat</note> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. So too with the enticer <note>Mesit</note> and subverter, one must uproot and eradicate him, for he comes from the impurity of the ancient serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said "Cursed is the serpent" <note>Genesis 3:14</note>; therefore, the powers of <term>Samael</term> <note>the angel of evil</note> are never pardoned. The command came not to love him nor to listen to him, as is said of the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is also like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the first-fruits <term>Bikkurim</term>, that the priests have no permission to eat them until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first-fruits, which are the "beginning," indicate great holiness, as I have written elsewhere. Therefore, they must go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they shall eat in Jerusalem. The secret of "minor" sacrifices and the Second Tithe is that their consumption is in Jerusalem. This is the blessing of "grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary ancestors of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat minor sacrifices until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul <note>nefesh</note>, and afterward comes the permission to enjoy. Know that just as the service of sacrifice is an offering to God, so too is the worshiper; for the essence of the service is that a person offers himself, in the secret of "When a man <note>Adam</note> among you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for thoughts of the heart, which are spiritual; it is offered all night so that the serpent cannot hinder it. Minor sacrifices represent the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The secret** of the firstborn is the secret of Israel, who are called holy, as it is written: "My firstborn son, Israel" <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. He has compassion on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, the firstling is eaten only by the priests. The secret of eating sacrifices corresponds to those with blemishes. For Israel is holy and Israel is called "Man" <note>Adam</note>, which is a holy entity; afterward, a blemish fell upon him after he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption in the secret of "I give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>scapegoat</gloss>, "and he shall bear their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory explained: "their iniquities" <note>avonotam</note> refers to the "iniquities of the perfect ones" <note>avonot tam</note> which rest upon his head and his people. But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in a consecrated animal in order to eat them. For if one willfully casts a blemish in holy things, he also violates the prohibition of labor and shearing with holy things, for even the "broken tablets" <note>of the Ten Commandments</note> remain holy.

### **The general principle** of the matter: Divine Service is the sacrifice; however, the "inner sacrifice" is the person himself. Thus his soul is called to the Altar on High after his death, and Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret, for man was made in the image of God. Therefore, the warning was given to be careful during his life regarding damages to souls, not to kill a person except after thorough inquiry and investigation. Then he is "dead by the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the Witness, He is the Judge," for the Lord, blessed be He, is a True Witness and a True Judge. So too the Sanhedrin must be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean they must have clear verification of the truth of the witnesses through inquiry and investigation; then their judgment is as the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death" <note>of His pious ones</note>.

### **And since** death is precious in the eyes of the Lord—for Israel is holy from the side of their soul, so that after their death the souls attach themselves above—therefore the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness" etc., "for you are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1-2</note>. This is not the case with the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, for it is appropriate for them since upon their death they go to destruction and have no portion in this world or the world to come. We, however, are children of God; when we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we instead have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

### **We return** to the matter: the person who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it is written "When a man <note>Adam</note> among you brings an offering." There is a further secret in this. Even when a person descends below, in the secret of <term>Gilgul</term> <gloss>reincarnation</gloss>, "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding the eating of non-sacred meat <note>basar ta'avah</note>, we were commanded regarding ritual slaughter <term>Shechitah</term> with great care to have no nick in the blade. For if so, it becomes a "carcass" <term>nevelah</term>, and a "vile thing is done in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation might be within it? "Love your fellow as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>—choose for him a "beautiful death," meaning a slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity spreads and takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and the animal or pure bird contains a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **One who eats** a limb from a living animal is like one who eats the flesh of <unclear>...</unclear> when a soul is reincarnated there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. So too the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure cattle, beasts, and birds; all indicate the spark spread within them, whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" <term>Sitra Achra</term> or the "Side of Holiness." I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "And they shall make for Me a sanctuary and I will dwell within them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. For they themselves are the Tabernacle, as man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart to the Holy place; and from the belly downward to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Now a man's table atones for him," as I have elaborated in its place.

### **Regarding** the matter of the Festival commandments and their sacrifices, I have written about each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals, to ascend for the pilgrimage, and "three times a year shall all your males appear." One should not say that just as he comes to see, so he comes to be seen; therefore, if he wishes to be seen in the Temple where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. For without this, it is forbidden to see the face of a wicked person; how then would he wish to appear before Him, may He be blessed, bringing a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself becomes a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. And it says "three times a year he shall appear"—this refers to Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering."

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual and symbolic meanings of the commandments in Parashat Re'eh, focusing on the three pillars of the world: Torah, Service, and Kindness. It explains that the Temple service and dietary laws are intended to elevate sparks of holiness and that a person's physical body and table serve as a contemporary sanctuary.</summary>
<keywords>Firstlings, Temple, Shekhinah, Ir HaNidachat, Mesit, Gilgul, Shechitah, Soul, Atonement, Sanhedrin, Mourning, Isaac</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta> as it is written: "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 

484. Not to shear the firstborn <note>Hebrew: <term>bechor</term></note>, and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: "You shall not shear the firstborn of your sheep" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>.
485. Not to eat leaven <note>Hebrew: <term>chametz</term></note> on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: "You shall not eat leavened bread with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, meaning during the time of the Passover sacrifice, which begins after midday.
486. Not to leave over the meat of the fourteenth day's festival offering until the third day, as it is said: "Neither shall any of the flesh... remain" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>.
487. Not to offer the Passover sacrifice on a private altar <note>Hebrew: <term>bamah</term></note>, as it is said: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>.
488. The commandment to rejoice on the festivals, as it is said: "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>.
489. The commandment of appearing <note>Hebrew: <term>re'iyah</term></note>, that every male appear three times a year.
490. Not to ascend to the Chosen House <note>Hebrew: <term>Beit HaBechirah</term>, referring to the Temple in Jerusalem</note> on a festival without an offering, as it is said: "And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### **Torah** is Light. These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service, and Deeds of Loving-kindness. 

**Torah** consists of the prohibitions "Do not add" and "Do not subtract," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. It is as the philosophers say: a thing that is perfectly complete cannot be described as lacking or redundant. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could accept an addition, it would mean it was not yet perfected. Therefore, the definition of the "complete" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is suspended upon His Great Name, which is <term>Y-H-V-H</term> <gloss>The Tetragrammaton</gloss>, for "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my commentary on Tractate Shevuot, in the chapter "Torah Ohr." And as it says in the Zohar regarding the verse "This is My Name and this is My Memorial": The letters <term>Y-H</term> <note>numerical value 15</note> with "My Name" <note>Hebrew: <term>Shemi</term>, value 350</note> equals 365 <note>the number of negative commandments</note>. The letters <term>V-H</term> <note>value 11</note> with "My Memorial" <note>Hebrew: <term>Zichri</term>, value 237</note> equals 248 <note>the number of positive commandments</note>. It is written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>; He is the absolute perfection in whom there is no subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, a warning not to erase the Name or to shatter a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the house in which the Blessed One dwells, as is the Sanctuary. It is written, "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like the enclosure of the house, and His Name is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God."

**Service** <note>Hebrew: <term>Avodah</term></note> refers to the majority of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place in the Chosen House, and the Torah gave the reason: "To His habitation you shall seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" <note>Hebrew: <term>leshichno</term></note> alludes to the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: <term>Shekhinah</term></note>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Y-V-D V-V</term> <note>A mystical spelling of the Divine Name</note>. As it is said, "Fear not, for she shall dwell with me," for in the Sanctuary, the Glory <note>Hebrew: <term>Kavod</term></note> is unified with the Beauty <note>Hebrew: <term>Tiferet</term></note> of His people. This is the meaning of "to place His Name there," which the Aramaic translation <term>Targum</term> renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>, referring to the external shells <note>Hebrew: <term>Kelipot</term>, forces of impurity</note>. Therefore, "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them within. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House; then the branch returns to its root. It is written of them, "There you shall ascend," meaning there they shall have an elevation and not outside. Since the holiness resides in the Chosen House in the Holy Land, we were commanded to "turn away from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this alludes to the ten nations whose power is not from the worship of idols. The matter is that nations in the Land of Israel, under the governance of the Honorable Name, who worship God through "cutting the shoots" <note>an idiomatic term for heresy or improper mystical practice</note>, this is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the governance of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against shattering a single stone of holiness, so conversely it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a "diverted city" <note>Hebrew: <term>Ir HaNidachat</term></note> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Similarly, one who entices and misleads <note>Hebrew: <term>Mesit u-Madiach</term></note> must be uprooted and eradicated, for he stems from the impurity of the ancient Serpent who was the first enticer. The Holy One immediately said, "Cursed is the Serpent," therefore the powers of <term>Samael</term> <gloss>the angel of evil</gloss> are never healed. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, as it was said to the Serpent, "I will put enmity between you and the woman." A false prophet is also like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the first fruits <note>Hebrew: <term>Bikkurim</term></note>, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness. Therefore, they go to the holy place and from there take their wisdom, for they are holy to God and shall eat in Jerusalem. The secret of "minor" sacrifices <note>Hebrew: <term>kodashim kalim</term></note> and the Second Tithe is that they are eaten in Jerusalem; this is the meaning of the blessing on grain, wine, and oil, which are the "fathers of fathers" of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat minor sacrifices until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul, and afterward comes the permission to enjoy. Know that just as the service of the sacrifice is an offering to God, so too is the worshipper; for the essence of the service is that one sacrifices himself, according to the secret of "When a man <note>Hebrew: <term>Adam</term></note> brings an offering from among you" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering <note>Hebrew: <term>Olah</term></note> is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for the thoughts of the heart which are spiritual; it is offered all night so the Serpent cannot hinder it. Minor sacrifices represent the peace of the soul and body.

### **The secret** of the firstborn <term>bechor</term> is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "Israel My firstborn." He has pity on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, it is eaten only by priests. The secret of eating sacrifices corresponds to those with blemishes. For Israel is holy and called "Man" <term>Adam</term>, which is a holy form; afterward, a blemish fell upon him after he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption through the secret of "I will give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>the scapegoat of Yom Kippur</gloss> which "carries their iniquities." Their iniquities rest upon the head of the goat and his people. But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in a sacrifice in order to eat it, for if one intentionally blemishes a sacrifice, he is also prohibited from working or shearing the holy animals, for even the broken Tablets of the Covenant are holy.

### **The general principle** of the service is the sacrifice, but the internal sacrifice is Man. Likewise, his soul is called to the Altar on High after his death, where Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret: for in the image of God was man made. Therefore, the warning was given to be careful with human life and not to kill a person except after thorough searching and inquiry. Then he is executed by the hand of Heaven, in the secret of "He is the witness, He is the judge," for the Lord is the True Witness and True Judge. So must the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <gloss>the high court</gloss> be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean they must clarify the truth of the testimony with complete clarity through searching and inquiry; then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones."

### **Since** the death of the pious is precious to the Lord—for Israel is holy from the perspective of their souls, which after death cleave to the heights—therefore the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness..." <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> because "you are children to the Lord your God." This is not the case for the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, for it is appropriate for them since upon death they go to destruction and have no portion in this world or the World to Come. We, however, are children of God. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we actually go to a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter that the person who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it says: "When a man brings an offering from among you." There is another secret here: even when a person descends through the secret of reincarnation <term>gilgul</term>—"Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even when eating mundane meat for pleasure, we were commanded regarding slaughter <term>shechitah</term> with great care to avoid any nick in the blade; for then it becomes a carcass <term>neveilah</term>, and a "disgrace <note>a pun on <term>neveilah</term></note> is done in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation is within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself"—choose for him a beautiful death, namely a slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and if there is a spark of holiness in the animal or pure bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **One who eats** a limb from a living animal is like one who eats the flesh of himself when there is a reincarnated soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh." Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the spark spread within them—whether it is from the side of impurity or the side of holiness. I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "Make for Me a sanctuary and I will dwell within them," for they themselves are the Tabernacle. For Man consists of three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart to the Holy place; and from the belly downward to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now a man's table atones for him," as I have explained in its proper place.

### **Regarding** the matter of the festivals and their sacrifices, I have written about each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to make the pilgrimage: "Three times a year shall all your males appear." One should not say: "Just as I come to see, I come to be seen." Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Holy Temple where the Glory dwells, he must turn from evil and do good, being a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden for a wicked person to enter the Hall—how could he wish to appear before the Blessed One and bring a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself becomes the sacrifice through the offering he brings. It says "three times a year he shall appear"—alluding to Isaac who was a "perfect burnt offering" <note>the text breaks off here</note>.

<summary>This page analyzes the laws of Parashat Re'eh, focusing on the sanctity of the Temple, the prohibition of idolatry, and the mystical significance of sacrifices and dietary laws. Horowitz explains that Man is a microcosm of the Temple and that the act of eating and animal slaughter involves the elevation of holy sparks and reincarnated souls.</summary>
<keywords>Bechor, Temple, Shekhinah, Idolatry, Gilgul, Shechitah, Sanhedrin, Festivals, Bikkurim, Neveilah, Purity, Sacrifices</keywords>
