These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service <term>Avodah</term>, and Deeds of Loving-kindness <term>Gemilut Hasadim</term>. 

Torah consists of the commands "Do not add" and "Do not subtract," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is perfect in the ultimate sense cannot be said to be lacking nor can it be increased. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could receive addition, it would mean it was not previously perfect. Therefore, the definition of "perfect" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is dependent upon His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>, for "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my work on Tractate Shevuot in the chapter "Torah Or." As stated in the Zohar on the verse "This is My Name and this is My Memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Yod-Heh</term> with "My Name" <note>Hebrew: Shemi</note> equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>Vav-Heh</term> with "My Memorial" <note>Hebrew: Zichri</note> equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. It is also written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>, and He is the absolute Perfection in whom there is no subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning, "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which is a warning against erasing the Name or breaking a stone from the Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the House in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; so too is the Sanctuary. It is written, "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like a frame for the House, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul within them. One who destroys His House, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." 

Divine Service <term>Avodah</term> comprises most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place, in the Chosen House, and the reason was given: "to His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" <term>leshichno</term> hints at the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh</term>. Do not fear that she will dwell elsewhere, for in the Sanctuary, the Glory <note>Tiferet</note> is united with the Divine Presence among His people. This is the meaning of "to place His Name there," which the Targum renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Surrounding the place of holiness, the wicked walk—these are the "Husks" <term>Kelipot</term> <note>Forces of impurity</note>. Therefore, "Guard yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** 
Sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written of them, "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an ascent <term>aliyah</term> and not outside. Since the holiness resides in the Chosen House which is in the Holy Land, we were commanded to "turn from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations served their gods. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this relates to the ten nations who, though they are not idolaters <unclear>in essence</unclear>, when nations in the Land of Israel—which is under the direct providence of the Honorable Name—serve God through "cutting the plantings" <note>A term for heresy or spiritual sabotage</note>, this is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the rule of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking even one stone of holiness, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a Subverted City <term>Ir HaNidachat</term> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Similarly, the enticer <term>mesit</term> and the subverter <term>madiach</term> must be uprooted and eradicated, for he comes from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was the first enticer. The Holy One immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of <term>Samael</term> <note>The personification of evil/Satan</note> are never cured. The command came not to love him nor listen to him, as was said regarding the serpent, "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is also like an enticer. 

Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <term>Bikkurim</term>, which the priests are not permitted to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness as I have written elsewhere; therefore they must go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they eat in Jerusalem. This is the secret of the "lighter" holy offerings <term>Kodashim Kalim</term> and the Second Tithe, whose consumption is in Jerusalem. This is the "blessing of grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary sources of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat the lighter holy offerings until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul, and afterward comes the permission to enjoy and derive benefit. Know that just as the service—the sacrifice—is an offering to God, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the service is that a person offers himself, in the secret of the verse, "When a man of you <note>literally 'from you'</note> brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering <term>olah</term> is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for the thoughts of the heart <term>hirhur ha-lev</term> which are spiritual; it is burned all night so the serpent does not hinder it. The lighter holy offerings represent the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The Secret** 
Of the firstborn is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "the firstborn of Israel." He has compassion on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, the firstborn animal is eaten only by the priests. The secret of eating sacrifices that have blemishes <term>mumim</term> <note>rendered profane</note> is that Israel is holy and called "Man" <term>Adam</term>. He was a holy creature, but afterward a blemish fell upon him when he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption through the secret of "I will give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the Scapegoat <term>Azazel</term> that "bore their iniquities," meaning the iniquities that rested upon his head and his people. However, we were commanded not to intentionally cause a blemish in a sacrifice in order to eat it. For if one casts a blemish in the holy offerings by his own choice, it is a grave sin. Likewise, there is a prohibition against working or shearing the holy animals, for even the broken Tablets of the Covenant remain holy.

The general principle is: the Service is the sacrifice; however, the inner sacrifice is the Man himself. Likewise, his soul is called to the Altar on High after death, and Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret that man was made in the image of God. Therefore, the warning was given to be careful during one's life regarding "damages to souls," not to kill a man except after great inquiry and investigation. Only then is it "death by the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the Witness, He is the Judge," for the Lord, may He be blessed, is the True Witness and the True Judge. So too must the Sanhedrin be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that they must clarify the truth of the testimony with complete clarity, through inquiry and investigation. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and the death of his <unclear>saints</unclear> is precious in the eyes of the Lord.

### **Since** 
The death of his [pious ones] is precious in the eyes of the Lord, because Israel is holy from the side of their soul—for after their death, the souls cling to the heights—therefore the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness [between your eyes for the dead]" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>, for "you are children to the Lord your God." This is not the case for the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, and rightly so, since upon their death they go to perdition and have no portion in this world or the world to come. We, however, are children of God. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we instead have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

Let us return to the matter: the man who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it says, "When a man of you brings an offering." There is a further secret here: that sometimes a soul is "reincarnated" <term>gilgul</term> even below the level of man, in the secret of "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding the eating of non-sacred meat <term>basar ta'ava</term>, we were commanded in the laws of slaughter <term>shechitah</term> with great care to avoid any "nick" in the blade. For if there is a nick, the animal becomes a carcass <term>nevilah</term>, and "a disgrace is done in Israel," for who knows what soul might be reincarnated within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" implies choosing a "beautiful death" for it—that is, slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and if there is a spark of holiness in the animal or pure bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **Eating** 
A limb from a living animal <term>ever min ha-chai</term> is like eating the flesh of a person when there is a reincarnated soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Similarly, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the spark spread within them—whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" <term>Sitra Achra</term> or the "Side of Holiness." I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them, "And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell within them," for they themselves are the Tabernacle. For man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart corresponds to the Holy Place; and from the belly downward corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods that are from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now, a man's table atones for him," as I have explained in its place.

### **The Matter** 
Of the commandments of the Festivals and their sacrifices, I have written each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to ascend for the pilgrimage: "Three times a year shall all your males appear." One should not say that just as he comes to see, he comes to be seen; therefore, if he wishes to be seen in the Sanctuary where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden to behold the face of the wicked; how then could he wish to appear before the Blessed One and bring a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself is a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. It says "Three times a year he shall appear"—this refers to Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering."

<summary>This page analyzes the laws of firstborn animals, sacrifices, and festivals in Parashat Re'eh through a mystical lens. It explains that man himself is the "inner sacrifice" and that the laws of kosher slaughter and mourning reflect the eternal nature of the Jewish soul and its potential for reincarnation.</summary>
<keywords>Bechor, Shekhinah, Temple, Reincarnation, Gilgul, Shechitah, Festivals, Sacrifice, Soul, Purity</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page: the primary offspring of the righteous are their good deeds. The reason they merit actual offspring is</meta> as it is said: "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 

484. Not to shear the firstborn <note>animal</note>; and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: "You shall not shear the firstborn [of your flock]" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>.
485. Not to eat leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: "You shall not eat leavened bread with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, meaning during the time of the slaughtering of the Passover sacrifice, which is after midday.
486. Not to leave over [any meat] from the festival offering of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said: "Neither shall any of the meat... remain [overnight]" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>.
487. Not to offer the Passover sacrifice on a private altar, as it is said: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>.
488. The commandment to rejoice on the festivals, as it is said: "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>.
489. The commandment for every male to appear <note>in the Temple</note> three times a year.
490. That we should not go up to the Chosen House <gloss>the Temple</gloss> on a festival without a sacrifice, as it is said: "And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### **Torah Light** 
These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Service <term>Avodah</term>, and Deeds of Kindness <term>Gemilut Hasadim</term>.

**Torah** is the command "You shall not add and you shall not subtract," which indicates the perfection of the Torah. It is as the philosophers have said: regarding a thing that is absolutely perfect, it is impossible to say it is lacking or redundant. For if it were lacking, it would not be perfect; and if it could receive an addition, it would mean it was not previously complete. Therefore, the definition of the "perfect" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is dependent on His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term> <gloss>the Tetragrammaton</gloss>, as it is said: "The Torah of the Lord <note>original: "Torat Y-H-V-H"</note> is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my commentary on Tractate Shevuot in the chapter "Torah Light." 

And as it is written in the Zohar on the verse, "This is My Name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Yod-He</term> <gloss>the first two letters of the Name</gloss> with "My Name" <note>original: "Shemi"</note> equals 365 <note>the number of prohibitive commandments</note>. The letters <term>Vav-He</term> <gloss>the last two letters</gloss> with "My memorial" <note>original: "Zikhri"</note> equals 248 <note>the number of positive commandments</note>. And it is written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>; He is the absolute perfect one, having no deficiency and no addition. 

Concerning this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>—a warning not to erase the Name or to shatter a stone from the Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are in the "House" in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; and so too is the Temple. It is written: "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>. The letters are like a frame for the House, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul for them. One who destroys His House, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God."

**Service** <term>Avodah</term> consists of most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came for there to be a fixed place, which is the Chosen House <gloss>the Temple</gloss>. He gave a reason for the matter: "To His dwelling you shall seek and you shall come there" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His dwelling" alludes to the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term>. As it is written: "Do not fear, for she dwells with me," for in the Temple, the "Glory" <note>the Sefirah of Tiferet</note> is united with His people. This is "to put His name there" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>, which the Targum <gloss>Aramaic translation</gloss> renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness, the wicked walk, for they are the "shells" <term>Kelipot</term> <gloss>forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore: "Take care that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **And sometimes**
Sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written regarding them: "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have their elevation <note>original: "Aliyah"</note> and not outside. 

Since the Chosen House is in the Holy Land, that is where the holiness resides. Therefore, we were commanded to "turn away from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations served <note>their gods</note>. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret alludes to the fact that the ten nations <note>the Canaanite tribes</note> were not merely idolaters; rather, the nations in the Land of Israel, being under the direct dominion of the Honorable Name, serve God through "cutting the plantings" <gloss>heretical separation of divine attributes</gloss>, which is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the dominion of external forces. 

Just as there is a great prohibition against shattering a single stone of the sanctuary, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a "Subverted City" <term>Ir HaNidachat</term> and never to rebuild it, for its location is impure. Similarly, one must uproot the "Enticer" <term>Mesit</term> and the "Subverter" <term>Madiach</term>, for he originates from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said: "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of the Left <gloss>the side of impurity</gloss> are not spared. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, similar to what was said to the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is also like an enticer.

Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <term>Bikkurim</term>, which the Priests have no permission to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the First Fruits, which are the "beginning," indicate a great holiness, as I have written elsewhere. Therefore, they must go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they shall eat in Jerusalem. 

This is also the secret of "lesser holy" sacrifices <term>Kodashim Kalim</term> and the Second Tithe <term>Ma'aser Sheni</term>—their consumption is in Jerusalem. This is the blessing of "grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary ancestors of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat "lesser holy" sacrifices until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul <note>original: "Nefesh"</note>; afterward, there is permission to enjoy them. 

Know that just as the Service <note>sacrifice</note> is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the Service is that a person offers himself, in the secret of the verse: "When a man <term>Adam</term> offers [a sacrifice] from you" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering <term>Olah</term> is entirely consumed, for it comes to rectify the straying of thought, which is spiritual. It is offered all night; the serpent cannot hinder it. The "lesser holy" sacrifices represent the peace of the soul and the body.

### **And the secret** 
Of the firstborn is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "My firstborn, Israel" <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. He has compassion on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, it <note>the firstborn animal</note> is eaten only by the Priests. 

The secret of eating holy things corresponds to those with blemishes. For Israel is holy, and Israel is called "Man" <term>Adam</term>, which is "Holy Knowledge" <term>Da'at Kodesh</term>. Afterward, a blemish fell upon him after he sinned, and he was clothed in "garments of skin" <note>Genesis 3:21</note>, but he has a redemption, in the secret of: "And I gave man <term>Adam</term> in your stead" <note>Isaiah 43:4</note>. This was the secret of the Scapegoat <term>Azazel</term>, which "carries their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>. The Sages, of blessed memory, explained that "their iniquities" <term>avonotam</term> <gloss>can be read as "the iniquities of the perfect ones"</gloss> fall upon the head of the goat and his people. But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in a consecrated animal in order to eat it. For if one intentionally causes a blemish in holy things by his own choice, he harms the sanctity. There is also a prohibition against working or shearing consecrated animals, for even the "broken tablets" <gloss>the first set of the Ten Commandments</gloss> remain holy.

### **The general principle**
Arising from this is that the Service is the sacrifice; however, the "inner sacrifice" is the person himself. Similarly, his soul is called after his death to the "Altar on High," and Michael is the High Priest. The secret is that man was made in the image of God. Therefore, the warning was given to be careful during his life regarding the injury of souls, not to kill a person except after thorough inquiry and investigation. Then, his death is "by the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the witness, He is the judge," for the Lord, may He be blessed, is a True Witness and a True Judge. So too must the Sanhedrin be: just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that they must clarify the truth of the witnesses with complete clarity—namely, inquiry and investigation—and then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven. "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His pious ones]" <note>Psalm 116:15</note>.

### **And since**
Death is precious in the eyes of the Lord—because Israel is holy by virtue of their souls, and after death their souls cleave above—the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness [between your eyes for the dead], for you are children of the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1-2</note>. This is not the case for the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs. This is appropriate for them, since upon their death they go to destruction and have no portion in this world or the world to come. We, however, are children of the Lord. When one is absent from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, he instead has a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to engage in excessive mourning or to perform these <note>mutilating</note> acts.

### **Let us return**
To the matter: the person who serves is himself the sacrifice, as it is said: "When a man offers [a sacrifice] from you." There is a further secret in this. Since man can descend even to the level of an animal—namely in the secret of reincarnation <term>Gilgul</term>, "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>—therefore, even when eating "secular meat" <term>basar ta'ava</term>, we were commanded regarding ritual slaughter <term>Shechita</term> with great care, without any nick <note>in the blade</note>. For if there is a nick, it becomes "carrion" <term>nevelah</term>, and "a disgrace is committed in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation is within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>—choose for him a beautiful death <note>a Talmudic principle applied here to the spark within the animal</note>, namely slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, or if the power of impurity spreads and takes hold of it, it is forbidden. But when it is slaughtered properly, and the animal is of the sacrificial types or a pure bird containing a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **And one who eats** 
A "limb from a living animal" is like eating from his own flesh when a reincarnated soul is present there. This is the secret of "Do not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Similarly, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the "spark" that spreads within them—whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" <term>Sitra De-Mas'ava</term> or from the "Side of Holiness" <term>Sitra De-Kedusha</term>. I elaborated on this in the portion of *Shemini*. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "And they shall make for Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. For they themselves are the Tabernacle. A person is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart corresponds to the Holy Place; and from the belly onward corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in the portion of *Terumah*. When one eats foods from the side of holiness, they are like the sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Now, a person's table atones for him," as I have elaborated in the appropriate place.

### **And regarding**
The matter of the commandments of the festivals and their sacrifices, I have written about each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to go up for the pilgrimage: "Three times a year shall all your males appear" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>. Our Sages said: just as one comes "to see," so he comes "to be seen." Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Temple where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. For if not, it is forbidden for a wicked person to enter the Hall <note>of the Temple</note>; how then could he wish to be seen before Him, may He be blessed, and bring a "burnt offering of appearance"? Then he himself becomes a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. It says "three times a year he shall appear"—Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering"...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical and legal dimensions of Parashat Re'eh, explaining that the Temple service, dietary laws, and mourning rituals all reflect the sanctity of the human soul and the process of elevating holy sparks.</summary>
<keywords>Parashat Re'eh, Temple Service, Shechita, Gilgul, Reincarnation, Sanhedrin, Firstborn, Dietary Laws, Holy Sparks, Shekhinah</keywords>

### **Torah Or** These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Service, and Acts of Loving-kindness. Torah is the prohibition of "do not add and do not diminish," which points to the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is perfect in ultimate perfection cannot be called lacking or excessive. For if it were lacking, it would not be perfect; and if it could receive an addition, it would not be perfect. Therefore, the definition of a "perfect" thing is that it has neither lack nor excess. It is known that the Torah depends on His Great Name, which is the <term>Yod</term>, <term>Heh</term>, <term>Vav</term>, <term>Heh</term> <gloss>the Tetragrammaton</gloss>, as in the verse "the Torah of the Lord <note>original: "Torat HaShem"</note> is perfect," as I have elaborated on this in my tractate <term>Shavuot</term>, in the chapter "Torah Or." This is also as written in the <term>Zohar</term> on the verse "This is My Name and this is My remembrance." The <term>Yod</term> and <term>Heh</term> with "My Name" equals 365, and the <term>Vav</term> and <term>Heh</term> with "My remembrance" equals 248. It is written "I am the first and I am the last," and He is the absolute perfection; there is no diminution or addition in Him. Regarding this, the warning was given: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." This is a warning against erasing the Name or tearing a stone from the Holy Temple. For the letters of the Name are in the house where He, blessed be He, dwells, and likewise the Temple. It is written "I am the Lord, My Name is..." The letters are like a closure for the house, and His Name, blessed be He, is the soul for them. He who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." Service refers to most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place, and one comes to the Chosen House, and the verse provides a reason: "Seek His dwelling and come there." "His dwelling" hints at the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the letters <term>Yod</term> and <term>Vav</term>, as it is written "And He brought down into the <unclear>hidden</unclear> <note>possibly: "Holy of Holies"</note> His holiness..." and as it is written "Do not fear, for it is My dwelling." For in the Temple, the Glory is unified in the splendor of His people, and this is "to His name, His name there," which is translated "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness, the wicked walk, for they are the <term>kelippah</term> <gloss>husk/shell of impurity</gloss>; therefore, "Take heed to yourself that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see."

### **And sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inside. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn offerings from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written regarding them "You shall offer them there," meaning there they shall have an elevation, and not outside. Since the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, is where holiness is, we were commanded to "turn from evil" and destroy all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate after them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. Its secret hints at the ten nations whose power is not from idol worship. The matter is that the nations in the Land of Israel, under the rule of the honored Name, serve God by cutting the shoots; this is true idol worship. However, those outside the Land are under the rule of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition to tear one stone from the holiness, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and annihilate an "apostate city" and never to rebuild it, for its place is unclean. Similarly, one who incites or leads others astray must be uprooted and eradicated, for he is from the impurity of the primordial serpent that incited. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the forces of the inciter are not revived. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, in the matter spoken to the serpent "I will put enmity between you and the woman." Also, a false prophet is like an inciter. Let us return to the matter that the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the first fruits, that the priests have no permission to eat them until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness, as I have written elsewhere; therefore, they shall go to the holy place and from there they will take their wisdom, for they are holy to God and shall eat in Jerusalem. The secret of the "lesser holy things" and the "second tithe" is that they are eaten in Jerusalem, and this is the "grain, wine, and oil," which are the progenitors of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat the lesser holy things until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the life, and afterwards is the permission to indulge and enjoy. Know that just as the service, which is the offering, is an offering to the Lord, so is the servant. For the essence of service is that a person offers himself, in the secret of "When a man offers from among you." The burnt offering is entirely consumed, for it comes to address the stirring of the thought, which is spiritual. And the serpent does not hinder it. And the lesser holy things are for the perfection of the soul and the body.

### **The secret** of the firstborn is the secret of Israel, who are called holy, as it is written "Israel is My firstborn." He has compassion on them, and you shall keep them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, it is only eaten by the priests. The secret of eating the holy things is in relation to them having blemishes and defects. For Israel is holy, and Israel is called "Man." And this is the secret of holiness, but afterwards a blemish fell upon him when he sinned and was clothed in garments of skin, but he has a redemption in the secret of "And I will give a man in your stead." This was the secret of <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>the scapegoat</gloss>, to carry their sins, meaning that their sins fall upon his head and his people. But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in the holy things in order to eat them, for he who causes a blemish in the holy things is acting on his own choice. Also, there is the prohibition of labor and shearing on holy things, for even the broken tablets are holy.

### **In conclusion**, the service is the offering, although the internal offering is the person. And his soul is called after his death at the altar above, and <term>Michael</term> <gloss>the archangel</gloss> is the High Priest. The point is the secret that "in the image of God the human was made." Therefore, the warning comes to be careful in his life regarding damage to human life, not to kill a person except after rigorous inquiry and examination. And then it is cleared by the hands of Heaven, in the secret of "He is the witness and He is the judge," for the Lord, blessed be He, is a true witness and a true judge. Likewise, the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <gloss>rabbinical supreme court</gloss> must be: just as they are true judges, they must be true witnesses. I mean that they must have the assurance of the truth of the witnesses in complete clarity, which is the inquiry and examination. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His saints]."

### **And since** it is precious in the eyes of the Lord, for Israel are holy by virtue of their souls, because after their death the souls cleave above, therefore the command came "Do not cut yourselves and do not make a bald spot, etc.," for you are children to the Lord your God. This is not the case for the nations; the cutting and the bald spot are their customs, for it is appropriate, since in their death they go to oblivion and have no portion in this world or the next world. Not so with us, the children of the living God. And when we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, on the contrary, we have a permanent seat above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to increase in mourning and to perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter that the person who serves is himself the offering, as it is written "When a man offers from among you." Furthermore, there is a secret in this, for there is a link even below for the person, in the secret of the reincarnation "Man and beast You save, O Lord." Therefore, even in eating mundane meat of desire, we were commanded in the slaughter and in great care without any defect, for then it is an <term>nevelah</term> <gloss>carcass of an animal that died naturally</gloss>, and then it becomes an unclean thing in Israel. For who knows what reincarnation is in it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" is to choose for him a good death, meaning slaughter without a defect. If the animal died by itself, or if the power of impurity spread and seized it, but when he slaughters it properly, and there is in the animal's sacrifice, like a pure bird, a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **And he who eats** a limb from a living animal is like one who eats from the flesh of <unclear>the living</unclear> when there is a reincarnation of a soul there. This is the secret of "Do not eat the soul with the flesh." Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure cattle, wild animals, and birds all point to the spark spreading within them, whether it is from the side of impurity or from the side of holiness. I have elaborated on this in <term>Parashat Shemini</term>. When Israel behaves in holiness, it is written of them "And they shall make Me a sanctuary and I will dwell among them," for they themselves are the tabernacle. For the human is like three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Holy Place, and from the belly onwards corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I have elaborated in <term>Parashat Terumah</term>. And when he eats foods that are from the side of holiness, then they are like an offering sacrificed upon the altar. Regarding this, the Sages said: "Now the table of a person makes atonement," as I have elaborated in its place.

### **And regarding** the matter of the festivals and their offerings, I have written about each in its own special place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to ascend for the pilgrimage, and "three times a year every male shall appear." It is not for nothing; as he comes to see, so he comes to be seen. Therefore, if he wishes to appear in the Holy Temple, where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. If not, it is forbidden to stand in the court of the wicked, and how can he wish to see before Him, blessed be He? He brings a burnt offering of appearance, and then he himself is an offering through the offering that he brings. And it is said "three times a year he shall appear," <term>Isaac</term> <gloss>the patriarch</gloss> who was a perfect burnt offering...

He made that salt the cause of his life, for it had stopped the flow of blood from him. When he felt that his body was capable of movement, he stood up and walked a little with trepidation while filled with fear. He went out into the darkness <note>possibly an outer courtyard or alleyway</note> until he gathered his strength in the vestibule until morning. When the day dawned, that cursed one-eyed woman <note>the old woman who acted as a decoy for the wicked household</note> went out seeking another victim <note>original: "prey like him"</note>. My brother followed her without her knowledge. He spent a month treating his wounds until he recovered, all while watching for her to go out. He saw her take people one after another and lead them to that house. My brother said nothing. When his spirit and strength returned to him, he went to his chest and made a bag from it, which he filled with broken glass <note>intended to mimic the sound and weight of coins to trick the woman</note>.

And morning overtook...

text:
<meta>This page continues the exploration of divine Names, moving from the Name of Hosts (Tzva’ot) to the combined Name "YHVH Elohim." It focuses on how the divine attributes of Judgment and Mercy balance one another through the Sefirah of "Justice" (Mishpat), associated with the patriarch Jacob.</meta>

# What is Gate 5
### M
<warning>Horizontal strip of semi-transparent tape across the middle of the page, partially obscuring lines 17-20.</warning>

A section in which the Name **YHVH Elohim** <note>original: "יה'וה אלהים"; this combination represents the unification of the attributes of Mercy (YHVH) and Judgment (Elohim)</note> is mentioned refers to actions performed through all the attributes that are completed by both the **Attribute of Judgment** <term>Hebrew: *Middat HaDin*; the divine quality of strict law and justice</term> and the **Attribute of Mercy** <term>Hebrew: *Middat HaRachamim*; the divine quality of compassion and grace</term>. You find this, for example, in the creation of the first man (Adam), in his judgment, and in his exile. In all those matters, you will find that they occurred through both Judgment and Mercy, all in perfect completion, with Mercy and Judgment applied exactly as is fitting in a **True Judgment** <note>original: "דין אמת"</note>. 

According to this principle, the Torah states: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: **The Rock** <note>original: "הצור"; a title for God as a firm foundation</note> who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty. He does not decree judgment until **His work is perfect**, meaning the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes: **Kindness** <term>Hebrew: *Chesed*</term> and **Judgment**. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <note>Hebrew: *Tamim*</note>. For the word *Tamim* <note>meaning perfect or complete</note> contains the secret of two things. It is as if one said **twins** <note>original: "תאומים"; *Te’omim*</note>, but the Torah uses the dignified term "perfect" (*Tamim*) when referring to the two celestial things above, and the term "twins" (*Te’omim*) for things below. 

Thus it says: "And they shall be doubled [twins] below... they shall be complete [perfect] at the top" <note>Exodus 26:24; referring to the construction of the Tabernacle</note>. Below they are called "twins," and above they are called "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things—opposites, like an advocate and an accuser—but above, everything is a single intention. Between the advocate and the accuser, both have one purpose; there is no hatred or love there, nor is there any favoritism, but only a **Judgment of Truth**. Therefore it says, "His work is perfect," meaning He deliberated with both Judgment and Mercy and then decreed the law. This is the secret of "True Judgment."

And regarding what is said, "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, the explanation is that everything is visible to every seeing eye, as it says, "For all His ways are justice." You already know that **Justice** <term>Hebrew: *Mishpat*; representing the middle path or balance</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. For Justice corresponds to the patriarch **Jacob**, who is the "middle line" that balances between the "two tents" of **Abraham** and **Isaac**. 
*   **Abraham** corresponds to **Kindness** (*Chesed*).
*   **Isaac** corresponds to **Judgment** (*Din*).
*   **Jacob** mediates between them, as he is called "a perfect [simple] man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. 

Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Kindness on Abraham’s side and from Judgment on Isaac’s side. Thus it says: "**Justice** and **Righteousness** in Jacob You have made" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. And the prophet said: "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice" uses the word "but" <note>original: "אך"; *ach*</note> to imply a division—meaning, use only half of the attribute of Justice, which is the Kindness within it. Since Justice is half Judgment and half Kindness, he said "but with justice" <unclear>and afterward said "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing."</unclear> He revealed the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger. 

For this reason, Justice depends on Jacob, who is the <insert>Father</insert> of the tribes. He knew the great pain of children when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees against them, so he seeks Mercy and Righteousness for them. The secret of "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through **Justice**" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note> is followed by "and the holy God is sanctified through **Righteousness**." This means when Justice is exalted, the harsh Judgment is eased and makes way for the attribute of **El** <note>original: "אל"; a Name associated with kindness</note>. This is the secret of what is said: "And the holy God is sanctified through **Righteousness**" <term>Hebrew: *Tzedakah*; often used in Kabbalah to mean the softening of judgment through benevolence</term>. In general, when the Lord of Hosts is exalted through Justice, the attribute of *El*, which is higher, arrives and performs Righteousness, and the strict Judgment passes. This is the secret behind the saying that **Justice is included within Kindness and Judgment**, as it says, "Justice and Righteousness in Jacob You have made." 

The great secret is: "Righteousness and Justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <note>Hebrew: *Tzedek*</note> can sometimes act as Judgment when it receives a certain flow, as I explained that *Tzedek* can be a very strong judgment. But when **Justice** (*Mishpat*) is joined with it, then the Throne is established in Mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice and reaches as far as Kindness and Truth together, they are called the **Shining Face**; then everything becomes great Mercy. This is the secret of "they shall come before...

->Your face<-

***

<meta>Commentary section in smaller Rashi script</meta>

This hints at "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." They have a single intention, for the ultimate purpose and essence is the distribution of Judgment and Kindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through spiritual arousal. In the **Zohar** <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> on the portion of Balak, it says that the "Ancient of Ancients" <note>original: "עתיקא דעתיקין"; the most hidden, merciful aspect of God</note> looks upon all, and all is life, and everything becomes like the Sabbath and rest. When the light is rectified on the right, all Judgment is seen in the balance. Before anything was separated into the paths of the right or the support of the left, these were secrets given only to the holy head. And it is written, "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters..." <note>Psalm 29:3</note>. This is to say that "all His ways are justice." Justice is a revealed path, visible to all below, and not just hidden above. As it says, "For all His ways are justice," meaning it is a path revealed to the eyes of all who can recount it. Therefore, this is not written in secret. This is similar to what was said to Job... <unclear>regarding the concealment of counsel</unclear>. The verse explains that He revealed the secret to you... <unclear>the secret of wisdom and understanding</unclear>. (2) And the movement of Justice is because the Attribute of Judgment is gathered under the "hand" of Kindness, as is included in the secret of the Name **El**.

<meta>catchwords: Your face, 61</meta>

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic concept of "Mishpat" (Justice) as the balancing force between "Chesed" (Kindness) and "Din" (Judgment). It identifies the patriarch Jacob with this balance and explores how biblical verses regarding God's "perfect work" refer to the internal harmony of divine attributes.</summary>
<keywords>Mishpat, Justice, Din, Judgment, Chesed, Kindness, Jacob, Abraham, Isaac, YHVH Elohim, Tzedakah, Righteousness, Divine Attributes, Sefirot</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
A portion in which the Name **YHWH Elohim** <note>a combination of the Name of Mercy and the Name of Judgment</note> is mentioned implies that those actions are performed with all the qualities <note>Sefirot</note> completed through the Attribute of Judgment <term>Din</term> and the Attribute of Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. You find this, for instance, in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion <note>from Eden</note>, along with all those related matters. You will find that all of them occurred through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy, all in complete perfection, with mercy and judgment balanced as is fitting for a judgment of truth. According to this principle, the Torah states: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is this: The Rock <note>Tzur</note>, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty; He does not decree judgment until His work is "perfect" <term>Tamim</term>. Rather, the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes, Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term> and Judgment <term>Din</term>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect." For the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> contains the secret of two things; it is as if it said "twins" <term>Teumim</term>, except that in the language of honor used for high matters, it says "perfect" <term>Tamim</term>, while for lower matters it says "twins" <term>Teumim</term>. Thus it says: "And they shall be doubled <term>Teumim</term> below... they shall be coupled <term>Tamim</term> together at the head" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are "twins," above they are "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things—opposites, like an advocate and an accuser—but above, everything is a single intention. Whether it is the advocate or the accuser, both have one purpose. There is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, but only a judgment of truth. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," meaning He consulted with both Judgment and Mercy and then decreed the law. This is the secret of the "judgment of truth" <term>Mishpat Emet</term>. 

As for the phrase "for all His ways are justice" <term>Mishpat</term>, the meaning is that everything is visible to the eyes of all who see <note>l</note>, as it says, "for all His ways are justice." You already know that Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. For Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Column, the one who balances between the two "tents" of Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term>; Isaac corresponds to Judgment <term>Din</term>; and Jacob decides between them: "a perfect man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on Abraham's side and from Judgment on Isaac's side. Thus it says: "You have executed justice <term>Mishpat</term> and righteousness <term>Tzedakah</term> in Jacob" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. And the prophet said: "Correct me, O Lord <term>YHWH</term>, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The meaning of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice <term>Mishpat</term>" is found in the word "but" <term>ach</term> <note>often used in Hebrew to signify a part or a limitation</note>, meaning with only half of the quality of Justice, which is Mercy. For Justice is half judgment and half mercy. Therefore he said "but with justice," and then added "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret to diminish the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger <note>Judgment</note>. 

Therefore, Justice is dependent on Jacob, who is the "father" among the tribes. <warning>Transcription becomes difficult due to the tape mentioned in the OCR warning.</warning> Having known the great pain of children, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees against them, he <note>Jacob</note> seeks mercy and righteousness for them. The secret is: "But the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice <term>Mishpat</term>" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written immediately after? "And the holy God is sanctified through righteousness <term>Tzedakah</term>." This means that when Justice is exalted, the harsh Judgment is eased and turns toward the quality of *El* <note>the Name associated with Mercy</note>. This is the secret of what is said: "And the holy God is sanctified through righteousness." Generally, when the Lord of Hosts is exalted through Justice, the quality of *El*—which is higher—arrives and performs righteousness <note>n</note>, and Justice is refined. This is the secret of their saying that Justice is comprised of Loving-kindness and Judgment, as it says, "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." The great secret is: "Righteousness <term>Tzedek</term> and justice <term>Mishpat</term> are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek</term> is sometimes Judgment, based on what it receives in abundance, as I explained that *Tzedek* is a powerful, strengthened judgment. But when Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is joined with it, then the Throne is established with Mercy. If it is exalted through Justice, and reaches as far as Loving-kindness and Truth together—which are called the "Shining Countenance"—then everything becomes great Mercy. This is the secret of: "shall go before 

->Your face<-"

They have a single intention, for the ultimate essence is the distribution of Judgment and Loving-kindness according to the recipients prepared for them through awakening. In the Book of Zohar <note>Parashat Balak</note> it is noted that all is the "Ancient of Ancients"... <note>The Rashi script commentary here includes complex Aramaic citations from the Zohar regarding the balance of the Right and Left sides, the "Holy Head," and the "Voice of the Lord."</note> (a) As he says, "for all His ways are justice," Justice is a revealed path... visible to all and not hidden above... text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
A passage that mentions **YHWH Elohim** <note>original: "יה'וה אלהים"; the combination of the Tetragrammaton and the Name of Judgment</note> refers to actions performed through all the attributes, completed through both the Attribute of Judgment <term>Middat Ha-Din</term> and the Attribute of Mercy <term>Middat Ha-Rachamim</term>. You find this, for example, in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion <note>from Eden</note>, as well as in all those related matters. You will find that they all occurred through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy, and everything was done in complete perfection, with mercy and judgment each applied as was fitting in a judgment of truth. 

Based on this principle, the Torah says: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4; original: "הצור תמים פעלו"</note>. The meaning of the verse is this: "The Rock" <term>Ha-Tzur</term> refers to the One who decrees the judgment with strength, yet He does not act with cruelty. He does not decree the judgment until His work is "perfect" <term>Tamim</term>, meaning the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes, Kindness <term>Chesed</term> and Judgment <term>Din</term>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect." 

For the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> is the secret of two things; it is as if it said "twins" <term>Te’omim</term>. However, in the language of honor, the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> is used for two things of the upper world, while "twins" <term>Te’omim</term> is used for the lower world. Thus it says: "And they shall be coupled <term>Te’omim</term> beneath, and they shall be together perfect <term>Tamim</term> at its head" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are called "twins," but above they are "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things, opposites like an advocate and an accuser. But above, everything is one intention; whether the advocate or the accuser, both have one single aim. There is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, only true justice. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," for He deliberated with judgment and mercy and then decreed the sentence; this is the secret of "True Judgment."

Regarding the phrase "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, it means everything is revealed to the eye of all who see. As you already know, "Justice" <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the "Middle Line" that balances between the two "tents," which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Kindness <term>Chesed</term>, and Isaac corresponds to Judgment <term>Din</term>. Jacob decides between them, as he is the "perfect man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob because it draws from Kindness on Abraham’s side and from Judgment on Isaac’s side. Thus it says: "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob" <note>Psalms 99:4</note>. 

The prophet also said: "O Lord, correct me, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The meaning of this verse, "correct me, O Lord, but with justice," uses the word "but" <term>Ach</term> <note>often used in Hebrew to imply a limitation or division</note> to signify a portion; that is, through the half of the attribute of Justice that is Kindness. Since Justice is half judgment and half kindness, he said "but with justice," and then added "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger. 

Therefore, Justice depends on Jacob, who is the "father" among the tribes. He knew the great pain of children when the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees against them, and he would seek mercy and righteousness for them. The secret of the verse "And the Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in justice" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note> is revealed by what is written immediately after: "And the holy God <term>El</term> shall be sanctified in righteousness." This means that when Justice is exalted, the judgment is eased and turns toward the attribute of **El** <note>The Name associated with pure Kindness</note>. This is the secret of "The holy God <term>El</term> is sanctified in righteousness." Whenever "the Lord of Hosts" is exalted in justice, the attribute of **El**, which is from above, arrives and performs righteousness, and the judgment is sweetened. This is the secret of the saying that Justice is included within Kindness and Judgment, as it says: "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." 

The great secret is: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalms 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek</term> is sometimes Judgment, based on its reception of the flow, as I have explained that Righteousness is a powerful and strong judgment. But when Justice is joined with it, then the Throne is established with mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice and reaches Kindness and Truth together, they are called "The Shining Countenance," and then everything becomes great mercy. This is the secret of "go before...

This hints that "The Lord our God, the Lord is One" refers to a single intention. Their goal and essence is the distribution of judgment and kindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through spiritual awakening. In the Zohar <note>the primary text of Kabbalah</note>, in the section on Balak, it says that the "Ancient of Ancients" is entirely white. All is life, all is YHWH... and His radiance is established on the right. See that everything is balanced in the scale... spreading to the paths of the right to support the judgment... and from our side they exist... the secret of the Holy Head. And it is written: "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters." Regarding "For all His ways are justice," Justice is a revealed path that is visible below to the eye of all, unlike the hidden realms. Therefore, regarding Job it is written that he spoke in secret... and the explanation of the verse is that He revealed the secret to you... bina... and the memory of Justice is that the attribute of Judgment is gathered under the hand of Kindness...

A portion which mentions the name **YH'VH Elohim** indicates actions performed through all the attributes, completed through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy. You will find this in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion. In all those matters, you will find they occurred through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy, all in complete perfection, with mercy and judgment applied exactly as required by true law. According to this principle, the Torah stated: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The meaning of the verse is this: The Rock who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty; He does not decree judgment until His work is first "perfected," meaning the judgment He decreed was preceded by consultation with both attributes, Kindness <term>Chesed</term> and Judgment <term>Din</term>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <term>Tamim</term>. For the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> contains the secret of two things; it is as if it said "twins" <term>Te'omim</term>, but the language of honor uses the term <term>Tamim</term> for two things on a high spiritual level, while for things below it uses the term <term>Te'omim</term>.

Thus it says: "And they shall be doubled <term>Te'omim</term> at the bottom, and they shall be coupled <term>Tamim</term> together at the top" <note>Exodus 26:24; referring to the construction of the Tabernacle</note>. Below they are "twins," above they are "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things, a thing and its opposite, like an advocate and an accuser. But above, all is a single intention; whether it is the advocate or the accuser, both have one purpose. There is no hatred or love there, and no partiality, only true judgment. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," for He consulted with both Judgment and Mercy before decreeing the sentence. This is the secret of true judgment. 

Regarding the statement "For all His ways are justice," it means everything is visible to every eye, as it says "For all His ways are justice." You already know that Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the "Middle Pillar" that balances between the two "tents" of Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Kindness <term>Chesed</term>, Isaac corresponds to Judgment <term>Din</term>, and Jacob decides between them, as he is called "a whole man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob because it draws from Kindness on Abraham's side and from Judgment on Isaac's side. Thus it says: "You have executed justice <term>Mishpat</term> and righteousness <term>Tzedakah</term> in Jacob" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. 

The prophet said: "O Lord, correct me, but with justice <term>Mishpat</term>; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The meaning of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice" uses the word "but" <term>Ach</term> to denote a division, as if to say: "with half of the attribute of Justice, which is Kindness." For Justice is half Judgment and half Kindness. Therefore he said "but with justice," and followed it with "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret to diminish the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger. Justice is therefore dependent on Jacob, who is the "Father" among the tribes; having known the great pain of children when the Holy One decrees upon them, he seeks mercy and righteousness for them. 

The secret of the verse "The Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note> is found in what is written immediately after: "And the holy God is sanctified in righteousness." This means when Justice is exalted, Judgment rests and turns toward the attribute of **El**, which is the secret of the verse "And the holy God <term>Ha-El</term> is sanctified in righteousness." Generally, when "The Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice," the attribute of **El**—which is higher—arrives and performs righteousness, and Justice is sweetened. This is the secret of the saying that Justice is included in Kindness and Judgment, as it says: "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." 

The great secret is: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek</term> sometimes acts as Judgment according to how it receives the divine flow <note>original: "Kabbalato b'shefa"</note>, as I explained that *Tzedek* can be a strong, harsh judgment. But when Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is partnered with it, then the Throne is established with Mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice, and reaches as far as Kindness and Truth together, they are called the "Shining Countenance," and then everything becomes great mercy. This is the secret of: "They shall go before

# Gate 5
<sig>M</sig>

The manifestation in which the Lord God is recognized is that they are performed through all the attributes that terminate in the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy. As you will find in the creation of the first man, in His judgment of him, in his expulsion, and in all those matters, you will find that they all came about through the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy, and everything was in complete perfection through Mercy and Justice—everything according to what is fitting in true judgment. And according to this principle, the Torah says, "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The interpretation of the verse is thus: The Rock, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty. He does not decree the judgment except that "His work is perfect," meaning the judgment He decreed was previously consulted with the two attributes, Grace <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness</gloss> and Justice <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. And this is "His work is perfect," for the term "perfect" <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect/whole</gloss> is the secret of two things. It is as if it said "twins" <term>te'umim</term>, but because of the language of honor, it uses the term "perfect" for the two things above, while below it uses the term "twins." And thus it says, "And they shall be twins" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below, they shall be "perfect" at the head; below, twins, above, perfect. This is because below, they appear as two things, a thing and its opposite, as one assisting and one accusing. But above, everything is a single intent; whether the assistant or the accuser, both have one intent, and there is no hatred or love there, and there is no partiality there, but only true judgment. Therefore, it said, "His work is perfect," for He consulted with Justice and Mercy and decreed the judgment, and this is the secret of true judgment. Regarding that which is said, "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, it means everything is before the eyes of all who see, as it says, "For all His ways are justice." You already know that justice is included in Justice and Mercy, for justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the middle line, the one who mediates between the two tents, which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Grace, Isaac to Justice, and Jacob acts as the arbiter between them, "a plain man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. And justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Grace on the side of Abraham and from Justice on the side of Isaac. And thus it says, "Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have performed" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. And the prophet said, "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse: "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice"—what it says "but" <term>ach</term> <gloss>only/but</gloss> divides, meaning in half of the attribute of justice, which is Grace, for justice is half judgment and half grace. Therefore it said, "but with justice," and said afterward, "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret of limiting the half of justice on the side of anger. Therefore, justice depends on Jacob, who is the patriarch of the tribes, who knew great sorrow regarding his children when the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed upon them, so that he would request mercy and righteousness for them. And the secret is, "The Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in judgment" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written after it? "And the holy God is sanctified in righteousness." This means when the judgment is exalted from the rest of Justice, it makes room for the attribute of God <term>El</term>, which is the secret of what is said, "And the holy God is sanctified in righteousness." It means when the Lord of Hosts is exalted in judgment, the attribute of God comes, which is above, and performs righteousness, and the judgment functions. This is the secret of what they said, that justice is included in Grace and Justice, and it says, "Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have performed." And the great secret is, "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>, for righteousness is sometimes Justice according to its reception of the abundance, as explained, for righteousness is great Justice in strength. But when justice is participated with it, then the throne is established with Mercy. And if it is exalted in justice, and reaches unto Grace, and truth together are called the shining faces, then everything becomes great Mercy, and this is the secret of "Your faces shall precede"

->Your faces<-

The text explores how the Divine influences are distributed based on those receiving them, utilizing the metaphor of the scales of justice and the unification of opposites.</note>

text:
The decree preceded the seventy years. And so it says: "And his days shall be one hundred and twenty years." And it says: "In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah" and so on. Is it possible to say so? Rather, the decree was made one hundred and twenty years earlier. And so it says: "Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken from being a people." And you find it was the fourth year of Ahaz. Is it possible to say so? Rather, the decree was made from the days of Amos, two years before the earthquake, as it is said: "Thus says Amos: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be exiled from its land."

And the seventy years we count for Media... this writing alone... for the first was given to Babylon. And another year for the whole of Babylon stood Darius, and he received... and that was the first year unique to him. End of note.

---

# Chapter 29

"And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up" and so on. "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia" and so on. "Who is there among you of all His people" and so on. "Then the heads of the fathers arose" and so on. "Forty thousand" and so on. "Besides their servants" and so on. In general and in detail, they were only forty-one thousand and three hundred and sixty; and these twelve thousand are those who ascended from the other tribes. "And they set the altar upon its bases" and so on. "And they gave money to the masons" and so on. Cyrus reigned three years incompletely <note>referring to partial years in the count</note>. In the reign of Ahasuerus, "in the beginning of his reign" and so on, "then the work on the house of God was ceased." "In the third year of his reign, he made a feast" and so on. For all four years, Esther was hidden in Shushan the capital. "And Esther was taken to the king" and so on. For all five years, Haman was gathering spoil for Mordecai. "In the first month, which is the month of Nisan" and so on. On the thirteenth of Nisan, Haman wrote the letters to destroy, to kill, and so on. On the fifteenth of Nisan, Esther came before the king. On the sixteenth of Nisan, they hanged Haman. On the twenty-third of Sivan, Mordecai wrote letters to rescind the letters of Haman. On the thirteenth of Adar, "the Jews struck all their enemies" and so on, and they killed five hundred men in Shushan and hanged the ten sons of Haman because they had been adversaries against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. "On that day, the number of the slain came" and so on. And at that time in the following year, it is said: "Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, wrote" and so on. Behold it says: "For according to the fulfillment of seventy years... to fulfill the seventy years for the ruins of Jerusalem." Fifty-two years after the destruction of the Temple, Israel served in the kingdom of the Chaldeans; and they were counted and ascended. Three years of Cyrus, fourteen of Ahasuerus, and two of Darius; and in the second year of Darius, the Temple was built. And so Zechariah said: "Then the angel of the Lord answered... Lord of Hosts..."

<summary>Chapter 29 recounts the decree of Cyrus, the return of the exiles, the building of the altar, and the chronology of the Persian period, including the story of Esther and the completion of the Second Temple.</summary>
<keywords>Cyrus, Ahasuerus, Esther, Haman, Mordecai, Darius, Jeremiah, Second Temple, seventy years</keywords>

The decree came seventy years prior <note>referring to the prophecy of the exile being decreed before it physically began</note>. And thus it says: "And his days shall be one hundred and twenty years" <note>Genesis 6:3</note>. Rather, the decree existed one hundred and twenty years prior <note>The 120 years mentioned in Genesis are interpreted here as a countdown to the Flood rather than a human lifespan</note>. And thus it says: "Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken from being a people" <note>Isaiah 7:8</note>. But was this not in the fourth year of Ahaz? Is it possible to say so? Rather, it was a decree issued in the days of Amos, two years before the earthquake, as it is said: "Thus said Amos: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land" <note>Amos 7:11</note>.

And the seventy <unclear>years</unclear>... we do not find a "year of the Medes" in the scriptures except for this one alone. It was <unclear>his year</unclear> because the first <unclear>year</unclear> was attributed to Belshazzar. And one more year was added to the total that Darius stood, and he <unclear>completed his years</unclear> and that was the first year unique to him. Until here.

# Chapter 29

"Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up..." etc. "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia..." etc. "Who is there among you of all His people..." etc. <note>Ezra 1:1-3</note>. "Then rose up the heads of the fathers..." etc. "Forty thousand..." etc. "besides their servants..." etc. <note>Ezra 2:64-65</note>. In the general and the specific counts, there are only forty-one thousand three hundred and sixty; the [additional] twelve thousand are those who went up from the other tribes. "And they set the altar upon its bases..." etc. "They gave money also to the masons..." etc. <note>Ezra 3:3-7</note>.

Cyrus reigned three partial years. In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, <note>an accusation was written</note> to stop the work on the House of the Lord <note>Ezra 4:6</note>. "In the third year of his reign, he made a feast..." etc. <note>Esther 1:3</note>. For all four years, Esther was hidden in Shushan the capital. "So Esther was taken to the king..." etc. <note>Esther 2:16</note>. For all five years, Haman was gathering spoil for Mordecai. "In the first month, which is the month of Nisan..." etc. <note>Esther 3:7</note>. On the 2nd <note>original: ב, likely a transcription error for 13th</note> of Nisan, Haman wrote the letters "to destroy, to kill..." etc. <note>Esther 3:13</note>. On the 15th of Nisan, Esther came before the king. On the 16th of Nisan, they hanged Haman. On the 23rd of Sivan, Mordecai wrote letters to rescind the letters of Haman. On the 13th of Adar, the Jews struck all their enemies... and they killed five hundred men in Shushan and hanged the ten sons of Haman, because of the <term>sitnah</term> <gloss>accusation/adversity</gloss> against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. On that day, the number of the slain was brought [before the king]. And at that time the following year, it is said: "Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail... wrote..." <note>Esther 9:29</note>.

Behold, it says: "After seventy years are completed for Babylon..." <note>Jeremiah 29:10</note> and "to fulfill the desolations of Jerusalem, seventy years" <note>Daniel 9:2</note>. For fifty-two years after the destruction of the Temple, Israel remained in the kingdom of the <term>Kasdim</term> <gloss>Chaldeans</gloss>; <unclear>they were remembered</unclear> and went up. There were three years of Cyrus, fourteen of Ahasuerus, and two of Darius. In the second year of Darius, the Temple was built. And thus Zechariah said: "Then the angel of the Lord answered and said: [O Lord of hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem... against which You have had indignation these seventy years?]" <note>Zechariah 1:12</note>.

<keywords>Cyrus, Ahasuerus, Darius, Esther, Haman, Mordecai, seventy years, Second Temple, chronology, Nisan, Adar, Sivan</keywords>

The decree preceded the seventy years. So it is said: "And his days shall be one hundred and twenty years" <note>Genesis 6:3</note>. And it says: "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, etc." <note>Genesis 7:11</note>. Is it possible to say he was [already] one hundred? Rather, the decree was [made] one hundred and twenty years [prior]. And so it says: "And within sixty-five years shall Ephraim be broken from being a people" <note>Isaiah 7:8</note>. And was that year four [years] prior? Is it possible to say so? Rather, the decree was a decree from the days of Amos, two years before the earthquake, as it is said: "Thus said Amos, by the sword shall Jeroboam die, and Israel shall surely go away captive out of their land" <note>Amos 7:11</note>.

And the seventy years were counted for the kingdom of Media; the writings only indicate this one <note>referring to a specific calculation of exile</note>... <unclear>it was decided for them because the calculation was given to the ruler</unclear>. And one additional year for the total; Darius stood and <unclear>collected the years; they were the specific calculation belonging to him</unclear>. Thus far.
