text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
beside them, upon his return to the Giver, as it is written: For they shall see eye to eye, when the Lord returns to Zion. And it is said: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. Father of Mercy, He shall comfort the laden people and remember the covenant of the steadfast <note>the Patriarchs</note>, and save our souls from the evil hours, and rebuke the evil inclination from those who are borne up, and favor us with eternal survival. And may He fulfill our requests with the measure of good, salvation, and mercy.

<note>Decorative ornament</note>

The Chair of the Prophets, the book of the fear of the coasts <unclear>...</unclear>
And this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted.
His majesty is over earth and heaven. He has raised a horn for His people, a praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people near to Him. Hallelujah.

And he says: In the name that stands for generations, and it is written <unclear>...</unclear> and in time as counted for the generation.
The Chair of the Prophets <term>pasak</term> <gloss>break</gloss> <note>all the coasts, etc.</note>

And with confidence he said: Return, O Lord, to the ten thousand thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength. Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy. For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed. For I have given you good instruction; do not forsake my Torah. It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it, and those who support it are happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old. Happy are they <note>referring to Psalm 145</note>, etc.

For the conductor, a psalm of David. May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high. May He send your help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifice. Selah. May He grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in Your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the saving strength of His right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever.

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory. And they receive permission from one another and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His Presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His power; holy forever and to all eternity. The Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of the radiance of His glory. Then a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place. And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great shaking of those who praise and say: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His Presence. The Lord shall reign forever and ever. The Lord, His kingdom stands forever and to all eternity. Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart to You. And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; He frequently turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You have sworn to our fathers from days of old. Blessed be the Lord, day by day He bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah. Lord of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed be He, our God, who created us for His glory, and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us a Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our heart through His Torah, and place in our heart love and fear of Him, to do His will and to serve Him with a perfect heart, so that we do not labor in vain nor give birth for terror. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing in the years of the Messiah and for the life of the world to come. So that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent; Lord my God, I will thank You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his trust. Trust in the Lord forever and ever, for in Yah, the Lord, is an everlasting Rock. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. The Lord desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.

<column-break/>

Lord, our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth.
Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the Lord.

And now, may the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies, Lord, and Your kindnesses, for they are from of old.

Magnified and sanctified be His great name <note>the start of the Kaddish prayer</note> in the world which He created according to His will. May He establish His kingdom, and cause His salvation to sprout, and bring near <note>an alternative reading: the end</note> of His Messiah. In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of the entire house of Israel, speedily and in a near time; and say, Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised, glorified and exalted, extolled and honored, adored and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Above <note>at times: and above all</note> all blessings and songs, praises and consolations that are uttered in the world; and say, Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and favor our prayer. May the prayer and supplication of the entire house of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven; and say, Amen. Receive, may the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be great peace from heaven, and life upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen. My help is from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His heights, may He make peace upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen.

A prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, answer me, for I am poor and needy. Guard my soul, for I am pious; save Your servant who trusts in You, You are my God. Be gracious to me, Lord, for to You I call all day long. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and listen to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, Lord, and shall honor Your name. For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God. Teach me, O Lord, Your way; I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your name. I will thank You, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever. For Your kindness is great toward me, and You have saved my soul from the lowest depths. O God, the arrogant have risen against me, and a company of violent men have sought my soul, and they have not set You before them. But You, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger and abundant in kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Work with me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because You, Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever. May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers; may He not forsake us nor abandon us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His judgments which He commanded our fathers. And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, that He maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is no other.

A song of ascents, of David. If it had not been the Lord who was on our side—let Israel now say—If it had not been the Lord who was on our side when men rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their anger was kindled against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul. Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped as a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth.

And You are holy, O You who are enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another and said: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory." Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the Lord.

text:
by their side, as he returns to the Giver, it is written: "For they shall see eye to eye when the Lord returns to Zion." And it says: "And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." The Father of mercy shall comfort His burdened people, and remember the covenant of the mighty ones, and save our souls from the evil hours, and rebuke the evil inclination from those who are carried, and show us grace for eternal survival. And He shall fulfill our requests with a measure of goodness, salvation, and mercy.

<note>Decorative ornament</note>

The throne of the prophets, the book of the awe of those who dwell, etc.
And the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel, according to the mouth of the Lord, by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted.
His glory is above earth and heaven. And He has lifted up a horn for His people, a praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, a people near to Him, Hallelujah.

And it says: "In the name of the Eternal, who stands for all generations." And it is written: "And the Lord," and "And the day," and "In the time," as it is counted for the generation of the congregation.
The throne of the prophets, a break <note>i.e., a paragraph division</note> (The sanctuary of those who dwell, etc.).

And trust, and say: "Return, O Lord, to the tens of thousands of the families of Israel." "Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength." "Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy." "For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed." "For I have given you good instruction; do not forsake My Torah." "It is a tree of life to those who grasp it, and those who support it are happy." "Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace." "Restore us, O Lord, to Yourself, and we shall return; renew our days as of old." "Happy," etc.

For the leader, a Psalm of David. "May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you high. May He send your help from the sanctuary, and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings, and accept your burnt sacrifice, Selah. May He grant you your heart's desire, and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up banners; may the Lord fulfill all your requests. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the mighty saving power of His right hand. Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have arisen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call." "And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit that is upon you, and My words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever."

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to the other and said: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory." And they receive [the response] one from the other and say: "Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His dwelling; holy upon the earth, the work of His might; holy forever and to all eternity. The Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of the radiance of His glory." A spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great, mighty commotion: "Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place." And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great trembling, praising and saying: "Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His dwelling." The Lord, forever and to all eternity. The Lord, His kingdom stands forever and to all eternity. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever for the impulse of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and prepare their heart toward You. And He, being compassionate, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; yes, He often turns His anger away and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, O Lord, are good, and forgiving, and abundant in loving-kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your Torah is truth. Grant truth to Jacob and loving-kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old. Blessed is the Lord, day by day He carries for us; God is our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. O Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is our God, who has created us for His glory, and separated us from those who go astray, and has given us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our hearts to His Torah, and place in our hearts His love and His fear, and to do His will, and to serve Him with a whole heart, so that we shall not labor in vain, nor bear children for panic. May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and that we may be worthy, and live, and see, and inherit goodness and blessing for the years of the Messiah and the life of the world to come. In order that my glory may sing to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and whose trust is the Lord. Trust in the Lord forever, for in the Lord God is an everlasting rock. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. He desires, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord our Lord, how glorious is Your name in all the earth!
Be strong and let your heart take courage, all who wait for the Lord.

And now, I pray, let the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies and Your loving-kindnesses, for they are from old.

Magnified and sanctified be His great name in the world which He has created according to His will; may He establish His kingdom, and cause His salvation to spring forth, and bring near [the time of] His Messiah, in your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily and at a near time, and say: Amen. Let His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed, and praised, and glorified, and exalted, and extolled, and honored, and raised up, and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, above (and beyond all) all blessings and songs, praises and consolations which are uttered in the world, and say: Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and favor our prayer. May the prayers and supplications of the whole house of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven, and say: Amen. Receive, may the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be great peace from heaven, and life, upon us and upon all Israel, and say: Amen. My help is from the Lord, maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His high places, may He make peace upon us and upon all Israel, and say: Amen.

A prayer of David. Incline Your ear, O Lord, and answer me, for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am pious; O my God, save Your servant who trusts in You. Be gracious to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in loving-kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All the nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, O Lord, and shall glorify Your name. For You are great and do wondrous things; You alone are God. Teach me Your way, O Lord; I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your name. I will thank You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify Your name forever. For Your loving-kindness is great toward me, and You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol. O God, the insolent have risen up against me, and a congregation of violent men have sought my soul, and have not set You before them. But You, O Lord, are a God full of compassion and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving-kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Show me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because You, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

O house of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
May the Lord our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; may He not leave us nor forsake us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His judgments, which He commanded our fathers. And let these my words, which I have prayed before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is none else.

A Song of Ascents, of David. "Had it not been the Lord who was for us," let Israel say. "Had it not been the Lord who was for us when men rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the torrent would have gone over our soul. Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul." Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, maker of heaven and earth.

text:
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the festival of Sukkot from the previous folio, specifically focusing on the mystical guests (Ushpizin) and the ethical requirements of hospitality and charity during the festival. It transitions into the 'Ra’aya Meheimna' (The Faithful Shepherd) section regarding the commandment of the Four Species.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

One who sees his portion within the holy nation excels in all matters of faith by receiving the <term>Ushpizin</term> <note>The seven mystical "guests" or founding fathers who visit the Sukkah: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David</note> to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. A person must bring joy to the poor, for the portion of those guests invited belongs to the poor. One who sits in the shadow of faith and invites these supernal guests—the guests of faith—but does not give them their portion <note>i.e., fails to feed the poor</note>, all of them stand over him and say:
> **"Do not eat the bread of a stingy man..."** <note>Proverbs 23:6; original: "Al tilcham et lechem ra ayin"</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One's, blessed be He. Concerning him, it is written:
> **"I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival offerings..."** <note>Malachi 2:3; original: "Vezareti feresh al pneichem... feresh chageichem"</note>

Woe to that person at the time when those guests of faith rise from his table! Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and prepare a table for them. Now that [the poor] invite him, and all the righteous ones, and King David, and they are not given their portion, it is the most difficult thing of all, and it is called:
> **"Move away from the tents of these wicked men..."** <note>Numbers 16:26; original: "Suru na me'al ohalei ha'anashim ha-resha'im ha-eleh"</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **"...but the belly of the wicked shall feel want."** <note>Proverbs 13:25; original: "U-beten resha'im techsar"</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **"The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up..."** <note>Proverbs 23:8; original: "Pitecha achalta teki'enah"</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **"For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that no place is clean."** <note>Isaiah 28:8; original: "Ki kol shulchanot mal'u ki tzo'ah bli makom"</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression... <note>The text here contains difficult Aramaic shorthand regarding David's role as the representative of the poor</note> because David was the "shield" for the poor, and he was made a guest, but [the host] did not want him, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. Since King David is the "Crown" and the "Right Hand" that sustains the world, the person who deprives him is more condemned than anyone. Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not exempted from acts of loving-kindness except by what he is able to do, as it is written: "according to the gift of his hand." One should not feel coerced, but should first satisfy himself and then give what remains to the poor; yet the spirit of all the guests remains with him. When the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, He calls out a blessing upon him:
> **"Then you shall delight in the Lord..."** <note>Isaiah 58:14; original: "Az ttit'anag al Hashem"</note>

And Isaac calls out over him:
> **"No weapon formed against you shall prosper..."** <note>Isaiah 54:17; original: "Kol kli yotzer alayich lo yitzlach"</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David says this because all the weapons of the King and the King's battles are entrusted to David's hand. Therefore, whoever rejoices with his portion... Jacob says to him: "Then your light shall break forth like the morning..." and the other righteous ones say: "And the Lord shall guide you continually and satisfy your soul..." King David says: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of weapons. When a person merits all these merits, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come is written of them:
> **"Your people shall all be righteous..."** <note>Isaiah 60:21; original: "Ve-amech kulam tzaddikim"</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

-> **"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day..."** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulav</term> <note>The palm branch used on Sukkot</note> as is proper during these days... this is the secret of what we established: "And you shall take" refers to a redemption, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion. The first [species] is the Lulav, which is prepared to take on the secret of the "Image of Man" (<term>Tzelem Adam</term>) and so it is below.

...The Holy One, blessed be He, called him "Image," as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, he is called by the name "Elohim" (God/Judge) at the time he brings truth and merit into the world... as it is written:

---

"Man in His image." And we have well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness"**—this was said at the time of the [divine] union. And such is the intention of both: "Image" (<term>Tzelem</term>) and "Likeness" (<term>Demut</term>) are one, emerging from the Male and Female. "And God created man in His image"—we find that at the time of the union, the King is present.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual consequences of failing to share the festival meal with the poor, which insults the mystical guests (Ushpizin). It then transitions into a mystical explanation of the Lulav and the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, Sukkot, King David, Lulav, Tzelem (Divine Image), Hospitality, Ra'aya Meheimna</keywords>

text:
<header>Emor</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion among the holy people, even more than all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss>, to receive the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. And a person ought to rejoice with the poor, because the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss> who are invited belongs to the poor. And he who dwells in all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss> and invites these supernal <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, the guests of faith, and gives them their portion, they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that that table which he prepared is his, and not the Holy One, blessed be He’s. Concerning him it is written:
> **Behold, I will rebuke your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, etc. The dung of your feasts, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person at the hour when those guests of faith stand up from the table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and to receive them at the table. Now that they have invited him, and all the righteous, and King David, and they do not give them their portion, that is more difficult than everything, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all rise and say: <term>Isaac</term> said:
> **And the belly of the wicked shall lack** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> said:
> **Your bread that you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And the rest of all the righteous said:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> said, and the laws of the destitute <note>or: oppression</note>, as it is written, and it was when the days were finished, and the Lord waved the... and they are speaking of the dead. Because David begged for the table and he was made a guest, but he did not seek, and did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. And like the crown and the right hand of King David, they judge the world, especially that person who closes his hand more than everything. Rabbi Eleazar said: The path of piety does not exempt a person, except by what he can, as it is written, according to the gift of his hand, etc. And not the board <note>or: tablet</note> of the poor, and the full and satisfied is the first, and what remains to give to the poor. Even the spirit of everything is that of the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, and he is given to the guests, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a friend with him, and for a blessing He calls upon him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This is what King David said, because all types of kings and those close to the King are entrusted into the hand of David. He who rejoices... in his portion, and his friend, etc. ...Jacob said to him... the rest of the righteous said... and the Lord shall satisfy you continually, etc. King David said, no weapon that is formed against you shall prosper, because he is entrusted with all types of types. And all the portion of a person who merits all this merit, the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, about them it is written:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

<column-break/>

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

**A commandment** this is, to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> properly on these days, and they are humble, and he adorns it, and the secret stands as we have established, "And you shall take," <term>Padirus</term> <gloss>a mystical term for taking/holding</gloss>, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time, for they are His. Likewise, they require the Holy One, blessed be He, in their portion, and delight in Him. And this is the first, this is the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss>, and it is fitting to take the mystery of the image of Man, and so below. It is done.

The creator, the blind to all in His mercies and in His laws, and also His deeds. All the creator, the blind, this is Man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls "the blind," as it is written, "And God created man in His image," and furthermore that which they seek in His name at the time when He is pure and distinct in the world, and they seek God, as it is written, "You shall not revile God," he called him in His name, as it is written, "And God created"

"man in His image," and beautifully we have established it, as it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness**, at the time when the union was mentioned. Like the crown that rises, we find that at the time of the union, it is found.

text:
<meta>continues from previous page: ...the people of the world who see that the person who has a portion in the holy nation is superior in everything regarding faith, by receiving guests to rejoice in this world and the world to come.</meta>

A servant <note>of God</note> must cause the poor to rejoice, for the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>Holy Guests</gloss> whom he invites belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these supernal guests, the Guests of Faith, and gives them their portion <note>by feeding the poor</note>, all of them stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6; the Guests refuse the table of one who does not share with the poor</note>

It follows that such a table which he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One’s, blessed be He. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those Guests of Faith rise from his table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham all his days stood at the crossroads to invite guests and receive them at his table. Now that they <note>the supernal Guests</note> invite him and all the righteous, and King David, and people do not give them their portion <note>by neglecting the poor</note>, this is the most difficult thing of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the rest of the righteous say:
> **For all tables are full of filthy vomit, so that there is no place clean** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression, for it is written <unclear>as the lead of the days</unclear> <note>The OCR text here contains highly corrupted readings of verses and Aramaic idioms</note>. This refers to David, for he was a guest and no one invited him or gave him a portion. Since King David is the crown and the right hand that sustains the world, that person who harms him is excluded from everything. Rabbi Eleazar said: The Torah does not impose a burden on a person beyond what he is able to do, as it is written, *every man shall give as he is able* <note>Deuteronomy 16:17</note>. One should not say: "I will eat and satisfy myself first, and what is left I will give to the poor." Rather, the essence of the Guests is the priority. If he gladdens the Guests, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, and the verse calls him for a blessing:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac says over him:
> **No weapon formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David said this because all the weapons of the King and the battles of the King were entrusted into the hands of David. Happy is the man who rejoices in his portion. Jacob said of him: *Then shall your light break forth as the morning, etc.* <note>Isaiah 58:8</note>. The rest of the righteous said: *And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul, etc.* <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. King David said: *No weapon formed against you shall prosper*, for he is appointed over all types of weapons. All this portion is merited by a person through these merits. Of the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, it is written:
> **Your people shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

***

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulvav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is proper in these days, to be humble and armed with it. This is the secret we have established: *And you shall take* <note>Hebrew: *u-lekachtem*</note> suggests *padi-ros* <note>A wordplay implying "redemption of the head"</note>, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion and take refuge in Him. First is the Lulav, which is the secret of the <term>Diyokna</term> <gloss>image/form</gloss> of Adam, and so it is below.

<unclear>Regarding the corrupted OCR text regarding Samael and mercy</unclear>. This "Adam" is what the Holy One, blessed be He, called "Man," as it is written: *And God created man in His own image.* Furthermore, it was explored in the <term>Bamma</term> <gloss>high place/altar</gloss> at the time when truth and radiance went out into the world. It is written *Elohim* <gloss>God/Judges</gloss> *you shall not revile* <note>Exodus 22:27</note>, and it is written: *And God created*

---

*man in His own image.* And we have well established what is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness** <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. This was said at the time of the union <note>of the divine attributes</note>. This is the intention of both, "image" and "likeness," for from the union of male and female came forth: *And God created man in His own image.* When the King ascended, we find that He was present at the time of the union.

<meta>continues from previous page: he would sit a second time for the people of the world who see that he has a portion in the holy nation. He has more than all others regarding faith, for receiving guests is to rejoice in this world and the world to come.</meta>

One must cause the poor to rejoice, for the portion of those <term>ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss> that one invites belongs to the poor. And he who sits in the shade of faith <note>within the Sukkah</note> and invites these supernal guests, these Guests of Faith, yet does not give them their portion <note>by failing to feed the poor</note>, all of them stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of a stingy man...** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that the table he prepared is his own and not for the Holy One, Blessed be He. About him it is written:
> **I will scatter dung upon your faces, the dung of your festivals...** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those Guests of Faith rise from his table! And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, stood at the crossroads to invite guests and prepare a table for them. Now, when they invite him and all the righteous ones and King David, and they are not given their portion, it is harder than all. It is called:
> **Depart now from the tents of these wicked men.** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And the rest of the righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of being crushed <note>oppressed/poor</note>, as it is written that he was like the dust of the seas. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, strikes, he speaks. Because David was low and became a guest <note>meaning he represents the attribute of Malchut, which has nothing of its own</note>, and if one does not want to invite him or give him a portion, it is as if he pushes away the Crown <note>the Shekhinah</note> and the Right Hand of King David. That person is excluded from everything. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not exempt from the duty of kindness except according to what he can afford, as it is written: *each according to the gift of his hand.* One should not be forced beyond their ability. If a person eats and is satisfied first, and gives what remains to the poor, that is also the portion of the guests. If he acts thus, the Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells with him and calls a blessing upon him:
> **Then you shall delight in the Lord...** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And <term>Isaac</term> calls over him:
> **No weapon formed against you shall prosper.** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Simeon said: King David said this because all the armaments and battles of the King are entrusted into the hands of David. Thus, one who rejoices in his portion and desires the poor, Jacob says of him: *Then your light shall break forth as the morning.* The other righteous say: *The Lord will guide you continually and satisfy your soul.* King David says: *No weapon formed against you shall prosper,* for he is appointed over all types of armaments. This person merits all these blessings, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come. Concerning them it is written:
> **Your people shall all be righteous...** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <note>Leviticus 23:40</note> <-

**This commandment** is to take the <term>lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is fitting in these days. They shall be humble and armed with it. This mystery is established: *And you shall take* <note>Hebrew: *u-lekachtem*</note> refers to the "Child of the Redemption" <note>Aramaic: *padiros*</note>, just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, man must seek the Holy One, Blessed be He, in their portion and take refuge in Him. The first among these is the <term>lulav</term>. It is prepared and pure to take the mystery of the image of Man, and so it is below. 

The Holy One, Blessed be He, calls Man "In My Image" <note>Aramaic: *samai*</note>, as it is written: *And God created man in His own image.* Furthermore, it is searched out in His name when Truth and Brilliance go out into the world. It is searched out through the name *Elohim* <gloss>God</gloss>, as it is written: *You shall not revile God* <note>Exodus 22:27</note>. He is called by His name, for it is written: *And God created...*

---

...man in His image. And we have established it well, for it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.** This was said at the time of the union <note>of the Divine attributes</note>. Such is the intention of both, <term>tzelem</term> <gloss>image</gloss> and <term>demut</term> <gloss>likeness</gloss>. From the union of male and female came forth: *And God created man in His own image.* <unclear>כפכח</unclear> When the King ascends, we find that at the time of the union, it is found.

text:
<header>Emor</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion in the holy people has a greater share in everything of <term>meheimnuta</term> <gloss>faithfulness/divine truth</gloss>, to receive the <term>ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests (the seven mystical guests invited into the Sukkah)</gloss> in order to rejoice in this world and the world to come. A person must rejoice with the poor, because the portion of those <term>ushpizin</term> is the poor. He who dwells in everything of faithfulness and invites these supernal <term>ushpizin</term>, the guests of faithfulness, and gives them their portion, they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

If it is found that that table which he prepared is his own, and not of the Holy One, blessed be He, concerning it is written:
> **And I will spread dung upon your faces, etc. The dung of your festivals, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person at the hour when those guests of faithfulness stand up from the table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and to receive them at his table. Now that they invite him and all the righteous and King David, and they do not give them their portion, that is the hardest of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all rise and say: <term>Isaac</term> said:
> **And the belly of the wicked shall lack** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> said:
> **The bread which you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the other righteous said:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, without a place** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> said, and concerning the laws of judgment, it is written: "And it was as the morning of the days, and the Lord waved [his hand]..." he speaks of when David cried out and he was made a guest, and he did not want or invite him or give him his portion. And as those crowns and the right hand of King David judge the world, so too does that person who acts perversely against him—more than anything. Rabbi Eleazar ben Rabbi Shimon said: Charity does not exempt a person, except as much as he is able, as it is written: "According to the day of the blessing of his hand, etc." And one should not eat <unclear>excessively</unclear> <note>The Hebrew text is damaged; the translation reflects the intent of duty toward the poor before one's own enjoyment.</note> but eat and be satisfied first, and what remains, give to the poor. For the spirit of all the <term>ushpizin</term> is there, and they are the <term>ushpizin</term>. And the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a friend to him, and a blessing is called upon him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Simeon said: This King David says it, because all the varieties of the King, and those near to the King, are entrusted into the hand of David. He who rejoices... his portion and his neighbor's... Jacob said to him, "And your morning shall break forth..." The rest of the righteous said, "And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy..." King David said, "No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper," for he is entrusted with all types of varieties. And all the portion of a person who merits all this merit, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, concerning them it is written:
> **And your people shall all be righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

<column-break/>

### The Faithful Shepherd

> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This is a **commandment** to take the <term>lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is proper in these days, and they are lowered, and he adorns it, and this is the mystery that we established: "And you shall take" <note>Hebrew: *u-lekhahtem*</note>... just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes them, Israel, at this time, for they are His. Likewise, they need to take the Holy One, blessed be He, into their portion and delight in Him. And for this, the first thing is this <term>lulav</term>, and he is invited to take the mystery of the image of man, and so below. He does.

The Blessed One... in His mercies and His laws, and also His deeds. All the blessed ones, this is man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls "man," as it is written: "And God created man in His image." And furthermore, that they are called by His name at the time that truth and peace are found in the world, and they are called "God," as it is written: "You shall not revile God" <note>Exodus 22:27</note>—He called him by His name, as it is written: "And God created"

<column-break/>

"man in His image." And beautifully we have established that which is written: **"Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness"** at the time that the union is mentioned. And such is the intent of both, "image" and "likeness," and it is one of male and female, for it went forth: "And God created man in His image." As the King ascends, we find that at the time of the union, it is found.

<summary>This page from the Zohar and the Faithful Shepherd discusses the spiritual duties of hosting guests (Ushpizin), the necessity of sharing with the poor, and the mystical significance of man's creation in the divine image during the festival period.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, Divine Image, Faithful Shepherd, Lulav, King David, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob</keywords>

<meta>This page transitions from general philological notes on demonic and angelic names (such as Danhish, Zeus, and Mana) to a specific examination of Text No. 20 (Museum Number CBS 16023). This text is an incantation written for a woman named Tardi, daughter of Oni, and is notable for its unique central illustration.</meta>

## UNIVERSITY MUSEUM. BABYLONIAN SECTION.

# No. 20 (Museum Number CBS 16023)

->In the name of Tardi, daughter of Oni<-

(2) Hormisdar Tardi. In the name of AAAAAA <note>The repeated letter Aleph often serves as a magical cipher or a call for divine attention</note>, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit <note>original: *latana*</note> and the evil Liliths <note>dangerous night-demons of Mesopotamian folklore</note> (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear to Tardi, daughter of [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel <note>the archangels Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael</note>. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah <note>a liturgical or musical pause</note>, Hallelujah. According to AAAAAA.

### Translation

Tardi, daughter of Oni (2) Hormisdar Tardi. In the name of AAAAAA, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear (to) Tardi, daughter of [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Hallelujah, Selah. According to AAAAAA.

### Commentary

A charm against ghosts. The interest of this bowl lies in the figure decorating the center. 

<note>The illustration depicts a demon with its arms and legs bound in manacles. On either side of the demon is an enclosed space; the space on the figure’s right side bears the inscription "Prohibition" </note><note>original: *asura*</note>, while the space on its left bears the inscription "Permission" <note>original: *resha*</note>. On the lower part of the demon's body, on the "Prohibition" side, the name of the client is written. This drawing graphically represents the idea that the demon is bound and has no legal or spiritual power over the woman.</note> 

The picture is of better quality than the inscription, which is very illiterate. The spelling is most careless.

1. The connection between the proper names is uncertain, as is the character of the names themselves. For **Hormisdar** <note>original: *hrmsdr*</note>, I might compare the Pahlavi <note>Middle Persian</note> name **Ormazdyar** <note>meaning "Friend of Ahura Mazda"</note>, found in Ferdinand Justi’s *Book of Iranian Names*, page 10a.
2. For the repeated letter **A** <note>original: א</note>, see the discussion on page 60.
3. **Latana** <note>original: *lt'n'*</note>: This is likely an artificial magical form created by adding a suffix; compare the similar forms for **Satan** <note>original: *stn'*</note>, **Talna** <note>original: *tln'*, a shadow-spirit</note>, and **Shidna** <note>original: *shydn'*, a demon-spirit</note>.

text:
to finish in judgment and pave the way to receive their holiness. Regarding this, it is said: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>. This means a miracle occurred regarding his attribute. Therefore, blessed be He, at the time of judgment, the Smallness <note>the lesser manifestation of the divine</note> has mercy on His world and returns to His deeds for the sake of the depths. This is the secret of the time of judgment: when everything is turned, then it is pure. 

In this way, contemplate how to understand the <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>Fear of Isaac</gloss> and the word according to its meaning. He is crowned in the Supreme, hiding His face below for His great soul, covering the attribute of Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. As His face is turned, the Supernal is revealed through the covering. This is the secret of "he turned his face" and was hidden. 

I will now explain to you more concerning the "back." Know that wherever you find the "light of the face" above, it is a great secret. The day of three attributes and the crown of the face are all attached to the <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>Fear of Isaac</gloss>. When the attribute of the <term>Keter</term> <gloss>Crown</gloss> illuminates its face, it is attributed to the totality of Mercy and is grasped there as Mercy. This is the secret: "God is the Lord, and He has given us light" <note>Psalm 118:27</note>. 

This is the order: "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound; they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance" <note>Psalm 89:16</note>. Contemplate the secret of: "when Isaac was old and his eyes were dim from seeing." You will then grasp the secret of the sounding of the <term>shofar</term> <gloss>ram's horn</gloss> on the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound" is that they will walk in the light of the face through the merit of the ram of Isaac. 

When you contemplate "in the light of Your countenance they shall walk," you will find our foundation when we say "the Rememberer of forgotten things." Through the secret of the "Back of the Throne," you will understand the difference between the "Rememberer of forgotten things" and the "Recall of the Back of the Throne." The "Rememberer of forgotten things" comes from the Great Mercy above, in the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light." The "Back of the Throne" comes from the attribute of <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>God/Judgment</gloss>, from the attribute of the darkness of which it is said "and darkness was upon the face of the deep" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>, which is the secret of the covering of Kindness <term>Chesed</term>. Therefore, the attribute of the Tetragrammaton illuminates below while being included in the attribute of <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>, which is the place of the secret of the head. This is the secret of "He turned His face." 

Understand this well regarding these two attributes. Now I will inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name, which is the mediator in the center. It connects and encompasses its perfection. These are the "nicknames" of the Name that stands in the middle, connecting the right side, which is <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Kindness</gloss>, and the left side, which is <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. They are all included in the middle through Kindness and Judgment. These are called the "Attributes of Mercy," and their height in the middle of the emanation is the Mercy of the worlds.

I will now explain. Know that all the holy names, the nicknames, and the words, whether they are called Kindness, whether they are called Mercy, or whether they are called Judgment: there is not one among them that is pure Kindness or pure Judgment or pure Mercy without a mixture. This applies to everything from the first emanation and downward. But from Him and upward, all is Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture. 

Now, open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters. They are like rules for the paths of the Chariot and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>Divine Emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand how the <term>Sefirot</term>, the Names, and the words are connected in the world. Regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, you will understand the secret of the "Root of the All." Know that the Names of the Supernal <term>Keter</term> <gloss>Crown</gloss> are all simple Names without any mixture. Like the known days of Mercy that are close to the name <term>Ehyeh</term> <gloss>I Will Be</gloss>, or the Kindness that is close to the name <term>Ehyeh</term>, they are all perfectly simple without mixture. This is the secret of what is said: "but with great mercies will I gather thee" <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. What are these "great mercies"? They are...

<keywords>Pachad Yitzchak, Keter, Mercy, Judgment, Shofar, Divine Countenance, Chesed, Din</keywords>

to finish in judgment and paved a way to receive their arrival. Regarding this, it is said: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, he <note>the Ancient One/Keter</note> fled to him, he fled to his attribute <note>Judgment</note> from the Word. Therefore, may He be blessed, at the time of the Small Judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for My sake, for My sake I will do it <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>, for how shall He be profaned? This occurs at the time of the Small Judgment. All of this generation consists of lines of "everything," and this is the secret of "all of it is turned white; he is clean" <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>. In this way, contemplate to understand the <term>Fear of Isaac</term> <gloss>the attribute of Judgment</gloss>, the strength and the Word, according to the sense that the Supreme <term>Keter</term> <gloss>Crown</gloss> is crowned, shining its face downward to the great Void, covered with Life to the lap of Mercy, according to the sense that the Supreme shines His face, becoming revealed from the covering. This is the secret: "God <note>YHVH</note> caused His face to shine and was gracious to you" <note>Numbers 6:25</note>.

Behold, I shall explain to you further through the Word: know that wherever you find "Light of the Face" above, it is a great secret. It is because the three attributes and the <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>Diadem/Shekhinah</gloss> are the face of the World, and they all cling to the <term>Fear of Isaac</term>. When the attribute of the Crown <term>Keter</term> shines its face, it is attributed to everything as Mercy and is grasped here as Mercy. This is the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light" <note>Psalms 118:27</note>. This is the order: "Happy is the people that knows the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance" <note>Psalms 89:16</note>. Thus, contemplate the secret: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>. Then you will grasp the secret of the blast <note>of the Shofar</note> in the secret of "God has gone up with a shout" <note>Psalms 47:6</note>, for the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that knows the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance" is that they will find mercy from the sound of the Shofar of the ram of Isaac. 

When you contemplate the meaning of "in the light of Your countenance they walk," which is our foundation, we say "He who remembers the visual-perceptions" <note>a liturgical phrase</note>. Through the secret of the "Back of the Word," you will understand what exists between "He who remembers the visual-perceptions" and "He who remembers the Back of the Word." For "Remembering the visual-perceptions" is drawn from the great Mercies of above, in the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light." But the "Back of the Word" is drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, from the attribute of Judgment of which it is said: "and darkness was upon the face of the deep" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>, and "He remembered the secret and the kindness." Therefore, the attribute of the Lord <note>YHVH</note> shines below, included in the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, the place where the secret is in the head. This is the secret of "He caused His face to shine and was gracious to you." 

Understand this well, for the world stands upon these two attributes. Therefore, I inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name <note>YHVH</note>, may He be blessed, which is the decisive factor in the middle, and it is uniquely composed of His completeness. Like the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>YHVH as Elohim</note>, which stands in the middle, surveying the right—which is Kindness <term>Chesed</term>—and the left—which is Judgment <term>Din</term>—and they are all included in the middle from Kindness and Judgment. They are all called by the nicknames of Kindness in the middle, and they are called the nicknames of Mercy, and their elevation is in the middle, for the Mercy and the Crowns prevail. 

Behold, I explain through the Word: know that all the Holy Names and the nicknames and the words—whether they are called Kindness, whether they are called Mercy, or whether they are called Judgment—not one of them is pure Kindness or pure Judgment or pure Mercy unless there is a mixture in them, from that level and below. But from that level and above, everything is pure Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture in the world. 

Now, open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, like the principles of the steps of the Chariot and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>Divine Emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand a bit of how the <term>Sefirot</term> and the Names and the words are connected in the world. By His crowning, may He be blessed, you will understand the secret of the General Root of everything, may He be blessed and exalted. Know that the names of the Supreme Crown <term>Keter</term> are all simple names without any mixture of a thing. Just as the known Mercies that are adjacent to the name <term>Eheyeh</term> or the Kindness adjacent to the name <term>Eheyeh</term> are all completely simple, having no mixture of a thing. Regarding this, it is said: And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, a miracle occurred for him, a miracle regarding his <term>middah</term> <gloss>divine attribute</gloss> of which it speaks. Therefore, May He be Blessed, at the time of the small judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for My sake, for My sake, I will do it <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>. This is the time of the small judgment. David, everything is sick, a generation of lines, everything; and this is the secret of: it is all turned white, he is clean <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>.

In this way, contemplate and understand the Fear of Isaac <note>the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment</note>, and from there, according to the sense that he is crowned in the Most High, he illuminates his face below. For when the Great Kindness <term>Chesed HaGadol</term> covers the <term>Atik</term> <gloss>The Ancient One</gloss> of Mercy, according to the sense that the illumination of His upper face reveals itself from under the covering. And this is: The Lord make His face shine upon thee <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. Behold, I am explaining to you further with the help of Heaven. For in every place where you find the illumination of the face above, it is a great secret, which is that the three attributes and the Crown <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>the Shekhinah</gloss> are the "face" of the Name. All of them are attached to the Fear of Isaac. When the attribute of the Crown <term>Keter</term> illuminates its face, it is attributed to the totality of Mercy and is grasped here as Mercy. This is the secret of: God is the Lord, who hath shewed us light <note>Psalm 118:27</note>. This is the order: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance <note>Psalm 89:16</note>.

Contemplate the secret of: And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim so that he could not see. From this, you will grasp the secret of the sounding of the <term>Shofar</term> <gloss>ram's horn</gloss> on the day of our festival. The secret of: Happy is the people that know the joyful sound; they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance. Mercy will be shown there from the <term>Shofar</term> of the ram of Isaac. When you contemplate: In the light of Thy countenance they shall walk, which is our foundation, we say: He who remembers the bindings <note>the Binding of Isaac</note>. And from the secret of "Remembrances of the Sounding," you will understand what is between "He who remembers the bindings" and "Remembrances of the Sounding." For the "Remembrances of the Bindings" are drawn from the great Mercies above, in the secret of "God is the Lord, who hath shewed us light." But the "Remembrances of the Sounding" are drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, from the attribute of the Satan, as it is said: for he will curse Thee to Thy face <note>Job 1:11</note>, and the secret of "the companion of kindness" is remembered.

Therefore, the attribute of the Lord <term>YHVH</term> shines below, included in the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, a place where everything is included in the head. This is the secret of: The Lord make His face shine upon thee. From this, understand the standing of these two attributes. Therefore, let it be known to you the secret of the attribute of the Name <term>YHVH</term>, May He be Blessed, which is the deciding factor in the middle. It unites from the side of its perfection. In the names of the <term>Milu'im</term> <gloss>expansions of the Name</gloss> of <term>YHVH</term> which stands in the middle, it illuminates the right side, Kindness <term>Chesed</term>, and the left side, Judgment <term>Din</term>. They are all included in the middle from Kindness and Judgment. All the nicknames of Kindness in the middle are called Nicknames of Mercy, and their ascent in the middle of the <term>Milu'i</term> is the proliferation of Mercies and closeness.

Behold, I clarify with the help of Heaven. Know that all the Holy Names and the Nicknames and the Words—whether those called Kindness, whether those called Mercy, whether those called Judgment—there is not one among them that is pure Kindness or pure Judgment or pure Mercy without having in them a mixture. All of them are from the middle and downwards. But from the middle and upwards, everything is Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture in the world.

Now open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, which are like principles for the levels of the Chariot <term>Merkavah</term> and the bond of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>Divine Emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand how the <term>Sefirot</term> and the Names and the Words are bound together in the world. Through His Providence, May He be Blessed, you will understand the secret of the General Root of everything. Know that the names of the Supernal Crown <term>Keter Elyon</term> are all simple names without any mixture of a thing. Like the known Mercies that are adjacent to the Name <term>El</term> or the Kindness adjacent to the Name <term>El</term>, they are all simple perfections without any mixture of a thing. This is the secret of what is said: but with great mercies will I gather thee <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. And what are "great mercies"? Only...

<keywords>Isaac, Mercy, Judgment, Shofar, Keter, Atik, Sefirot, Divine Names, Chesed, Din</keywords>

to finish with judgment and to pave a path for their destruction. Regarding this it is said: And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, he fled from it, he fled from his attribute <note>the attribute of strict judgment</note>. Therefore, may He be blessed, at the time of harsh judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for My sake, for My sake, I will do it <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>; for how could He be destroyed? This is the time of harsh judgment: All of it has turned white; he is clean <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>, and this is the secret of: All has turned, therefore he is clean. 

In this manner, contemplate and understand the Dread of Isaac <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>the attribute of severe judgment</gloss>. When it is crowned by the Supreme <term>Keter</term> <gloss>the Crown, the highest emanation</gloss>, it illuminates its face downward to the great abyss, covering it with Mercy. This is like the Supernal face illuminating and revealing itself from under the covering. This is the meaning of: The Lord cause His face to shine upon you <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. 

I shall now explain to you another secret. Know that wherever you find the "shining of the face" above, it is a great secret. It is because the three attributes <note>likely Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note> and the Crown <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>the Diadem or Shekhinah</gloss> are the face of the inwardness. They all cling to the Dread of Isaac, and when the attribute of the Crown <term>Keter</term> illuminates its face, it is attributed to the totality of Mercy and is perceived here as Mercy. This is the secret of: God is the Lord, and He hath given us light <note>Psalm 118:27</note>. 

This is the order of the verse: Happy is the people that know the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance <note>Psalm 89:16</note>. Contemplate the secret: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing. From this you will grasp the secret of "Sound the <term>Shofar</term> <gloss>ram's horn</gloss> on the New Moon" <note>Psalm 81:4</note>, for the sake of the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound <term>Teruah</term>; they walk in the light of Thy countenance" means they will receive mercy from the ram of Isaac. 

When you contemplate the phrase "in the light of Thy countenance they walk," it is the foundation of what we say in prayer: He who remembers the binding <note>of Isaac</note>. From the secret of the "remembrance of the binding" you will understand the difference between "He who remembers the binding" and "He who remembers the ashes of the binding." "Remembering the binding" is drawn from the Great Mercy above, through the secret of: God is the Lord, and He hath given us light. "The ashes of the binding" are drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, from the attribute of the Judge <term>Dayan</term>, of whom it is said: For He shall look upon the face of the deep. Thus, the attribute of the Tetragrammaton <term>Y-H-V-H</term> shines below, included within the attribute of <term>Elohim</term>, which is the place of the foundation of the head. This is the secret of: He caused His face to shine upon you.

Stand firm in knowing these two attributes. Now I will inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term> which balances in the center and unites with its perfection. Like the image of a balance, <term>Y-H-V-H</term> stands in the middle, balancing the right side which is Kindness <term>Chesed</term> and the left side which is Judgment <term>Din</term>. They are both included in the center, between Kindness and Judgment. All the titles of Kindness in the center are called Titles of Mercy, and their ascent to the middle of the balance increases Mercy and closeness. 

I will now explain. Know that all the Holy Names, the Titles, and the Words—whether they are called Kindness, whether they are called Mercy, or whether they are called Judgment—none of them are pure Kindness, pure Judgment, or pure Mercy. Rather, they are all a mixture from the level of the Balance and below. However, from the Balance and above, everything is pure Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture at all. 

Now open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, which are like principles for the levels of the Chariot <term>Merkavah</term> and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand how the <term>Sefirot</term>, the Names, and the Words are tied together in the world. By His will, you will understand the secret of the general rule of everything. Know that the Names of the Supreme Crown <term>Keter Elyon</term> are all simple names without any mixture of anything. Even the known Mercies that are adjacent to the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> or the Kindness adjacent to the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> are all entirely simple and have no mixture. This is the secret of: But with great mercies will I gather thee <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. What are these "great mercies"? They are...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical mitigation of strict judgment through the "shining of the face" and the role of the central Sephirah in balancing Kindness and Judgment. It explains that while lower emanations are mixtures of attributes, the highest Crown consists of pure, unmixed Mercy.</summary>
<keywords>Isaac, Keter, Chesed, Din, Teruah, Shofar, Binding of Isaac, Names of God, Balance</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>to finish with judgment and to clear a path to take them in. Concerning this it was said: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, he fled from his attribute, for the text is speaking of his own nature. Therefore, Blessed be He, at the time of minor judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for the sake of His name to His preoccupation, for thus He is blessed. And this is during the time of minor judgment: "it is all turned white, he is clean" <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>; and this is the secret of everything being overturned, therefore it is pure. 

Through this path, contemplate and understand the "Fear of Isaac" <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>the attribute of Severity or Judgment</gloss>. Its strength and existence are based on the notion that it is crowned by the Supernal One, who illuminates His face from above to the Great Abyss, covering the living with the garment of Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. This is the meaning of His supernal face being illuminated and revealed. This is the secret of "The Lord make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you" <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. 

Behold, I will explain further, for whenever you find "light of the face" above, it is a great secret. It refers to the "Day that is entirely Good" and the Crown <term>Keter</term>, which are the "Face" of the World. All are attached to the "Fear of Isaac." When the attribute of the Crown illuminates its face, it is attributed to complete Mercy and is perceived here as Mercy. This is the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light" <note>Psalms 118:27</note>. 

This is the order of the verse: "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound <term>Teruah</term> <gloss>the broken blast of the Shofar</gloss>; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance" <note>Psalms 89:16</note>. Contemplate the secret of "when Isaac was old and his eyes were dim from seeing." You will then understand the secret of the Shofar blast <term>Tekiah</term> in the secret of the Shofar on the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound" is that they will walk in the light of the face, receiving mercy from the ram of Isaac <note>A reference to the ram sacrificed in place of Isaac, associated with the Shofar of Rosh Hashanah</note>. 

When you contemplate "in the light of Thy countenance they walk," which is our foundation, we say in prayer: "He who remembers the kindnesses of the fathers" <note>original: "Zocher chasdei avot"</note>. You will then understand the difference between "He who remembers the kindnesses" and "all the memories of the mothers." For "Remembering the kindnesses" is drawn from the Great Mercy above, in the secret of "God is the Lord and He has given us light." But the "memories of the mothers" are drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>the attribute of Judgment</gloss>, from the attribute of the darkness of which it is said, "And darkness was upon the face of the deep" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>, where the secret of "And He remembered His kindness" is mentioned. 

Therefore, the attribute of the Tetragrammaton <term>YHVH</term> <gloss>the four-letter name of God</gloss> illuminates below, being included in the attribute of <term>Elohim</term>, the place of the secret of the head. This is the secret of "His face shines upon you." Understand this pillar that stands between these two attributes. I must inform you of the secret of the name <term>YHVH</term>, which is the deciding factor in the center, unifying all towards its perfection. It is like the central pillar <term>Amuda de-Emtaita</term> that balances the right, which is Kindness <term>Chesed</term>, and the left, which is Judgment <term>Din</term>. They are both included in the center, drawn from both Kindness and Judgment. Those on the side of Kindness in the center are called "Attributes of Mercy," and their root in the central pillar is Mercy and closeness. 

Behold, I am clarifying: know that all the holy names and titles, whether called Kindness or Mercy or Judgment, none of them are purely Kindness, purely Judgment, or purely Mercy. Rather, they are mixed. This applies to every level from the middle downwards. However, from the middle and upwards, everything is complete Mercy and pure Kindness without any mixture at all. 

Now, open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, which are like the principles of the central points and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand how the Sefirot and the names and words are connected in the world. Regarding His crown, you will understand the secret of the general principle of everything. Know that the names of the Supernal Crown <term>Keter</term> are all simple names without any mixture of anything else. Just as the known mercies associated with the name "God" <term>El</term> or "Kindness" <term>Chesed</term> are completely simple without mixture. This is the secret of "But with great mercies will I gather thee" <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. What are "great mercies"? They are...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical connection between Isaac's attribute of Judgment and the Supernal Mercy of the Crown, explaining how the central pillar of the Sefirot balances these forces. It details how divine names represent mixtures of Mercy and Judgment except at the highest levels where Mercy is pure.</summary>
<keywords>Isaac, Keter, Shofar, YHVH, Elohim, Chesed, Din, Rachamim, Sefirot, Central Pillar</keywords>
