When the King had finished his pleasant meal, he poured wine and established a joyful feast.
When the King had consumed two or three goblets of wine, his face glowed from the warmth of the spirits.
He said, "O host of the golden palace, your residence is pleasant and your provisions are abundant.
Yet this sixty-step high palace, whose summit the sky touches with a lasso,
How can you, after sixty years have passed, be able to mount it?"
The host replied, "May the King endure forever; may the Kauthar <note>a river in Paradise</note> be his wine, and the houri his cupbearer.
This is not strange for me, for I am a man; how could I remain behind from such a height?
What is strange is that there is a girl, moon-like, soft and delicate as fur and fine silk,
Who brings an ox like a mountain on her neck to the place where it grazes.
She carries it up the sixty steps in one go, without resting on any step.
The ox, moreover, is a beast like an elephant, which cannot even drag its own fat for a mile.
By God, if anyone in this land were to lift a single breath from the ground,
And a woman then carries it up a sixty-step fortress, would this not be a wonder?"
When the host told the King this story, the King bit his fingertip in astonishment.
He said, "How can such a deed be? It is not possible, or if it is, it must be sorcery.
I cannot believe this claim to be true, until I see it with my own eyes first."
Then he requested of the host that he prove the truth of his statement.
When the host heard this, he went down and told the story to the ox-slayer.

<summary>The King expresses disbelief at his host's claim that a delicate girl carries a massive ox up sixty steps, prompting the host to attempt to prove the feat.</summary>
<keywords>Haft Paykar, Nizami Ganjavi, King, Host, Feat of Strength, Illusion, Wonder</keywords>

text:
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Tabernacle's construction, specifically focusing on the mystical mechanics of the Cherubim and the unity of the Divine Name. It transitions from the structural elements of the Sanctuary to the internal spiritual state required to perceive the Divine essence.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Of the radiance—all of them established it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is the "crushed one"? <note>original: "deika katya," referring to a state of brokenness or contraction</note> Isaac bowed his head. Isaac was "crushed" and took pity on his portion; Heaven forbid he should be angry, for his portion was not like the others. And behold, Isaac represents the quality of Severity <note>term: Din - the attribute of strict justice and judgment</note>, yet here he is associated with Kindness <note>term: Chesed - the attribute of expansive love</note>. For when all are in Judgment, Mercy <note>term: Rachamim - the balancing attribute of compassion</note> emerges from the King. Wisdom inherits Kindness, for Kindness bows, and Isaac as Judgment is included in Kindness. Isaac bows before Mercy, for from it comes the "Hard Judgment," and in this way, they are included above, one within the other, until everything is known as one. Everything depends on this unity, and for everything to be found as one, the Heavens are needed forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no "scratches" <note>imperfections or divisions</note> in it when we see it as one. One desires both of them to complete the whole, such as Jacob <note>who represents the balance between Kindness and Severity</note>, and this is what is written:
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves that if you only read from our side or the other side, the whole is not known. Everything rises in one balance <note>term: Matkla - the mystical scales of equilibrium</note>; it does not change and will not be altered, as it is written:
> I am the Lord, I do not change <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: All the shining cups <note>the Sephirot or divine emanations</note> are illuminated by one another and depend on one another. Their foundation is one whole, never to be separated. Whoever separates them by his own power is separated from the Life of the Worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** said: It is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This refers to what is written regarding the "brazen-faced" Cherubim <note>Keruvim</note>. It is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written, "And He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when the Divine Presence dwells in a settled state with support (this is when perfection is found). "He rode upon a Cherub" (singular) refers to when the King is not settled upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" (plural) refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from its fellow, for it is written:
> and their faces shall look one to another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This occurs when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "Do not uncover the nakedness of a daughter-in-law or a youth." Woe to the one who uncovers their nakedness <note>meaning to reveal secrets prematurely or to cause division in the divine realms</note>. In this manner, it is written of Jacob that he "passed through from end to end." And thus is the portion of Israel with the Holy One, Blessed be He; they are found in their adornments in the likeness of that which is above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In former days, when one man said to his fellow, "Show me one vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to his fellow, "Take money and show me another," but there is no one to taste and no one to incline his portion, except for those few who are gathered and elevated to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Of them it is written:
> Your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the money is filled and sustained. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised <note>the covenantal people</note>, all those who are tied to the upper knots, they investigate. Woe that it is filled, and all those below depend on it. A window is opened, and they are polished and prepared from the smoke to the order that rests upon them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>term: Sifra Detzniuta - a foundational, highly cryptic Kabbalistic text</note>, it proves: Woe above, woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. What is the "fright" of the Book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These chapters are all in the Great Palace and fill the whole earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are superior in this way. **The Rabbi said**: Woe to the one who bends and bows, and to the one who does not ascend and bow to them in this way.

---

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived in the fields and did not know the ways of the city-dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat in its raw form <note>as plain kernels</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good fine bread. He said, "What is this for?" They said, "It is bread to eat." He ate it and found it very pleasant. **The Rabbi said**: "From what is this made?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said, "And what are these made of?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him royal pastries <note>delicacies</note> made with honey and oil. He said, "And what are these made of?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Surely I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat!" Because of that... <note>The parable illustrates that while the simple man thinks he knows the "essence" by eating raw grain, he misses the refined beauty of the "garments" or "preparations" (the commandments and mystical insights) that turn the raw essence into a royal feast.</note>

<summary>This page explores the mystical unity of the Divine attributes through the symbolism of the Cherubim and concludes with a famous parable about a villager who fails to appreciate refined bread because he only knows raw wheat, illustrating the depth of the Torah's hidden meanings.</summary>
<keywords>Cherubim, Balance (Matkla), Unity of God, Parable of the Wheat, Isaac, Jacob, Sifra Detzniuta, Severity and Kindness</keywords>

**Rabbi Eleazar** explained all of these things. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac, saying, "Who is the <term>din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>? It is the bent/constricted one." Isaac said, "The <term>din</term> is the part that is hidden; heaven forbid that I should be angry if it is not my portion." And yet, is Isaac not <term>chesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness</gloss>? It is bent, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is all <term>din</term>; He is <term>rachamim</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> that is bent, and Mercy is hidden. He inherits the <term>chesed</term> because the <term>chesed</term> is bent. And Isaac, as <term>din</term>, is <term>chesed</term>. Isaac is bent by Mercy, which is severe <term>din</term>. And in this, it was above, this from that, and it went forth from that until everything became known as one, and from one all are suspended. And everything is not found as one unless the heavens are forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** made it known that there are no traces <unclear>that can be seen</unclear> when we see it, and one desires both to understand everything, such as Jacob, and this is what is written:
> "The middle bolt in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end." <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

It is a complete vessel, for if it were not called from this side and from this side, everything would not be known. Everything is able to be in one balance; it neither rises nor changes, as it is written:
> "For I the Lord do not change." <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are shining sparks, from here and from here they are suspended, and they establish the palace as one, and everything is not to be separated. And whoever separates them by his power is separated from eternal life. **Rabbi Yitzhak** said: It is written:
> "And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them." <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is what is written: "And they are brazen-faced, the Cherubim," and this is what is written: "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written: "And He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim"—when it begins to be settled in assistance, it is written "He who sits upon the Cherubim" (this is when it is found in perfection). "And He rode upon a Cherub"—one, when the King is not settled upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim"—two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from the other, for it is written:
> "And their faces shall look one to another." <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

When they are at peace in the world. **Rabbi Yitzhak** said: We have learned, "The nakedness of a sister and the nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover." Woe to whoever uncovers their nakedness. In this manner, it is written regarding Jacob, "from end to end." And in this way, the portion of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in His ornaments, in the manner of the above, as it is written:
> "Israel in whom I will be glorified." <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Yitzhak** said: In the days of the ancients, it was as when one said to his companion, "Prepare for me a portion of wheat and take from it silver." Now, a man says to his companion, "Take from it silver," and he sees it in the husk, and there is no one who tastes it, and there is no one who knows its portion, except for the few wise and light ones who are attached to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written:
> "And your people all of them righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified." <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that it is consumed and the silver is maintained. **Rabbi Yitzhak** said: Woe, for we see that all those who are connected to the higher knots stand and observe, woe that it is consumed, and all those below are suspended. Woe. The window opens, a door, and they are changed and fixed from the knot to the order that is <unclear>upon them</unclear>. And like a book of longing, it is written: woe above, woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. He who is the longing of the book—**Rabbi Hizkiyah said**: These are the chapters that are all in the great palace, and they fill the whole earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are thus, and they are superior. **Rabbi** said: A curse be upon him who covers and bends, and for him who does not rise and bend them thus.

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived among the villagers and did not know the dwellings of the city. He sowed wheat and ate wheat as it was. One day, he entered the city to the king's feast. He said, "Why does this man eat here?" They said, "It is the king's custom to eat." He ate and tasted a sweetness he had never known. **Rabbi** said: From what is this made? They said, "From wheat." Later, the king brought him delicacies that were in the city. He tasted them and said, "And this sweetness, what is it?" They said, "From wheat." Later, the king brought him royal delicacies that were in honey and oil. He said, "And this sweetness, what is its making?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Certainly, this city is the secret of all the sweetness here, and it is the root of all the sweetness that is here, it is wheat." And because of that...

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>of the brightness — all of them established it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: who is the "oppressed person" <note>original: *dikah katya*</note> who bent down? Isaac was thin and oppressed, he looked upon his portion; Heaven forbid he should be angry, for his portion was not like the others. And behold, Isaac is from the side of <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Lovingkindness</gloss> which bends, yet it is said that all of them are <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. He is from the side of <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> which bends, and Mercy is the King. Wisdom inherits Lovingkindness, for Lovingkindness bends. And Isaac, though acting as Judgment, is from the side of Lovingkindness. Isaac bent within Mercy, yet from him comes harsh Judgment. And so it was above, this from that, and it emerged from this until that, so that all is recognized as one. All things are suspended from one another, and to find that all is one, the Heavens are needed forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no paths for it <note>the Divine presence</note> except when we see it as one. One desires both to complete the whole, such as Jacob, as it is written:
> And the middle bolt in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end. <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves the whole; for if you do not read it but from this side and from that side, all is recognized. It can do all; in one <term>Metkala</term> <gloss>Scale of Balance</gloss> it rises, it does not change and shall not be altered, as it is written:
> I am the Lord, I change not. <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** [said]: all these lights shine from one another and are suspended from one another. Their foundation is one whole, not to be separated. Whoever separates them by his own strength is separated from the Life of Worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** [said]: it is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them. <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is what is written, "fierce of face" <note>original: *azim panim*</note>, the <term>Keruvim</term> <gloss>Cherubim</gloss>. And it is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>Psalm 80:2</note> and "He rode upon a Cherub and did fly" <note>Psalm 18:11</note>. "Sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when the Divine settles in support; it is written "Sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note> when perfection is found. "He rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> when the King is not settled upon His throne. "Sits upon the Cherubim" means two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from the other, for it is written:
> And their faces shall look one to another. <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This is when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "the nakedness of your daughter-in-law" <note>Leviticus 18:15</note> and "the youth of your father-in-law" <note>referring to uncovering secrets</note>, you shall not reveal. Woe to him who reveals their nakedness <note>uncovering divine mysteries inappropriately</note>. In this manner it is written of Jacob that he "passed through from end to end." And thus the portion of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in their adornment, just like the pattern above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified. <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** [said]: in former days, when one man said to another, "Show me a certain vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to another, "Take money and show me another," and there is no one to taste and no one to incline his portion, except for those few who are gathered and supreme before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written:
> Your people shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the silver is depleted and remains. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, all those who are crowned stand above in investigation. Woe that it is filled, and all these depend on the lower world. A window was opened for us and they are renovated and prepared from the incense for the arrangement that rests upon them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>original: *Sifra de-Tzniuta*</note> it is proven: woe above and woe below, and all rise in one scale of the balance. What is the concealment of the Book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These are the chapters that are all in the Great Palace and fill all the earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: all of them are more excellent than this. **The Rabbi said**: Woe to him who bends and bows, and to him who does not rise and bend to them so.

A parable of a man who lived among the fields and did not know the ways of the city dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat in its raw form. One day he entered the city, and they brought before him a good bread. He asked, "What is this for a man to eat?" They said, "It is bread, for eating." He ate it and found its taste very pleasant. **The man said**, "From what is this made?" They said, "From wheat." Later they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said, "And from what are these made?" They said, "From wheat." Later they brought him the royal pastries <note>original: *tariki malkin*</note> kneaded with honey and oil. He said, "And from what are these sweets made?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Truly, I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat." <meta>continues from previous page regarding the Middle Bolt and the divine balance of the Sefirot</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

of the radiance — they have all established it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is this "crushed one" <note>likely referring to the crushing of the spirit or the refinement of the soul</note>? Isaac bowed his head. Isaac, who represents the portion of Judgment <note>Din</note>, was concerned for his portion, Heaven forbid! He was stirred, for his portion was not like the others. For Isaac represents Judgment, yet here it is described as Mercy <note>Chesed</note>. And it is asked: since all is Judgment, how can it be Mercy? And how can Mercy be found within the King? He inherited the side of Lovingkindness <note>Chesed</note> so that the Lovingkindness was bent <note>integrated</note>, and Isaac, as Judgment, became part of Mercy. Through this, Judgment was softened by Mercy. And so it is above: one is included in the other, and one emerges from the other, until everything is known to be one. For they all depend upon one another, and for all to be found as one, the Heavens <note>the Sefirah of Tiferet</note> are required forever and ever. 

**Rabbi Eleazar** made it known that there are no divisions within it when we look at it as one, and one is desired within both of them to complete the whole, just like Jacob. And this is what is written:
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves that if you do not read from this side and from that side, all is known as one power, all rising in one balance, never changing and never shifting, as it is written:
> I the Lord do not change <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Judah** said: All the lights shine from one another and depend upon one another, and their foundation is one, all of it, and they must not be separated. One who separates them in his mind is separated from the Life of Worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** said: It is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This refers to what is written regarding the "brazen-faced" <term>Keruvim</term> <gloss>Cherubim</gloss>. And it is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>Psalm 80:1</note>, and it is written, "And He rode upon a cherub and did fly" <note>Psalm 18:10</note>. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when the Divine Presence comes to rest in a state of support <note>a state of stability</note>; it is written "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note>, for this is found in perfection. But "He rode upon a cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King is not resting upon His throne. "Sitting upon the Cherubim" refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from its fellow, for it is written:
> And their faces shall look one to another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This occurs when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned that the nakedness of a daughter-in-law or a youth must not be revealed. Woe to the one who reveals their nakedness! In this manner, it is written of Jacob that he "passes from end to end." And in this way, the portion of Israel belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they are found in His adornments, mirroring the pattern above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In earlier days, when a person said to his fellow, "Show me one thing and take money for it." Now, a man says to his fellow, "Take money and show me a mystery," and there is no one to taste it and no one to incline his ear, except for a few choice individuals who belong to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Of them it is written:
> And your people shall all be righteous, they shall inherit the land forever; they are the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe, for the money is full and established! **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, yet all those who are separated from the higher knots seek... woe, for it is filled, and all those below depend on these... woe. A window was opened for us and they were corrected and prepared from the smoke to the order that rests upon them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>Sifra Di-Tzeniuta</note>, it proves woe above and woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. What is the fear of the Book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These chapters are all within the Great Palace and fill the whole earth. **Rabbi Judah** said: All of them are even more superior than this. **The Rabbi said**: Woe to the one who deviates and bows, and to the one who does not rise and bow to them in this way.

---

### The Parable of the Wheat

It is like a man who lived in the fields and did not know the ways of the city dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat in its raw form <note>literally "as its own body"</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good bread. He said: "What is this man eating?" They said: "It is bread, made for eating." He ate it and found it very tasty. **The Rabbi said**: "From what is this made?" They said: "From wheat." Afterward, they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said: "And from what are these made?" They said: "From wheat." Afterward, they brought him royal pastries <note>fine delicacies</note> made with honey and oil. He said: "And from what are these made?" They said: "From wheat." He said: "Certainly, I am the master of all these, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat!" And because of that... <note>He remains ignorant of the refinement and art that transforms the raw grain into a masterpiece, just as one who only knows the literal Torah does not understand its mystical secrets.</note>

<summary>This page discusses the balance of divine attributes, the symbolism of the Cherubim's faces as an indicator of cosmic peace, and presents a parable illustrating that while the literal Torah is the "wheat," its mystical interpretations are the refined delicacies that reveal its true worth.</summary>
<keywords>Isaac, Judgment (Din), Mercy (Chesed), Cherubim, Jacob, Sifra Di-Tzeniuta, Parable of the Wheat, Literal vs. Mystical, Divine Balance</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The radiance—all of them are established by it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac, saying, "If the <term>din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss> is severed, if it bends, then Isaac is the severed <term>din</term>. He tasted his portion, heaven forbid, he became angry and did not remain in his portion. And yet, is Isaac not <term>chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> that bends, and is everything not <term>din</term>? Is <term>rachamei</term> <gloss>Compassion</gloss> not the bending, and is compassion not from it?" He grasped that he inherits <term>chesed</term>, for <term>chesed</term> bends, and Isaac as <term>din</term>, he is <term>chesed</term>. Isaac bent through <term>rachamei</term>, which is the harsh <term>din</term>. Through this, one was above the other, and he issued from it, until all was known to be one. From one, all are suspended, and if all were not found to be one, the heavens would require it forever and for all eternity. **Rabbi Eleazar** made known that there are no boundaries for Him when we behold Him thus, and one desires both to comprehend everything, such as Jacob, and this is that which is written:
> "A bar from one end to the other." <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This clarifies that if one does not call out from this side and from this side, everything is known. Everything is able to be weighed in one <term>mitkala</term> <gloss>scale/balance</gloss>; it does not sink, and it does not change, just as it is written:
> "I, the Lord, have not changed." <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Judah** said: All the radiant lights are suspended from one and the other. They are established as one, and they are not to be separated. And he who separates them with his power is separated from eternal life. **Rabbi Isaac** said: It is written,
> "I will make boys their leaders, and capricious children shall rule over them." <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is that which is written, "and the cherubim have faces of brass," and it is written, "He who sits upon the cherubim," and it is written, "He rode upon a cherub and flew." "He who sits upon the cherubim"—when He begins to be seated in assistance, it is written "He who sits upon the cherubim" (this is when He is found in completeness). "And He rode upon a cherub"—this is when the King is not seated upon His throne. "He who sits upon the cherubim"—these are two. Woe to the world when one cherub turns its face away, for it is written,
> "And their faces were toward one another." <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This is when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "The nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover." Woe to him who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner, it is written of Jacob, "A bar from one end to the other." In this way, the portion of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in His adornments, as it is written:
> "Israel, in whom I will be glorified." <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In the former days, it was that when one said to his companion, "Show me a measure, and take money from it." Now, a man says to his companion, "Take money from it," and he looks at the husk, and there is no one who tastes, and there is no one who knows his portion, except for a few who are small, who are joined to the Holy One, blessed be He. It is found as it is written:
> "Your people also shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified." <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe to that which is poured out, and money is established. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe to those who are gathered; I see all those who are gathered from the knots that stand above. Woe to those who are gathered, and all those who hang below, those who are woe. The window opens a door, and they are changed and prepared from the knot to the order that oversees them. And as the book of attachment clarifies, woe above and woe below, and all of them arise in one scale. Regarding the attachment of the book, **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These are the chapters, for all of them are in the great hall and fill all the earth. **Rabbi Judah** said: All of them are thus, and they are excellent. **The Rabbi said**: Woe to him who is bent and has bowed, and to him who has not ascended and bowed them thus.

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived among the wild, and he did not know the dwellings of the city. And he sowed wheat and ate wheat as it was. One day, he entered the city to the baker, a good man. He said, "What is this? For what is this man?" They said to him, "It is to eat." He ate and tasted the sweetness of it. **The Rabbi said**: This exaltation, he makes it. They said, "Wheat." Afterward, the baker brought fine loaves made with flour. He tasted their sweetness and said, "And this sweetness, how was it made?" They said, "Wheat." Afterward, the baker brought royal delicacies made with honey and oil. He said, "And this sweetness, how was it made?" They said, "Wheat." He said, "Certainly, this contains all the sweetness that is here, for it is the root of all the sweetness that exists—it is wheat." And because of that...

<summary>This page explores the mystical union and balance of the divine attributes through the metaphor of the Cherubim and the scales of judgment and mercy, culminating in a parable about wheat as the hidden essence of all nourishment.</summary>
<keywords>Cherubim, Din, Chesed, Rachamei, Balance, Jacob, Wheat Parable, Divine Essence, Zohar</keywords>

# (XXVI)

->APPENDIX B.<-

**For hatred:** I call to you, evil demon, and foreign demon <note>original: shida akhira'ah</note>, and demon without mercy. I call to you, evil demon who sits in the graveyard and holds the <term>akhasta</term> <gloss>a vessel or cup, often associated with a measure of suffering</gloss> of the sons of men. She shall go and set her knot <note>a magical binding or curse</note> upon <term>P' B' P'</term> <gloss>Ploni bar Ploni, a placeholder for the target's name</gloss> in his head, in his eyes, in his mouth, in his tongue, in his belly, and in his throat. And pour into him troubled waters <note>original: maya pazu'ey</note> in his belly. And if 5 you do not go and cast water into his belly, I shall send evil upon you through the angels Fuziel, Gozal, Pasdiel, and Peruzal. I have called you and <unclear>bound</unclear> <margin>2. l. qitrei <note>a correction suggesting "knots" or "bindings"</note></margin> those six <note>referring to the demonic entities or the angels of the curse</note> so that you shall go quickly against <term>P' B' P'</term> and release into him foul <note>original: sava</note> waters in his belly, and kill <term>P' B' P'</term>, for this is my desire. Amen, Amen, Selah.

**For hatred:** Write upon a day-old egg at a Christian grave <note>literally: the grave of a Nazarene</note>. I adjure 10 you by the luminaries <margin>3. naharei <note>a correction for "lights" or "luminaries"</note></margin> of heaven and earth: just as heaven was separated from the earth, so split and separate <term>P' B' P'</term> from <term>P' B' P'</term> his wife. Separate them from one another just as life is separated from death, and as the sea is separated from the dry land, and water from the river, and the mountain from the valley <note>original: galamta, meaning a clod of earth or raw matter</note>, and night from day, and light from darkness, and the sun from the moon. 15 So shall you separate <term>P' B' P'</term> from <term>P' B' P'</term> his wife. Separate them from one another during the twelve hours of the day, the three <term>watches</term> <note>original: arl, likely a corruption of "watches" or "divisions"</note> of the night, the seven days of the week, the thirty days of the month, the seven Sabbatical years <note>original: shemitin</note>, and the fifty years of the Jubilee <note>original: yovla</note>. On every single day, in the name of Tamtamiel the angel-Satan, and in the name of Ziabaiel the angel, and in the name of Darsamiel the angel, and in the name of Zahabukh the angel, and in the name of Dataf the angel, and in the name of Zahatzmiel the angel, and in the name of Zasniel the angel. They are appointed over pain and over <unclear>finizta</unclear>, <unclear>tzatka</unclear>, and <unclear>hadarzufa</unclear> <note>these terms likely refer to specific types of physical or spiritual afflictions</note>. Separate 20 <term>P' B' P'</term> from <term>P' B' P'</term> his wife, and let them be far from each other. They shall not be able to comfort one another, quickly in this and quickly <unclear>by leprosy</unclear> <note>original: be-tzari'a, possibly meaning "through a plague"</note>. Finished.

<summary>This page contains two Aramaic magical recipes for "hatred," intended to cause physical illness or the permanent separation of a married couple. The spells invoke demons of the graveyard and specific angels to enforce the curses through symbolic separations and physical afflictions.</summary>
<keywords>magical recipes, protective magic, aggressive magic, divorce spells, demonology, graveyard magic, Ploni bar Ploni, angel names, Sabbatical years, Jubilee</keywords>

For Hatred. I call upon you, evil spirit, and destructive spirit <note>original: "shada" <gloss>demon/spirit</gloss></note>, and spirit without mercy. I call upon you, evil spirit, you who dwell in the graveyard and take hold of the cloak of human beings. You shall go, tie a knot upon <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> <note>often abbreviated in manuscripts as "Ploni son of Ploni"</note> on his head, his eyes, his mouth, his tongue, his throat, and his entrails, and you shall pour filthy water into his belly. And if you do not go and pour water into his belly, I will send upon you evil ones: the angels Puziel, Guzael, Pasdiel, and Pruzael. I have summoned you and bound you <note>emending the text based on the note "ve-kiturei" <gloss>and bindings</gloss></note> so that you go immediately upon <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> and pour filthy water into his belly, and kill <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear>, for this is what I desire. A.A.S.

For Hatred. Write upon an egg laid that day, in the grave of a Christian <note>original: "Natzrani" <gloss>Christian/Nazarene</gloss></note>. I adjure you by the hidden things of heaven and earth: just as the heavens were separated from the earth, so shall you separate and divide <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> and <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and separate them one from another, as the living were separated from the dead, and as the sea was separated from the dry land, and the water from the river, and the mountain from the valley, and the night from the day, and the light from the darkness, and the sun from the moon. So shall you separate <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> from <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and separate them one from another, by the twelve hours of the day and three hours of the night, and the seven days of the week, and the thirty days of the month, and the seven years of release, and the fifty years of the jubilee, each and every day, in the name of the angel Tamtamiel, the satan, and in the name of the angel Ziabael, and in the name of the angel Darsamiel, and in the name of the angel Zahabuch, and in the name of the angel Da'af, and in the name of the angel Zehazmael, and in the name of the angel Sasniel, who is appointed over the pain, and over the <unclear>finitah</unclear> <gloss>uncertain term, perhaps affliction</gloss> and the <unclear>tzacha</unclear> and the <unclear>hadrozofa</unclear>. Separate <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> from <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and let them distance themselves, one from the other, and let them not be able to find comfort in one another, in a hurry and in pain. Complete.

She shall go and place a knot <note>a magical binding</note> for So-and-So son of So-and-So in his head, in his eyes, in his mouth, in his tongue, in his belly, and in his gullet. And if 5 you do not go and cast water into his bowels, I shall send against you evil ones: the angels Puziel, Guziel, Pasdiel, and Peruzal. I have called you and <unclear>bound</unclear> <margin>variant: buried</margin> you that you shall go quickly against So-and-So son of So-and-So and cast foul water into his bowels and kill So-and-So son of So-and-So, for I desire it. Amen, Amen, Selah.

**For hatred**: Write on a day-old egg at the grave of a Christian <note>original: Nozrani</note>: I adjure 10 you by the <unclear>luminaries</unclear> <margin>variant: rivers</margin> of heaven and earth. Just as the heavens are separated from the earth, so divide and separate So-and-So son of So-and-So from So-and-So his wife. # (XXVI)

->APPENDIX B.<-

For Hatred: I call to you, evil demon, and alien demon <note>original: sha</note>, and demon without mercy. To you I call, evil demon who sits in the graveyard and takes the shroud <note>original: achasta; possibly a funerary vessel or cloth</note> of human beings. She shall go and repeat the knot for <term>So-and-so son of So-and-so</term> <gloss>original: P'B'P, abbreviation for Ploni bar Ploni</gloss> in his head, and in his eyes, and in his mouth, and in his tongue, and in his stomach, and in his windpipe. And release upon him foaming waters in his belly. And if 5 you do not go and cast waters into his belly, I will send against you the evil angels Puziel, Gozal, Pasdiel, and Pruziel. I call to you <note>marginal note: and the knots</note> are these six, that you shall go quickly to So-and-so son of So-and-so and release foul waters into his belly and kill So-and-so son of So-and-so, for I desire [it]. <term>Amen, Amen, Selah</term>.

For Hatred: Write on a day-old egg at the mouth of a Christian grave: I adjure 10 you by the rivers <note>original: naharei</note> of heaven and earth. Just as the heavens are separated from the earth, so split and separate between So-and-so son of So-and-so and So-and-so his wife. And separate them from one another just as the living are separated from the dead, and as the sea is separated from the dry land, and the water from the river, and the mountain from the valley <term>galmata</term>, and the night from the day, and the light from the darkness, and the sun from the moon. So separate So-and-so son of So-and-so from So-and-so his wife. Separate them from one another during the 15 twelve hours of the day and the three watches <note>original: arl; likely an error for 'watch' or 'hour'</note> of the night, and the seven days of the week, and the thirty days of the month, and the seven Sabbatical years, and the fifty years of the Jubilee, every single day. In the name of Tamtamiel the satanic angel, and in the name of Ziabael the angel, and in the name of Darsemiel the angel, and in the name of Zahavuch the angel, and in the name of De'ataf the angel, and in the name of Zehatzmael the angel, and in the name of Zasniel the angel, who are appointed over pain and over <term>pinizta</term>, <term>tzatacha</term>, and <term>hadarzufa</term> <note>specific types of strife or magical afflictions</note>. And separate 20 So-and-so son of So-and-so from So-and-so his wife. They shall distance themselves from one another and they shall not be able to comfort one another, quickly in judgment and quickly in leprosy <note>original: batzri'a</note>. End.

<summary>This appendix provides two Aramaic magical recipes for causing hatred and separation. The first summons graveyard demons to inflict physical illness, while the second uses a day-old egg and cosmic analogies to dissolve a marriage.</summary>
<keywords>separation magic, graveyard demons, adjuration, Aramaic incantations, Tamtamiel, marriage dissolution, ritual objects, angelic names</keywords>

# Apostle

he was the one who began to speak. 12 And the priest of the messenger of God, who was outside the city, brought a bull and wreaths to the door of the house where they were staying, and he wished to offer a sacrifice to them. 13 When Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their clothes and leapt out to the crowd, and were crying out: 14 "Men, why are you doing this? We are also men of like nature as you, and we feel as you do. We believe you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth, the seas, and all that is in them. 15 He is the one who, in past generations, allowed all the nations to go their own way. 16 Nevertheless, He did not leave Himself without a witness, as He did good things from heaven: He sent them rain and made fruits grow in their seasons and filled their hearts with food and gladness." 17 And when they said this, the people saw it and said that no man should offer them a sacrifice. 18 But Jews came there from <term>Konia</term> <gloss>Iconium</gloss> and from Antioch, and they taught the people against them, and they stoned Paul and threw him outside the city because they thought he was dead. 19 And the disciples gathered around him, and he rose and entered the city. On the next day, he and Barnabas left and came to the city of Derbe. 20 And when they taught the people of that city, many disciples were added to them; they returned to the city of Lystra and to Konia and to the city of Antioch. 21 And they were encouraging them in their belief.

# Apostolos <note>The term denotes the Apostolic writings or the Acts of the Apostles.</note>

For he began to speak. 12 The priest of the <term>angel</term> <gloss>messenger</gloss> of God <note>original: "אלדים" (Elohim)</note>, who was outside the city, brought oxen and garlands to the opening of the house where they were encamped, and he wished to offer a sacrifice to them. 13 Barnabas and Paul, when they heard, tore their garments and leaped out to the assembly of the people, and they were crying out. 14 And they said, Men, why do you do such things? We are also men like yourselves, and we fear like yourselves. We believe that you should turn away from these vain things and turn to the living God, 15 who made heaven and earth, the seas, and all that is in them. 16 He, in the generations that passed, allowed all the nations to walk in the way of their choosing. 17 Even so, He did not leave His essence without witness; He did good to them from the heavens, and He brought down rain for them, and grew fruits for them in their seasons, and filled their hearts with food and gladness. 18 And since they said this, the people saw and said that no man should offer a sacrifice to them. 19 And Jews came there from Iconium and from Antioch, and they taught the people against them, and they stoned Paul and cast him out of the city because they thought he was dead. 20 The disciples gathered around him, and he arose and entered the city. On the second day, he and Barnabas departed from there and came to the city of Derbe. 21 And since they taught the people of that city, many disciples were added to them; they returned to the city of Lystra, to Iconium, and to the city of Antioch. 22 And they established themselves in the faith.

<summary>This page recounts the events in Lystra where Barnabas and Paul prevent a sacrifice intended for them, urging the people to worship the living God instead. It further details the subsequent opposition from Jews of Iconium and Antioch, Paul's stoning and recovery, and the continued missionary travels to Derbe.</summary>
<keywords>Barnabas, Paul, Lystra, Iconium, Antioch, Derbe, sacrifice, apostles, faith, stoning</keywords>

# Acts <note>original heading: "אפוסטולוס" (Apostolos), the Greek name for the book of the apostles</note>

he was the one who began the speaking. 12 And the priest of the "messenger of God" <note>original: "מלאך אלדים". In the Greek this is the priest of Zeus; the translator uses the same phrase he gave to Barnabas in the previous verse.</note>, who was outside the city, brought an ox and a garland to the door of the house where they were staying, and he wanted to offer a sacrifice to them. 13 When Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments, leapt up, and went out to the crowd <note>original: "בית אוכלוסא", literally "the house of the multitude", from the Greek <term>ochlos</term> <gloss>crowd</gloss> by way of Aramaic</note>, and they were crying out, 14 and said: "Men, why are you doing this? We too are human beings like you, with feelings like yours <note>original: "וחוששכם כמותכם"; the wording is awkward, and the sense is "subject to the same sufferings as you"</note>, and we bring you the message <note>original: "וסוברין אנחנו", a rendering of the Syriac for "we announce good news"</note> that you should turn away from these worthless things and turn toward the living God. He it is who made the heavens and the earth, the seas, and all that is in them. 15 He it is who, in the former generations, allowed all the nations to walk in the way of their own choosing. 16 Even so, He did not leave Himself without a witness <note>original: "לא הניח עצמותו אפילו שלא יהא הזהרו בו"; the Hebrew is obscure here and is translated according to the sense of the passage</note>: He did good things for them from heaven, brought down rain for them, made fruits grow for them in their seasons, and filled their hearts with food and gladness." 17 And when they had said this, they barely restrained the people <note>the manuscript reads "ראוהו העם ואמרו", literally "the people saw him and said"; the expected sense, as in the Greek and Syriac, is that the apostles with difficulty held the people back</note> so that no one would offer a sacrifice to them. 18 And Jews came there from <term>Kuniya</term> <gloss>Iconium</gloss> and from Antioch, and they stirred up the people against them, and they stoned 19 Paul <note>the manuscript spells the name "פוליפוס" (Polipos) here, apparently a copyist's slip for Paul</note> and threw him outside the city, because they thought he was dead. 20 And the disciples gathered around him, and he rose and entered the city. And on the second day he went out from there with Barnabas, and they came to the city of Derbe. 21 And when they had taught the people of that city and had gained many disciples, they returned to the city of Lystra, and to Iconium, and to the city of Antioch, 22 and they were strengthening the believers <note>original: "ומאמינים הם"; the sentence breaks off at the page end and continues on the next page</note>

<note>Catchword at the foot of the page: "in themselves" (original: "בעצמם"), the first word of the next page.</note>

<summary>The people of Lystra try to sacrifice to Paul and Barnabas, who tear their clothes and urge the crowd to turn to the living God, maker of heaven and earth. Jews from Iconium and Antioch then turn the people against them; Paul is stoned and left for dead, but rises and travels with Barnabas to Derbe and back through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.</summary>
<keywords>Acts 14, Paul, Barnabas, Lystra, Derbe, Iconium, Antioch, sacrifice, priest of Zeus, living God, creation, rain and fruitful seasons, stoning of Paul, disciples, Hebrew New Testament, Gaster manuscript</keywords>

For I had already seen the kingdoms, which are a hint to the kingdoms. And if so, what are "these" to live? [It is] a matter of living with them.

"And the angel answered and said to me, 'These are four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. In which the black horses are going out to the north country, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the south country. And the strong ones went out and sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth, and he said, "Go, walk to and fro in the earth," and they walked to and fro in the earth. And he cried out to me, and spoke to me, saying, "See, those going out to the north country have set my spirit to rest in the north country."' "

"And he answered": These are four spirits of the heavens, like [the verse] "to his spirits." And so [it is written] "and he came to Jerusalem," like "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: to the [one] son of black, like "to the white, black," and those similar to it. To the division of the four chariots and they go out to the four spirits of the heavens, all to give authority to the four kingdoms to rule in the four spirits, each one in its time, all in the entire world, which is mentioned [as] strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth": Meaning in the mission of God, that he gave them authority over this, like [the verse] "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin> "In which": The black ones. And he mentioned the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, which they were [in] to destroy it, and afterwards they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. And the white ones, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them, for that kingdom [was] clear, for Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he reigned, and afterwards [he] and his successors [ruled] over the entire world. 

"And the dappled ones went out to the south country": These were a part that was holy [in] their passing, for Rome is distinct, and Julius Caesar, who reigned over Rome, will prove it; he began to fight with the kingdom of Greece, and in the beginning of his wars he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southerly, and in all the lands the sons of Greece were reigning. And Julius Caesar overcame them and it is mentioned [that] he transferred the kingdom from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans. "And the strong ones": They are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael, who were ready by themselves to seek a kingdom to live [in] a place, for that [is] why he gave them a spirit. And this is what he said, "And they sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth." "And he said": Meaning he gave them permission to walk to and fro and to conquer lands. "And he cried out": Meaning he called to me with a loud voice and said to me, "See, those going out to the north country have set my spirit to rest in the north country," meaning the part of the black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>The text explains the vision of the four spirits/winds of heaven as authorities granted to the four kingdoms to act according to God's mission. It details the movements of these kingdoms (Babylon, Greece, Rome, and Ishmael) and their roles in history, concluding with the rest of the spirit in the north country.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four spirits, Babylon, Media and Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Alexander of Macedon</keywords>

In which the black horses go out toward the north country, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out toward the south country. And the strong ones went out, and sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth, and he said, 'Go, walk to and fro in the earth.' And they walked to and fro in the earth. Then he cried out to me, and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.'"

**And he answered.** These are the four spirits. Similar to the seven spirits. And likewise "he came to Jerusalem" as if [written] "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: for the seven, a black son as for a white son. And those similar to it. For the seven, the fourth part of the chariots, and they go out to the seven spirits of the heavens. As if to give authority to the seven kingdoms to rule in the seven spirits, each one in its time. As if for everything in the world, that which is the seven of strength. "Standing before the Lord of all the earth." As if in the mission of God, that He granted them power over this. Like "the sons of God came to stand before the Lord" <margin>Job 2</margin>. **In which.** The black ones. And he mentioned the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, which were in everything to destroy it, and after that they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. And the white ones, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them, for the kingdom is <unclear>broken</unclear>. That Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him and reigned, and after that [the] <term>Kuz</term> <gloss>unknown term</gloss> and <term>Kakhis</term> <gloss>unknown term</gloss> after him in all the world. **And the dappled ones went out toward the south country.** Which were a holy part, as it passed, for Rome is <unclear>different</unclear>, and Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece. And at the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern, and in all the lands the sons of Greece were reigning. And Caesar prevailed over them, and he transferred the kingdom from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans. **And the strong ones.** They are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael, which mustered itself to seek a kingdom to be a place that would be for <unclear>tranquility</unclear> for them, a spirit for them. And this is what he said, "And they sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth." **And he said.** Meaning, he gave them permission to walk to and fro and to conquer lands. **Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me, "**See, those that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country**," meaning the portion of the black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

found that the kingdoms already seen were a hint to the seven kingdoms <note>likely referring to historical stages of the four major empires</note>. And so, "What are these, my lord?" is an inquiry into the nature of my life within them.

### Zechariah 6

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses goes out to the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out to the south country. And the strong went out and sought to go, to walk about the earth; and he said, 'Go, walk about the earth.' So they walked about the earth. Then he called out to me and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those who go out to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.'"

**And he answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like "to the four winds." Similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" means "to Jerusalem." Alternatively, "a white son of a black" <note>an idiomatic or grammatical comparison</note> is like "to a white son of black," and others like it. He divided the four chariots as going out to the four winds of the heavens. This was to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time. This refers to the whole world, as the language implies strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth": this means by the mission of God who gave them dominion over this, just as it is written <margin>Job 2</margin> "and the sons of God came to stand before the Lord."

**The one in which.** "The black." He mentioned the black ones because the time of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the north country, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white," which is the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them," for that kingdom was swift as lightning. Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he reigned, and after him his successors ruled throughout the whole world.

**And the dappled went out to the south country.** These were the portion of the Romans, for Rome is in the north, and Augustus <note>originally: "Yoichum" or "Ochus" Caesar, likely a corruption of Augustus or a general term for the Caesars</note> Caesar, who ruled over Rome, began to fight the kingdom of Greece. In the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks were ruling in all lands, but Augustus Caesar prevailed over them, and he transferred the kingdom from the Greeks and returned it to the Romans.

**And the strong.** These are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>the Arab/Islamic Caliphate</note> who strengthened themselves of their own accord to seek a kingdom, to find a place that would be for their spirit. This is why it says, "and they sought to go, to walk about the earth."

**And he said.** Meaning, He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**Then he called out.** Meaning, He called to me with a great voice and said to me, "See, those who go out to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country," meaning the portion of the black horses who went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>The text explains Zechariah's vision of the four chariots as the four world empires: Media-Persia, Greece, Rome, and Ishmael. It provides historical context for their conquests, including Alexander the Great's defeat of Darius and the rise of the Roman and Islamic powers.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four winds, Media, Persia, Alexander of Macedon, Greece, Rome, Augustus Caesar, Ishmael, Babylon</keywords>

text:
<page-num>21</page-num>
<header>Zechariah</header>

For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are a hint at the seven kingdoms. And so, what are these things? It is a matter of the living beings, to be revived by them.

And the angel answered and said to me, These are the four winds of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The black horses therein go forth into the north country; and the white go forth after them; and the grizzled go forth toward the south country. And the bay went forth, and sought to go that they might walk to and fro through the earth: and he said, Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth. Then cried he unto me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.

**And he answered.** These are the four winds. Just as there are seven spirits. And likewise, "and he came to Jerusalem" is like "to Jerusalem." Another interpretation: "to the seven" <note>This refers to the frequent use of the preposition "lamed" (to/for) which the commentator here suggests functions as a prefix indicating direction or attribution to the seven kingdoms.</note> is like "to the black," or "the black." And similar to it, to the seven, he divided the four chariots, and they go forth to the seven winds of the heavens. To give permission to the seven kingdoms to rule over the seven winds, each in its time. Throughout the entire world which has seven strengths. **Standing before the Lord of all the earth.** As in, by the mission of God, who gave them power over this. As it is written, "and the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin> **Wherein.** The black ones. And he mentioned the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, as they were there to destroy it, and afterwards they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. **And the white ones,** which are the kingdom of Greece, went forth after them, for the kingdom is speckled. For Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him and reigned, and afterwards [the kings] after him [reigned] over the whole world. **And the grizzled went forth toward the south country.** These were a holy portion <note>Referring to the Roman power which succeeded the Greeks.</note>, for Rome is different, and Julius Caesar, who ruled over Rome, began to war against the kingdom of Greece. At the beginning of his wars, he went to the land of Egypt, which is southerly, and the sons of Greece were ruling in all those lands. And Julius Caesar prevailed over them, and he removed the kingdom from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans. **And the bay.** They are a hint at the kingdom of Ishmael, who bestirred themselves to seek a kingdom, to live in a place that would be for them a spirit of power. And this is what is said, "and they sought to go that they might walk to and fro through the earth." **And he said.** Meaning, he gave them permission to walk to and fro and to conquer lands. **And he cried.** Meaning, he called out to me with a loud voice and said to me, **"Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."** Meaning, the portion of the black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>This page contains a commentary on the sixth chapter of the Book of Zechariah, interpreting the four chariots as symbolic representations of historical kingdoms, including Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and the rise of Ishmael.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, Four Winds, Babylon, Media and Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Alexander of Macedon, Julius Caesar</keywords>

<meta>Continues the commentary from the previous page (Zechariah 6). The commentary appears to be that of David Kimhi (Radak). The OCR of the small commentary type is badly garbled in places: the abbreviation printed as לז' / כלז' evidently stands for "meaning / that is to say", and the numeral printed as ז' is read here as ד' (four) where the sense requires it. ->**Zechariah**<-

for I have already seen the kingdoms, that they are a hint to the four kingdoms. And if so, "what are these", <unclear>לחיות ענין לחיותי בהם</unclear>:

And the angel answered and said to me: "These are the four winds of heaven, going forth from presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes out to the land of the north; and the white ones went out after them; and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south. And the strong ones went out, and they sought to go and walk about through the earth. And he said, 'Go, walk about through the earth.' And they walked about through the earth." Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying: "See, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."

**"And he answered."** "These are the four winds": this is like "to the four winds". In the same way, "and he came Jerusalem" <margin>2 Samuel 10</margin> is like "to Jerusalem". <unclear>ד"א לז' בן שחור כמו לבן שחור</unclear>, and others like it. The meaning is that the four chariots go out to the four winds of heaven, that is to say, to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time: that is, over the whole world, which has four corners. **"From presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth"**: that is, on the mission of God, who sent them for this purpose, as it says, "and the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**"The one with."** The black ones. He did not mention the red ones <note>the OCR prints "the black ones" here, but the sense requires the red horses of the first chariot</note>, because the matter of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the land of the north, which is Babylon, to destroy it, and afterwards they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. **"And the white ones"**, which is the kingdom of Greece, **"went out after them"**, for the kingship was transferred <unclear>נברק</unclear>. For Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingship from him and reigned; and afterwards he and those who came after him ruled over the whole world.

**"And the dappled ones went out to the land of the south."** <unclear>שהיו חלק קדוס כעבור</unclear> for Rome is northern <note>the OCR prints an unreadable word here; "northern" is the likely reading, set against Egypt as "southern" below</note>. Julius Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to wage war against the kingdom of Greece, and at the start of his wars he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern. In all those lands the Greeks were then ruling. Julius Caesar prevailed over them, and he it was who removed the kingship from the Greeks and returned it to the Romans.

**"And the strong ones."** <note>Hebrew: <term>amutzim</term> <gloss>strong ones</gloss></note> These are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>the Arab, Islamic empire</note>, who exerted themselves of their own accord to seek kingship <unclear>לחיות מקום שיהיה לשיכך לז' קתר להם רוח</unclear>. This is what it says: "and they sought to go and walk about through the earth."

**"And he said."** That is, he gave them permission to walk about and to conquer lands.

**"And he cried out."** That is, he called to me in a loud voice and said to me: **"See, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north"**, that is, the portion of the black ones, who went out to Babylon to destroy it

<summary>This page gives the Hebrew text of Zechariah 6:5-8, in which the angel explains the four chariots as the four winds of heaven, together with a commentary reading each group of horses as a world empire. The black horses are Media and Persia destroying Babylon, the white are Greece under Alexander, the dappled are Rome under Julius Caesar, and the strong ones are the kingdom of Ishmael.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah 6, four chariots, four winds of heaven, four kingdoms, Babylon, Media and Persia, Darius, Greece, Alexander of Macedon, Rome, Julius Caesar, Egypt, kingdom of Ishmael, land of the north, Job 2, 2 Samuel 10, Radak, Robert Estienne</keywords>

And when Zakufael, the Prince of the Lord <note>original: "יי' השר"</note>, sees <term>Zakufael</term> <gloss>the prince charged with recording the merits of Israel</gloss>, the Prince of the Lord who is appointed to write the merits of Israel that are performed before the Throne of Glory, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And when Zakfiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord who guards the keys of the palaces of the Arabot firmament, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Anafiel? Because the branch <note>original: "ענף"</note> of his splendor, his majesty, his crown, his radiance, and his brilliance covers all the splendors of the highest Arabot firmament like the Creator of the world. Just as of the Supreme Creator it is written, "His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise," so too does Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord, cover with his splendor and his majesty all the splendors of the highest Arabot. And when Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Kotertashiel, the great, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Kotertashiel? Because he is appointed in purity over the four heads of the River of Fire <note>original: "נהר נור"</note> that is before the Throne of Glory. And every single prince who goes out and enters before the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss> does not go out or enter except by his authority, for the boundaries of the four heads of the River of Fire are entrusted to his hand. And not only that, but the majority of his height is seventy thousand myriads of <term>parsaot</term> <gloss>leagues/parasangs</gloss>, and he is the crown-prince <note>original: "כותרתשי"</note> of the River of Fire, and he goes out and enters before the <term>Shekhinah</term> to interpret the merits of all who enter the world, as it is written: "The court sat in judgment, and the books were opened." And when Kotertashiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Shaqed-Hazyah, the great, mighty, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Shaqed-Hazyah? Because he weighs all merits on a pair of scales before the Holy One, blessed be He. And when Shaqed-Hazyah, the Prince of the Lord, sees Zephanuri, the great, mighty, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, and the splendor revered by all the heavenly host, he removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is his name called Zephanuri? Because he breathes into him in purity...

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
A portion in which the Name **YHWH Elohim** <note>a combination of the Name of Mercy and the Name of Judgment</note> is mentioned implies that those actions are performed with all the qualities <note>Sefirot</note> completed through the Attribute of Judgment <term>Din</term> and the Attribute of Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. You find this, for instance, in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion <note>from Eden</note>, along with all those related matters. You will find that all of them occurred through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy, all in complete perfection, with mercy and judgment balanced as is fitting for a judgment of truth. According to this principle, the Torah states: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is this: The Rock <note>Tzur</note>, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty; He does not decree judgment until His work is "perfect" <term>Tamim</term>. Rather, the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes, Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term> and Judgment <term>Din</term>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect." For the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> contains the secret of two things; it is as if it said "twins" <term>Teumim</term>, except that in the language of honor used for high matters, it says "perfect" <term>Tamim</term>, while for lower matters it says "twins" <term>Teumim</term>. Thus it says: "And they shall be doubled <term>Teumim</term> below... they shall be coupled <term>Tamim</term> together at the head" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are "twins," above they are "perfect." This is because below they appear as two separate things—opposites, like an advocate and an accuser—but above, everything is a single intention. Whether it is the advocate or the accuser, both have one purpose. There is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, but only a judgment of truth. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," meaning He consulted with both Judgment and Mercy and then decreed the law. This is the secret of the "judgment of truth" <term>Mishpat Emet</term>. 

As for the phrase "for all His ways are justice" <term>Mishpat</term>, the meaning is that everything is visible to the eyes of all who see <note>l</note>, as it says, "for all His ways are justice." You already know that Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. For Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Column, the one who balances between the two "tents" of Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term>; Isaac corresponds to Judgment <term>Din</term>; and Jacob decides between them: "a perfect man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on Abraham's side and from Judgment on Isaac's side. Thus it says: "You have executed justice <term>Mishpat</term> and righteousness <term>Tzedakah</term> in Jacob" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>. And the prophet said: "Correct me, O Lord <term>YHWH</term>, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The meaning of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice <term>Mishpat</term>" is found in the word "but" <term>ach</term> <note>often used in Hebrew to signify a part or a limitation</note>, meaning with only half of the quality of Justice, which is Mercy. For Justice is half judgment and half mercy. Therefore he said "but with justice," and then added "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret to diminish the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger <note>Judgment</note>. 

Therefore, Justice is dependent on Jacob, who is the "father" among the tribes. <warning>Transcription becomes difficult due to the tape mentioned in the OCR warning.</warning> Having known the great pain of children, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees against them, he <note>Jacob</note> seeks mercy and righteousness for them. The secret is: "But the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice <term>Mishpat</term>" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written immediately after? "And the holy God is sanctified through righteousness <term>Tzedakah</term>." This means that when Justice is exalted, the harsh Judgment is eased and turns toward the quality of *El* <note>the Name associated with Mercy</note>. This is the secret of what is said: "And the holy God is sanctified through righteousness." Generally, when the Lord of Hosts is exalted through Justice, the quality of *El*—which is higher—arrives and performs righteousness <note>n</note>, and Justice is refined. This is the secret of their saying that Justice is comprised of Loving-kindness and Judgment, as it says, "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." The great secret is: "Righteousness <term>Tzedek</term> and justice <term>Mishpat</term> are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek</term> is sometimes Judgment, based on what it receives in abundance, as I explained that *Tzedek* is a powerful, strengthened judgment. But when Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is joined with it, then the Throne is established with Mercy. If it is exalted through Justice, and reaches as far as Loving-kindness and Truth together—which are called the "Shining Countenance"—then everything becomes great Mercy. This is the secret of: "shall go before 

->Your face<-"

<meta>Commentary section below the main text</meta>

This hints at "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." They have a single intention, for the ultimate essence is the distribution of Judgment and Loving-kindness according to the recipients prepared for them through awakening. In the Book of Zohar <note>Parashat Balak</note> it is noted that all is the "Ancient of Ancients"... <note>The Rashi script commentary here includes complex Aramaic citations from the Zohar regarding the balance of the Right and Left sides, the "Holy Head," and the "Voice of the Lord."</note> (a) As he says, "for all His ways are justice," Justice is a revealed path... visible to all and not hidden above... (b) And the "Zebul" of Justice, because the quality of Judgment is gathered under the hand of Loving-kindness, as is included in the mystery of the Name *El*.

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic concept of Justice (Mishpat) as a balance between Mercy (Chesed) and Judgment (Din). Using the figure of Jacob as the Middle Column, Gikatilla describes how the Name YHWH Elohim and the concept of "perfection" reflect the harmonization of divine attributes.</summary>
<keywords>Mishpat, Tzedek, Din, Rachamim, Jacob, Abraham, Isaac, Tzur, Tamim, YHWH Elohim, Middle Column, Sefirot, Zohar</keywords>

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>

Since there is no faithfulness in the whole, why do you turn toward every whole?
All reliance is upon you, for you are the pillar and the mainstay.

If they cut their hands <note>an allusion to the women in the story of Joseph who were so captivated by his beauty that they cut their hands while peeling oranges</note> at the sight of Joseph’s face,
You have cut two hundred Josephs of the spirit from heart and intellect.

From impurity and from goodness you form the image of a person,
Who flees two leagues away from the stench of impurity.

Before the earthy food that becomes pure greenery,
It escapes from defilement when you have breathed a soul into it.

Come, O heart, go to the heavens, go to the pasture of God;
You have grazed enough in the pasture of beasts.

Place all your desire upon that for which there is no hope,
For it was from that first despair that you reached this side.

Be silent, so that the Lord who grants speech may speak,
For He is the one who made the door and the lock, and He is the one who made the key.

<margin>
8 (V) palm/hand and intellect
11 (V) you grazed for a while
13 . (V) lock omitted before
</margin>

<summary>This poem explores the futility of worldly attachments and encourages the soul to transcend physical needs, finding ultimate fulfillment only in the Divine who holds the key to spiritual liberation.</summary>
<keywords>faithfulness, Joseph, spirit, impurity, pasture, desire, despair, silence, Divine</keywords>

چو وَفا نبوَد در كُل چه رَوی تو سوی هر كُل
همه بر تُست تَوَكُّل كه عِمادی و عمیدی

اگر از چهرۀ يوسف نَفَری كف ببريدند
تو دو صد يوسفِ جانرا ز دل و عقل بُريدی

ز پليدی و ز خوبی تو كُنی صورتِ شخـ
كه كُريزد بدو فرسنگ وَی از بوی پليدی

پيشِ طعمه خاكی كه شَوَد سبزۀ پاكی
برَهَد او ز نجاست چو درو روح دميدی

هله ای دل بسما رَو بچراگاهِ خُدا رَو
بچراگاهِ سُتوران چو يکی چند چريدی

تو همه طمع بر آن نِه كه بر آن نيست اُميدت
كه ز نَوميدیِ اوّل تو بدين سوی رسيدی

تو خَمُش كُن كه خُداوندِ سُخُن‌بخش بگويد
كه هم او ساخت در و قُفل و هم او كرد كليدی
