<meta>continues from previous page</meta> as it is written, "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 484: Not to shear the firstborn <term>bechor</term>, and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said, "You shall not shear the firstborn [of your sheep]" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 485: Not to eat leaven <term>chametz</term> on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said, "You shall not eat leaven with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, meaning during the time of the slaughtering of the Passover sacrifice, whose time is after midday. 486: Not to leave over the meat of the fourteenth day's festival sacrifice <term>chagigah</term> until the third day, as it is said, "And none of the meat... shall remain [until morning]" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. 487: Not to offer the Passover sacrifice on a private altar <term>bamah</term>, as it is said, "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>. 488: The commandment of rejoicing on the festivals, as it is said, "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. 489: The commandment of appearing <term>re'iyah</term>, that every male appear three times a year. 490: That we should not ascend to the Chosen House <note>The Temple in Jerusalem</note> on a festival without a sacrifice, as it is said, "And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### **Torah** Light <note>Hebrew: Torah Or</note> 
These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service <term>Avodah</term>, and Deeds of Loving-kindness <term>Gemilut Hasadim</term>. 

Torah consists of the commands "Do not add" and "Do not subtract," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is perfect in the ultimate sense cannot be said to be lacking nor can it be increased. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could receive addition, it would mean it was not previously perfect. Therefore, the definition of "perfect" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is dependent upon His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>, for "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my work on Tractate Shevuot in the chapter "Torah Or." As stated in the Zohar on the verse "This is My Name and this is My Memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Yod-Heh</term> with "My Name" <note>Hebrew: Shemi</note> equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>Vav-Heh</term> with "My Memorial" <note>Hebrew: Zichri</note> equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. It is also written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>, and He is the absolute Perfection in whom there is no subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning, "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which is a warning against erasing the Name or breaking a stone from the Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the House in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; so too is the Sanctuary. It is written, "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like a frame for the House, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul within them. One who destroys His House, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." 

Divine Service <term>Avodah</term> comprises most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place, in the Chosen House, and the reason was given: "to His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" <term>leshichno</term> hints at the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh</term>. Do not fear that she will dwell elsewhere, for in the Sanctuary, the Glory <note>Tiferet</note> is united with the Divine Presence among His people. This is the meaning of "to place His Name there," which the Targum renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Surrounding the place of holiness, the wicked walk—these are the "Husks" <term>Kelipot</term> <note>Forces of impurity</note>. Therefore, "Guard yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** 
Sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written of them, "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an ascent <term>aliyah</term> and not outside. Since the holiness resides in the Chosen House which is in the Holy Land, we were commanded to "turn from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations served their gods. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this relates to the ten nations who, though they are not idolaters <unclear>in essence</unclear>, when nations in the Land of Israel—which is under the direct providence of the Honorable Name—serve God through "cutting the plantings" <note>A term for heresy or spiritual sabotage</note>, this is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the rule of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking even one stone of holiness, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a Subverted City <term>Ir HaNidachat</term> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Similarly, the enticer <term>mesit</term> and the subverter <term>madiach</term> must be uprooted and eradicated, for he comes from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was the first enticer. The Holy One immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of <term>Samael</term> <note>The personification of evil/Satan</note> are never cured. The command came not to love him nor listen to him, as was said regarding the serpent, "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is also like an enticer. 

Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <term>Bikkurim</term>, which the priests are not permitted to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness as I have written elsewhere; therefore they must go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they eat in Jerusalem. This is the secret of the "lighter" holy offerings <term>Kodashim Kalim</term> and the Second Tithe, whose consumption is in Jerusalem. This is the "blessing of grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary sources of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat the lighter holy offerings until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul, and afterward comes the permission to enjoy and derive benefit. Know that just as the service—the sacrifice—is an offering to God, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the service is that a person offers himself, in the secret of the verse, "When a man of you <note>literally 'from you'</note> brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering <term>olah</term> is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for the thoughts of the heart <term>hirhur ha-lev</term> which are spiritual; it is burned all night so the serpent does not hinder it. The lighter holy offerings represent the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The Secret** 
Of the firstborn is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "the firstborn of Israel." He has compassion on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, the firstborn animal is eaten only by the priests. The secret of eating sacrifices that have blemishes <term>mumim</term> <note>rendered profane</note> is that Israel is holy and called "Man" <term>Adam</term>. He was a holy creature, but afterward a blemish fell upon him when he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption through the secret of "I will give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the Scapegoat <term>Azazel</term> that "bore their iniquities," meaning the iniquities that rested upon his head and his people. However, we were commanded not to intentionally cause a blemish in a sacrifice in order to eat it. For if one casts a blemish in the holy offerings by his own choice, it is a grave sin. Likewise, there is a prohibition against working or shearing the holy animals, for even the broken Tablets of the Covenant remain holy.

The general principle is: the Service is the sacrifice; however, the inner sacrifice is the Man himself. Likewise, his soul is called to the Altar on High after death, and Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret that man was made in the image of God. Therefore, the warning was given to be careful during one's life regarding "damages to souls," not to kill a man except after great inquiry and investigation. Only then is it "death by the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the Witness, He is the Judge," for the Lord, may He be blessed, is the True Witness and the True Judge. So too must the Sanhedrin be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that they must clarify the truth of the testimony with complete clarity, through inquiry and investigation. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and the death of his <unclear>saints</unclear> is precious in the eyes of the Lord.

### **Since** 
The death of his [pious ones] is precious in the eyes of the Lord, because Israel is holy from the side of their soul—for after their death, the souls cling to the heights—therefore the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness [between your eyes for the dead]" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>, for "you are children to the Lord your God." This is not the case for the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, and rightly so, since upon their death they go to perdition and have no portion in this world or the world to come. We, however, are children of God. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we instead have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

Let us return to the matter: the man who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it says, "When a man of you brings an offering." There is a further secret here: that sometimes a soul is "reincarnated" <term>gilgul</term> even below the level of man, in the secret of "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding the eating of non-sacred meat <term>basar ta'ava</term>, we were commanded in the laws of slaughter <term>shechitah</term> with great care to avoid any "nick" in the blade. For if there is a nick, the animal becomes a carcass <term>nevilah</term>, and "a disgrace is done in Israel," for who knows what soul might be reincarnated within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" implies choosing a "beautiful death" for it—that is, slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and if there is a spark of holiness in the animal or pure bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **Eating** 
A limb from a living animal <term>ever min ha-chai</term> is like eating the flesh of a person when there is a reincarnated soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Similarly, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the spark spread within them—whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" <term>Sitra Achra</term> or the "Side of Holiness." I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them, "And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell within them," for they themselves are the Tabernacle. For man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart corresponds to the Holy Place; and from the belly downward corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods that are from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now, a man's table atones for him," as I have explained in its place.

### **The Matter** 
Of the commandments of the Festivals and their sacrifices, I have written each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to ascend for the pilgrimage: "Three times a year shall all your males appear." One should not say that just as he comes to see, he comes to be seen; therefore, if he wishes to be seen in the Sanctuary where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden to behold the face of the wicked; how then could he wish to appear before the Blessed One and bring a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself is a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. It says "Three times a year he shall appear"—this refers to Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering."

<summary>This page analyzes the laws of firstborn animals, sacrifices, and festivals in Parashat Re'eh through a mystical lens. It explains that man himself is the "inner sacrifice" and that the laws of kosher slaughter and mourning reflect the eternal nature of the Jewish soul and its potential for reincarnation.</summary>
<keywords>Bechor, Shekhinah, Temple, Reincarnation, Gilgul, Shechitah, Festivals, Sacrifice, Soul, Purity</keywords>

as it is said, "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox." <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note> **484.** The prohibition against shearing a firstborn animal; the same applies to other sanctified animals, as it is said, "And you shall not shear the firstborn of your ox, etc." **485.** The prohibition against eating leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said, "You shall not eat leaven with it," <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note> meaning at the time of the slaughter of the Passover offering, the time for which is after midday. **486.** The prohibition against leaving any meat from the Passover offering of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said, "Neither shall any of the meat... remain all night." <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note> **487.** The prohibition against offering the Passover sacrifice in a private high place, as it is said, "You may not slaughter the Passover offering within any of your gates." <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note> **488.** The commandment to rejoice during the festivals, as it is said, "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God." <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note> **489.** The commandment of appearance—every male three times a year. <note>Exodus 23:17</note> **490.** The prohibition against ascending to the Chosen House <note>The Temple in Jerusalem</note> on a festival without an offering, as it is said, "And they shall not appear before Me empty-handed." <note>Exodus 23:15</note>

### **The Light of Torah**
These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Worship, and Acts of Loving-kindness. Torah represents the commandment "You shall not add to it nor take away from it," <note>Deuteronomy 13:1</note> which points to the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers say: a thing that is perfect in ultimate perfection cannot have anything added to it or taken away from it. For if it were lacking, it would not be perfect; and if it were capable of increase, it would not have been perfect to begin with. Therefore, the definition of the perfect is that which has neither deficit nor surplus. It is known that the Torah depends on His great Name, which is the Tetragrammaton <note><term>YHVH</term> <gloss>The unpronounced four-letter Name of God</gloss></note>, as it is written, "The law of the Lord is perfect," <note>Psalm 19:8</note> as I have elaborated upon this in my *Tractate Shevuot*, in the chapter "The Light of Torah." And as it is written in the *Zohar* regarding the verse, "This is My Name and this is My remembrance" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: *Y-H* with "My Name" equals 360, and *V-H* with "My remembrance" equals 248. It is written, "I am the first and I am the last." <note>Isaiah 44:6</note> This is the Absolute Perfect, containing no diminution or addition. Regarding this, the warning was given: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note> This is a warning against erasing the Name or destroying a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are the house in which He (blessed be He) dwells, and likewise the Temple. It is written, "I am the Lord, My Name is the Eternal One; I am One and My Name is One." The letters are like the body for the house, and His Name (blessed be He) is the soul within them. He who destroys His house, so to speak, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." Worship constitutes the majority of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The commandment was given for there to be a permanent place, specifically in the Chosen House, and a reason was provided: "To His habitation you shall seek, and you shall come there." <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note> "To His habitation" alludes to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the name <term>YHVH</term> <gloss>The Tetragrammaton</gloss>, as it is written, "And the Lord is in His holy temple," <note>Habakkuk 2:20</note> which is the secret of the Name <term>Adonai</term> <gloss>Lord</gloss>, which is the <term>Shekhinah</term>. For in the Temple, the Glory is unified in the splendor of His power, and this is "to place His Name there," which is translated as "to cause His <term>Shekhinah</term> to dwell." Around the place of holiness, the wicked walk, for they are the <term>Kelipah</term> <gloss>Shells/forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore, "Take heed to yourself, lest you offer your burnt offerings in any place that you see." <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>

### **And sometimes** 
sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to occupy oneself with bringing the sacrifice from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch is returned to its root, and it is written regarding them, "There you shall offer," <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note> meaning there they shall have their elevation and not outside. Since the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, is where holiness resides, we were commanded to be "turn from evil" and destroy all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate after them; this is commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The Sages of blessed memory alluded to this secret: "Nations outside the land are not idolaters." <note>Talmud, Chullin 13b; meaning their worship is not an act of rebellion against the specific sanctity of the Land of Israel.</note> The matter is that the nations who are in the Land of Israel, under the rule of the honored Name, worship God while "cutting the shoots" <note>An allusion to heresy or blasphemy against the divine unity.</note>, and this is true idolatry. However, those outside the Land are under the rule of external powers. Just as there is a great prohibition against tearing down one stone of the holy place, so too, conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eradicate an apostate city, and not to rebuild it again, for its place is defiled. Likewise, one who entices others to worship idols must be uprooted and eradicated, for he is from the impurity of the primordial serpent that was a tempter, and the Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent." <note>Genesis 3:14</note> Therefore, one does not argue in favor of the enticer. The command was given not to love him but to hate him, as is stated regarding the serpent, "And I will put enmity between you and the woman." <note>Genesis 3:15</note> Also, a false prophet is like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits, which the priests have no authority to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the First Fruits, which are the "Beginning," point to great holiness, as I have written elsewhere. Therefore, they shall go to the holy place, and from there the priests, who are holy to their God, shall take them and eat them in Jerusalem. The secret of the "lesser holy things" <note><term>Kodashim Kallim</term> <gloss>Offerings of lesser sanctity, such as peace offerings</gloss></note> and the Second Tithe is that their consumption is in Jerusalem. This is like the grain, the wine, and the oil, which are the ancestors of all food. It is forbidden to eat the lesser holy things until after the tossing of their blood, for the blood is the soul. Afterward, the body is permitted for enjoyment. Know that just as worship—which is the sacrifice—is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshipper; for the essence of the worship is that he offers himself, in the secret of "When any man from among you brings an offering," <note>Leviticus 1:2</note> and the burnt offering is wholly consumed, for it comes because of stray thoughts—the secret of the mind, which is spiritual—and "it shall burn on it all the night," <note>Leviticus 6:2</note> for "he schemes iniquity upon his bed." <note>Psalm 36:5</note> The lesser holy things correspond to the perfection of the soul and the body.

### **And the secret** 
of the unblemished firstborn is the secret of the holy people of Israel, who are called "My firstborn son is Israel." <note>Exodus 4:22</note> They are the "perfect congregation" and are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, it is only eaten by the priests. The secret of eating the holy things when they have acquired a blemish and were redeemed is because the holy people of Israel are called "Man," and he was holy. Afterward, a blemish fell upon him after he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption in the secret of "And I will give a man in your stead." <note>Isaiah 43:4</note> This was the secret of <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>The scapegoat</gloss>, "and he shall bear their iniquities," and our Sages of blessed memory said: "the iniquities of the perfect, which rest upon his head and upon his people." But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in the holy things in order to eat them, for then one is casting a blemish into the holy things by his own choice. Likewise, there is a prohibition against labor and shearing with holy things, for even the broken tablets are holy.

### **The summary** 
of what has been stated: worship is the sacrifice, but the inner sacrifice is the person. So too, his soul is offered after his death upon the altar above, and Michael is the High Priest. Everything is the secret of "In the image of God was man created." Therefore, a great warning is given to be careful regarding the laws of life and death, not to kill a person except after thorough investigation and examination. Then he dies by the hand of Heaven, in the secret of "He is the witness and He is the Judge," for the Holy One (blessed be He) is a true witness and a true judge. Likewise, the Sanhedrin must be such; just as they are true judges, they must be true witnesses—meaning that the truth of the testimony must be clarified for them with absolute certainty, which is the investigation and examination. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His saints]." <note>Psalm 116:15</note>

### **And since** 
it is precious in the eyes of the Lord, because the people of Israel are holy by virtue of their souls, which after their death adhere to the heights above, therefore the commandment was given: "You shall not cut yourselves, you shall not make any baldness," <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> etc., "for you are children to the Lord your God." <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> This is not the case for the nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, for it is appropriate, since in their death they go to destruction, and they have no portion in this world or the next. It is not so with us; we are children of the Lord. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, on the contrary, we have a permanent dwelling above with our Father in heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to overdo mourning and to perform these acts.

### **Let us return** 
to the matter: the person who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it is written, "When any man from among you brings an offering." And there is a further secret in this: it happens that a person is sacrificed even below, in the secret of reincarnation—"Man and beast You save, O Lord." <note>Psalm 36:7</note> Therefore, even in the eating of ordinary food, the meat of desire, we were commanded regarding ritual slaughter and a great warning against any defect, for then it is an animal that died of itself, and it becomes a carcass among Israel. For who knows what reincarnation is in it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>—choose for him a beautiful death, meaning slaughter without defect. And if the animal dies by itself, then the power of impurity spreads and takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it while it is healthy, and there is in the animal, wild beast, or clean bird a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **And one who eats** 
a limb from a living animal is like one who eats from the flesh of his brother when there is a reincarnation of a soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh." <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note> Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of clean animals, beasts, and birds—all point to the spark that spreads within them: whether it is from the side of impurity or from the side of holiness. I have elaborated on this in the portion of *Shemini*. When Israel conducts themselves in holiness, it is written of them, "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them," <note>Exodus 25:8</note> for they themselves are the Tabernacle. For so is man in his three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Sanctuary, and from the stomach downwards corresponds to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in the portion of *Terumah*. When one eats food that is from the side of holiness, then they are like an offering sacrificed upon the altar. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Now a person's table atones," <note>Talmud, Berakhot 55a</note> as I have elaborated in its place.

### **And the matter** 
of the commandments of the festivals and their offerings, I have written about each in its own special place. The commandment was given to rejoice on the festivals and to make the pilgrimage—"Three times a year shall all your males appear." <note>Exodus 23:17</note> Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Just as one comes to see, so one comes to be seen." Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Holy Temple, where the Glory dwells, one must turn from evil and do good and be a faithful servant to his Creator. For if not for this, it is forbidden to look at a wicked person, and how much more so would one wish to be seen before Him (blessed be He)? He brings a burnt offering of appearance, and then he himself is a sacrifice through the offering that he brings. It is said, "Three times a year shall he be seen"—Isaac, who was a perfect burnt offering.

<summary>This page details the laws concerning the firstborn, festival observances, and the sacrificial system, while linking these physical rituals to the spiritual perfection of the soul and the concept of reincarnation.</summary>
<keywords>Firstborn, Passover, Holiness, Temple, Sacrifices, Shekhinah, Reincarnation, Worship, Festivals, Pilgrimage</keywords>

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
As it is said: "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 

484. The prohibition against shearing a firstborn animal, and the same applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: "And you shall not shear the firstborn of your sheep" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 
485. The prohibition against eating leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: "You shall not eat leavened bread with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, meaning during the time of the Passover sacrifice, whose time is after midday. 
486. The prohibition against leaving any of the festive sacrifice of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said: "None of the meat... shall remain" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. 
487. The prohibition against offering the Passover sacrifice on a private altar <note>Hebrew: bamah</note>, as it is said: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>. 
488. The commandment to rejoice on the festivals, as it is said: "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. 
489. The commandment of appearing <note>Hebrew: Re'iyah</note> for every male three times a year. 
490. The prohibition against ascending to the Chosen House <note>The Temple</note> on a festival without a sacrifice, as it is said: "And they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### **Torah** is light. These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Service <note>Hebrew: Avodah</note>, and Acts of Loving-kindness <note>Hebrew: Gemilut Chasadim</note>. 

Torah is represented by the commands "Do not add" and "Do not subtract," which point to the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is absolutely perfect cannot be subject to lack or excess. For if it lacked something, it would not be perfect; and if it could receive an addition, it would mean it was previously incomplete. Therefore, the definition of "perfect" is that which has neither lack nor excess. It is known that the Torah is suspended upon His Great Name, which is <term>Y-H-V-H</term>, as it is said: "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my work on Tractate Shavuot, in the chapter "Torah Or." 

As it is written in the Zohar regarding the verse "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Y-H</term> combined with "My name" <note>Hebrew: Shemi</note> equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>. The letters <term>V-H</term> combined with "My memorial" <note>Hebrew: Zichri</note> equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. And it is written: "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>. He is the Absolute Perfection, containing no subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>. This is a warning against erasing the Name or tearing down a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are the "House" in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; so too is the Sanctuary. It is written: "I am the Lord, that is My name." The Holy One is One and His Name is One. The letters are like a body to the House, and His Name is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." 

Service <note>Avodah</note> refers to the majority of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a specifically fixed place in the Chosen House <note>The Temple</note>, and the text provides the reason: "To His habitation you shall seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "His habitation" hints at the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term>, as it is said: "The Lord is in His holy palace" <note>Habakkuk 2:20</note>. This is the secret of the Name <term>Adonai</term>, which is the <term>Shekhinah</term>, for in the Sanctuary, the Glory is united with His "Tiferet of Strength." This is the meaning of "to put His Name there," which the Targum translates as "to rest His Presence." And "around the place of holiness the wicked walk"—referring to the <term>Kelipot</term> <gloss>Husks/Forces of Evil</gloss>. Therefore: "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. 

This is the secret of the commandment to occupy oneself with bringing the sacrifice from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the "branch" is returned to its "root." Regarding them it is written: "There you shall ascend" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an elevation <note>Hebrew: Aliyah</note> and not outside. Since holiness resides in the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, we are commanded to "turn from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate them. This was specifically commanded in the Holy Land. Our Sages of blessed memory hinted at this secret: "Gentiles outside the Land are not true idolaters." The matter is this: Gentiles in the Land of Israel, who are under the dominion of the Honorable Name, worship God by "cutting the plantings" <note>A metaphor for heresy/dualism</note>, and this is true idolatry. However, those outside the Land are under the dominion of external forces. 

Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking even one stone from the holiness, so conversely it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a Subverted City <note>Hebrew: Ir HaNidachat</note> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Similarly, one must uproot and eradicate the Enticer <note>Hebrew: Mesit</note>, for he stems from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said: "Cursed is the serpent," therefore we do not seek merit for an enticer. The command came not to love him but to hate him, as said regarding the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman." A false prophet is also like an enticer. 

Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <note>Bikurim</note>, which the priests are not permitted to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the First Fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness, as I have written elsewhere. Therefore, they must go to the holy place, and from there the priests—who are holy to their God—shall take them and eat them in Jerusalem. The secret of "Lesser Sanctity" offerings <note>Kodashim Kalim</note> and the Second Tithe <note>Ma'aser Sheni</note> is that they are eaten in Jerusalem. This is like the "grain, wine, and oil," which are the archetypal ancestors of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat Lesser Sanctity offerings until after the sprinkling of their blood. For the blood is the soul <note>Nefesh</note>, and only afterward is the body permitted for enjoyment. 

Know that just as the Service—which is the sacrifice—is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshipper. For the essence of the Service is that a person offers himself, following the secret of "When a man <note>Hebrew: Adam</note> brings an offering *from you*" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The Burnt Offering <note>Olah</note> is entirely consumed, for it comes to atone for thoughts—the secret of the mind, which is spiritual. It burns "all night" because "he devises iniquity upon his bed" <note>Psalm 36:5</note>. Lesser Sanctity offerings represent the perfection of both soul and body.

### **The secret** of the unblemished firstborn is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "My firstborn son, Israel." 

They are the <term>Tam</term> <gloss>simple/perfect</gloss>, the complete assembly, called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, it is only eaten by the priests. The secret of eating consecrated animals when they incur a blemish and are redeemed is this: Israel is holy, and Israel is called "Adam." He <note>Adam</note> was originally holy, but afterward a blemish fell upon him after he sinned, and he was clothed in "garments of skin." But he has a redemption, in the secret of "I will give a man <note>Adam</note> in your stead" <note>Isaiah 43:4</note>. This was the secret of <term>Azazel</term>, which "carries their iniquities." Our Sages interpreted this as "the iniquities of the <term>Tam</term> <gloss>perfect one</gloss>" <note>A play on words in Hebrew between "iniquities" (avonot) and "the perfect" (Tam/Jacob)</note>, which fall upon his head and his people. However, we are commanded not to intentionally cause a blemish in consecrated animals in order to eat them. For then, by his own choice, he casts a blemish into the holiness. There is also a prohibition against working or shearing consecrated animals, for even the broken Tablets of the Covenant remain holy.

### **The general principle** of the matter is that the Service is the sacrifice, but the "inner sacrifice" is the human being. 

Likewise, one's soul is offered after death upon the Altar on High, where Michael <note>the Archangel</note> is the High Priest. This is all the secret of "for in the image of God He made man." Therefore, the warning is extremely grave to be careful in capital laws <note>Hebrew: dinei nefashot</note>, not to put a person to death except after thorough investigation and inquiry. Then, his death is by the hand of Heaven, in the secret of "He is the witness, He is the judge." For as the Holy One is a true witness and a true judge, so must the Sanhedrin be. Just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that the truth of the testimony must be clarified with absolute clarity through investigation and inquiry. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His pious ones]" <note>Psalm 116:15</note>.

### **Since** "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death," because Israel is holy from the side of their soul—for after death the souls cleave above—therefore the command came: 

"You shall not cut yourselves, and you shall not make a bald spot... for you are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. This is not the case with the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, and rightly so, since at death they go to destruction and have no portion in this world or the World to Come. We, however, are children of the Lord. When we are absent from this world—which is a temporary dwelling—on the contrary, we then have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter: the person who serves is himself the sacrifice, as it says, "A man who brings an offering *from you*." 

There is a further secret here: sometimes even on the physical level a human is "offered," namely through the secret of <term>Gilgul</term> <gloss>reincarnation</gloss>. "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding the eating of non-sacred meat—meat of desire—we were commanded regarding ritual slaughter <note>Shechitah</note> with a grave warning that there be no "nicking" of the blade. For if so, it becomes a carcass <note>neveilah</note>, and "a disgrace is done in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation <note>gilgul</note> might be within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself"—choose a "beautiful death" for him, meaning slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity spreads and takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it while it is healthy, and there is a spark of holiness in the pure animal, beast, or bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **One who eats** a "limb from a living animal" is like one who eats the flesh of his brother when a reincarnated soul is present. 

This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh." Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all point to the spark spread within them—whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" or the "Side of Holiness." I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "And they shall make for Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell within them." For they themselves are the Tabernacle. A person in his three parts corresponds to the Tabernacle: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart to the Holy Place, and from the belly downward to the Holy Courtyard, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods from the Side of Holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now, a person's table atones for him."

### **The matter** of the commandments of the Festivals and their sacrifices—I have written about each in its specific place. 

The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to ascend for the pilgrimages: "Three times a year all your males shall appear." Our Sages said: "Just as he comes to see, so he comes to be seen." Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Temple, where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. For if not for this, it is forbidden to look at a wicked person; how then could he wish to appear before Him, may He be blessed, bringing a Burnt Offering of Appearance? Then, he himself becomes a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. It says "Three times a year he shall appear"—this refers to Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering"...

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual dimensions of the Temple service, the prohibition against self-mutilation based on the soul's immortality, and the mystical reasons for ritual slaughter (Shechitah) related to the reincarnation of souls (Gilgul) and the elevation of holy sparks.</summary>
<keywords>Sanctuary, Shekhinah, Gilgul, Reincarnation, Shechitah, Dietary Laws, Firstborn, Isaac, Sanhedrin, Holy Sparks, Human Sacrifice, Festivals</keywords>

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
The decree came seventy years prior. And so it says: "And his days shall be one hundred and twenty years" <note>Genesis 6:3</note>. And it says: "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life" <note>Genesis 7:11</note> and so on. Is it possible to say <note>that the decree was given at the birth of the child</note>? Rather, the decree existed one hundred and twenty years before. And so it says: "Within sixty and five years shall Ephraim be broken from being a people" <note>Isaiah 7:8</note>. But you find this was actually in the fourth year of Ahaz. Is it possible to say so? Rather, it was a decree issued since the days of Amos, two years before the earthquake, as it is said: "Thus said Amos: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land" <note>Amos 7:11</note>.

And the seventy <unclear>...</unclear> we counted as a year for the Medes in the scriptures; this one alone was <unclear>...</unclear> because the first part was given over to <unclear>...</unclear> and furthermore one year for the total that Darius stood, and <unclear>...</unclear> that the first was unique to him. Thus far.

---

# Chapter 29

"And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Lord stirred up" <note>Ezra 1:1</note> and so on. "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia" and so on. "Who is there among you of all His people" and so on. "Then rose up the heads of the fathers' houses" and so on. "Forty-two thousand" and so on, "besides their servants" and so on <note>Ezra 2:64</note>. In the general and the specific counts, they were only thirty-one thousand three hundred and sixty; the other twelve thousand are those who went up from the other tribes. "And they set the altar upon its bases" and so on, "and they gave money to the masons" and so on <note>Ezra 3:3-7</note>.

Cyrus reigned three partial years. In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they <note>the enemies of Judah</note> wrote an accusation to stop the work of the House of the Lord. "In the third year of his reign, he made a feast" <note>Esther 1:3</note> and so on. For all of those four years, Esther was hidden in Shushan the capital. "And Esther was taken to the king" <note>Esther 2:16</note> and so on. For all of those five years, Haman was gathering spoil for Mordecai. "In the first month, which is the month of Nisan" <note>Esther 3:7</note> and so on. On the thirteenth of Nisan, Haman wrote the scrolls to destroy, to kill, and so on. On the fifteenth of Nisan, Esther came before the king. On the sixteenth of Nisan, they hanged Haman. On the twenty-third of Sivan, Mordecai wrote scrolls to rescind the scrolls of Haman. On the thirteenth of Adar, the Jews struck all their enemies and so on, and they killed five hundred men in Shushan and hanged the ten sons of Haman, because of the accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. On that day, the number of those killed came before the king. And at that same time the following year, it is said: "Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, wrote" <note>Esther 9:29</note> and so on.

Behold, it says: "For according to the completion of seventy years" <note>Jeremiah 29:10</note> and "to complete the desolations of Jerusalem seventy years" <note>Daniel 9:2</note>. For fifty-two years after the destruction of the Temple, Israel remained under the Kingdom of the Chaldeans <gloss>Babylonians</gloss>, and then they were remembered and went up. There were three years of Cyrus, fourteen of Ahasuerus, and two of Darius. In the second year of Darius, the Temple was built. And so Zechariah said: "Then the angel of the Lord answered and said: O Lord of hosts, [how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem... against which You have had indignation these seventy years?]" <note>Zechariah 1:12</note>.

<summary>This page calculates the timeline of the Persian kings and the return from Babylonian exile, reconciling the reigns of Cyrus, Ahasuerus, and Darius with the prophecy of seventy years and the events of the Book of Esther.</summary>
<keywords>Cyrus, Ahasuerus, Darius, Esther, Haman, Mordecai, seventy years, Second Temple, chronology</keywords>

"And they set the altar upon its bases" and so on, "and they gave money to the masons" and so on <note>Ezra 3:3-7</note>.

Cyrus reigned three partial years. In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they <note>the enemies of Judah</note> wrote an accusation to stop the work of the House of the Lord. "In the third year of his reign, he made a feast" <note>Esther 1:3</note> and so on. For all of those four years, Esther was hidden in Shushan the capital. "And Esther was taken to the king" <note>Esther 2:16</note> and so on. For all of those five years, Haman was gathering spoil for Mordecai. "In the first month, which is the month of Nisan" <note>Esther 3:7</note> and so on. On the second of Nisan, Haman wrote the scrolls to destroy, to kill, and so on. On the fifteenth of Nisan, Esther came before the king. On the sixteenth of Nisan, they hanged Haman. On the twenty-third of Sivan, Mordecai wrote scrolls to rescind the scrolls of Haman. On the thirteenth of Adar, the Jews struck all their enemies and so on, and they killed five hundred men in Shushan and hanged the ten sons of Haman, because of the accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. On that day, the number of those killed came before the king. And at that same time the following year, it is said: "Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, wrote" <note>Esther 9:29</note> and so on.

Behold, it says: "For according to the completion of seventy years" <note>Jeremiah 29:10</note> and "to complete the desolations of Jerusalem seventy years" <note>Daniel 9:2</note>. For fifty-two years after the destruction of the Temple, Israel remained under the Kingdom of the Chaldeans <gloss>Babylonians</gloss>, and then they were remembered and went up. There were three years of Cyrus, fourteen of Ahasuerus, and two of Darius. In the second year of Darius, the Temple was built. And so Zechariah said: "Then the angel of the Lord answered and said: O Lord of hosts, [how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem... against which You have had indignation these seventy years?]" <note>Zechariah 1:12</note>.

<summary>This page calculates the timeline of the Persian kings and the return from Babylonian exile, reconciling the reigns of Cyrus, Ahasuerus, and Darius with the prophecy of seventy years and the events of the Book of Esther.</summary>
<keywords>Cyrus, Ahasuerus, Darius, Esther, Haman, Mordecai, seventy years, Second Temple, chronology</keywords>

# Book of Fear

Be careful regarding the honor of your wife, according to the words of Rabbi <unclear>Yochanan</unclear> <note>often abbreviated in these texts as R' L' or R' Y', referring to the Talmudic sage</note>, "He who loves his wife as himself and honors her more than himself." For it is enough for you that she raises your children and saves you from sin. Be careful regarding her response <note>specifically referring to her grief or emotional distress</note>, for her tears are frequent and the gates of tears are never closed. Do not engage in excessive conversation with her; regarding one's own wife, they said this, so certainly regarding the wife of your fellow. What is "excessive conversation"? It is like that which someone asked Beruriah, "On which road shall we go to Lod?" She said to him, "Galilean fool, you should have said, 'By which to Lod?' and not..."

<column-break/>

# Book of Fear

that the redness goes and the whiteness comes, and he has no share in the World to Come. It is better for a person to cast himself into a furnace of fire than to whiten the face of his fellow in public. Even if you have rebuked a person in private many times and he did not accept it, it is permitted to shame him, to whiten his face, to hate him, and to pursue him until he accepts it. Whoever is able to rebuke and does not rebuke is a sinner, but if he has rebuked, then he has saved his own soul.

<summary>This page concludes the warnings against public humiliation by explaining the physical and spiritual consequences of shaming others, while clarifying the boundaries regarding when a persistent sinner may be rebuked publicly.</summary>
<keywords>Book of Fear, Honor, Wife, Beruriah, Public Shaming, Rebuke, World to Come</keywords>

->11<-
One who buys three trees within the property of another,
brings [the first fruits] and recites the declaration.
Rabbi Meir says:
Even two trees.
One who bought a tree and its land,
brings and recites the declaration.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even sharecroppers and leaseholders bring and recite.

# Chapter 2

## Tractate Bikkurim Chapter 2 Mishnah 1
->1<-
The <term>terumah</term> <gloss>priestly tithe</gloss> and the <term>bikkurim</term> <gloss>first fruits</gloss>,
one is liable for death and the added fifth <note>penalties for an unauthorized person eating these items</note> for their misuse,
they are prohibited to <term>zarim</term> <gloss>non-priests</gloss>,
they are the property of the priest,
they are neutralized in a mixture of one part in one hundred,
and they require the washing of hands and the setting of the sun <note>to complete ritual purification before being eaten</note>.
These apply to both <term>terumah</term> and <term>bikkurim</term>,
which is not the case for <term>ma'aser</term> <gloss>tithe</gloss>.

## Tractate Bikkurim Chapter 2 Mishnah 2
->2<-
There are rules for <term>ma'aser</term> and <term>bikkurim</term> that do not apply to <term>terumah</term>:
The <term>ma'aser</term> and <term>bikkurim</term> require bringing to the designated place <note>the Temple in Jerusalem</note>,
they require the recitation of the declaration <note>the confession of the first fruits as mandated in Deuteronomy 26</note>, and they are prohibited to a <term>onen</term> <gloss>one in mourning for a close relative before burial</gloss>;
Rabbi Shimon permits this.
They are subject to the law of <term>bi'ur</term> <gloss>the final removal/clearance of tithes every three years</gloss>.
Rabbi Shimon exempts them.
They are prohibited to be eaten in Jerusalem in any quantity <note>if they are considered unclean or restricted</note>,
and their produce <note>if they were planted or harvested in a specific way</note> is prohibited to be eaten in Jerusalem,
even by non-priests and animals.
Rabbi Shimon permits this.
These apply to <term>ma'aser</term> and <term>bikkurim</term>,
which is not the case for <term>terumah</term>.

<summary>This page concludes the regulations regarding ownership requirements for first fruits and begins a comparative analysis of the legal status of first fruits (bikkurim), priestly tithes (terumah), and standard tithes (ma'aser).</summary>
<keywords>Mishnah, Bikkurim, Terumah, Ma'aser, First Fruits, Priestly Tithe, Jerusalem, Ritual Purity, Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Shimon</keywords>

text:
Sukkah

<margin>
Eye of Justice, Lamp of the Commandment
</margin>
<margin>
[Tradition of the Shas]
* Who considers it uncleanness <term>tumah</term> <gloss>ritual impurity</gloss> in thought?
* The reasoning of Rabbi Yose, who deems vessels <term>kelim</term> <gloss>utensils/objects</gloss> to be susceptible to impurity because they are significant.
* And if we say they disagree, it suffices with the thought of the <term>log</term> <gloss>a liquid measure</gloss>.
* For it is written, it is favorable to him, and they thought that since all purities <term>taharot</term> <gloss>laws of ritual purity</gloss> were established, they all apply to him.
* The reason is explained further on.
* [S] Regarding the matter of the merchant, it is all impurity.
* [R. Eliezer] As we argue, and there is no intent for the side that supports.
* [R. Isaac] (Impurity) They write the intent that supports all of them.
* [R. Isaac Pu.] (L) <unclear>stands nu. zay.</unclear>
</margin>

<column-break/>

<note>A printer's mark or ornament appears here.</note>

<unclear>Those</unclear> who lead to impurity through thought. * Who considers it impurity in thought? And if you say it concerns the impurity of vessels because they are significant, and it suffices with the thought of the <term>log</term> <gloss>a liquid measure</gloss>. And if you say it concerns the impurity of vessels because they are significant, and if we say they disagree, it suffices with the thought of the <term>log</term>. <unclear>It is easy to doubt impurity</unclear>: in the sign. text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>

<margin>Source Reference: Ner Mitzvah</margin>
<margin>
Tradition of the Shas:
* Who considers it susceptible to ritual impurity through intention alone.
* The reasoning of Rabbi Yose, who declares vessels that are significant to be susceptible to impurity.
* And if we say they disagree, it would be sufficient for it to have the status of a vessel through intention alone.
* As it is written, he is pleased with them, and they thought to establish all purities through them.
* The reason is explained later.
* [S] To the donkey-driver, everything that covers is considered impurity.
* [Zechariah Elazar] Thus says Marmerginun, and you have no intention for the support.
* [Zechariah Isaac] (Impurity to) They write the intention since it supports all of them.
* [Zechariah Isaac 86:] (Later) 56. 37.
</margin>

<column-break/>

<note>Small circular decorative printer's ornament used as a separator.</note>

They descend into the status of impurity through intention. * Who considers it susceptible to impurity through intention alone? And if you say it refers to the impurity of vessels which are significant, then it would be sufficient with the intention of a vessel. And if you say it refers to the impurity of vessels which are significant, and if we say they disagree, then it would be sufficient with the intention of a vessel. It is easy to clarify the doubt regarding the impurity: as specified below. At its rising. He explains his words: Purity. A vessel. For it is written that he is pleased with them, and they thought to establish all purities, all of them ascended for him. And if you say impurity for all of them further. The reason is explained later: Generally, why are they significant (Ezekiel 15) from those that roll vessels, since they are supported by each other, for they are supported by each other, in the manner of impurity to be supported by each other.

<column-break/>

Sukkah 14

->Chapter One<-

They descend into the status of ritual impurity through intention, but they do not emerge from their status of impurity except through a change brought about by a physical action <note>Hebrew: "ma’aseh"</note>. An action removes an item from the status of a previous action or from the status of a previous intention, but intention does not remove an item from the status of an action nor from the status of a previous intention. And if we say that these items were meant for the purpose of eating, they should become susceptible through intention and lose that status through intention. But did we not learn in a Mishnah: * All handles of food that are in the stack in the threshing floor are ritually pure (and Rabbi Yose) (Rabbi Yose declares them impure). It is understandable according to the one who says the Mishnah refers to the stack, as it was taught that he bound them, that is fine. But according to the one who says: what is meant by "in the stack"? It means the actual stack of grain. What can be said? Here too, it means the actual stack. If so, what is the reasoning of the Sages? It is because they speak according to the view of Rabbi Yose, as we learned: * Rabbi Yose declares them impure. This is understandable there; the reason for Rabbi Yose’s view is according to Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish. For Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork <note>term: "atar" <gloss>pitchfork or winnowing fan</gloss></note>. But here, what are they fit for? It must be said: to catch the fallen grain with their husks. Regarding the matter itself: All handles of food that are in the stack in the threshing floor are ritually pure, and Rabbi Yose and Simeon ben Lakish said: what is meant by "in the stack"? Rabbi Yochanan said: It means the actual stack. Rabbi (Eliezer) says: To permit the pile, for it is the actual stack. Rabbi (Eliezer) who said "in the stack" meant to permit the pile, that is why Rabbi Yose declares it impure. Rather, Rabbi (Eliezer) asked: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork? To tell you: just as this pitchfork turns the grain in the threshing floor from place to place, so too the prayer of the righteous turns the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

Gemara: Rav said: The Mishnah's *dispute regarding covering with boards is between Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Meir. But if the board is four handbreadths wide, everyone agrees that it is valid as long as one does not sleep under it. Gemara: Rav said: The dispute concerns boards that are four handbreadths wide. For everyone agrees that if it is four handbreadths wide, it is valid. Even if it is less than this, they are just like ordinary reeds. Rav Pappa said: This is what he is saying: if they are four handbreadths wide, everyone agrees it is disqualified. If they are less than three handbreadths wide, everyone agrees it is valid, for they are like ordinary reeds. Where do they disagree? From three handbreadths to four handbreadths. One Sage <note>Rabbi Meir</note> holds: Since they do not have the minimum measurement of a "place," we do not decree against them. And the other Sage <note>Rabbi Judah</note> holds: Since they are similar to the ceiling of a house, we decree against them. We learned in the Mishnah: If one placed a board upon it that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid, provided that one does not sleep under it. This is understandable according to Shmuel, who said the dispute is when they are not four handbreadths wide, but if they are four, everyone agrees it is disqualified, and for that reason, one may not sleep under it. But according to Rav, who said the dispute is when they are four handbreadths wide, but if they are not four, everyone agrees it is valid, then according to Rabbi Judah, why should one not sleep under it? Do you think this Mishnah represents everyone's view? The latter part of the Mishnah follows the view of Rabbi Meir. Come and hear: * Two sheets join together.

<column-break/>

<note>The text continues with a discussion of the laws of Sukkah construction, specifically regarding the use of boards and the measurements required for validity.</note>

It also includes a homiletic teaching comparing the prayer of the righteous to a pitchfork that turns divine judgment into mercy.</summary>

<meta>continues from previous page: ...The Sukkah can be rendered susceptible to ritual impurity <term>tumah</term> <gloss>impurity</gloss> through thought, but it can only be removed from that state of impurity through a change in action. An action removes the status established by a previous action and by a thought. A thought, however, does not remove the status established by an action, nor does it remove the status established by another thought. And if you say that this applies only to vessels, which are significant, but handles <term>yadot</term> <gloss>extensions or handles of fruit</gloss> that serve the purpose of eating are established through thought and removed through thought? But did we not learn in a Mishna: All handles of food that were threshed on the threshing floor are pure (and Rabbi Yose declares them impure). It is well according to the one who says that "threshed" means he untied their bundles; that is clear. But according to the one who says, "What is the meaning of 'threshed'? It means actually threshed," what can be said? Here, too, it means they were actually threshed. If so, what is the reasoning of the Others who spoke like Rabbi Yose? For we learned: Rabbi Yose declares them impure. What is this? It is well that there, the reasoning of Rabbi Yose is appropriate for what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned with a pitchfork. But here, for what are they fit? They are fit so that when one gathers them, he takes them with their stalks. The core matter itself: All handles of food that were threshed on the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yose declares them impure. What is "threshed"? Rabbi Yochanan says: Actually threshed. Rabbi Eliezer says: He untied their bundles. It is well according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says "threshed" means he untied their bundles; that is why Rabbi Yose declares them impure. But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says "threshed" means actually threshed, why does Rabbi Yose declare them impure? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned with a pitchfork. Rabbi Eliezer said: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork? To tell you that just as this pitchfork turns the grain on the threshing floor from place to place, so too does the prayer of the righteous turn the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

Mishna: One may use boards for roofing <term>sikhukh</term> <gloss>covering of a Sukkah</gloss>, these are the words of Rabbi Judah, and Rabbi Meir prohibits it. If one placed upon it a board that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid, provided that one does not sleep under it.

Gemara: Rav said: The dispute concerns boards that have four [handbreadths], for Rabbi Meir holds the decree of ceiling [that they resemble a fixed ceiling], and Rabbi Judah does not hold the decree of ceiling. However, regarding boards that do not have four [handbreadths], everyone agrees it is valid. And Shmuel said: The dispute concerns those that do not have four [handbreadths], but if they have four [handbreadths], everyone agrees it is invalid. Do they not have four [handbreadths]? Even if they are less than three [handbreadths], they are merely like reeds. Rabbi Papa said: This is what he is saying: If they have four, everyone agrees it is invalid. If they are less than three, everyone agrees it is valid. What is the reason? They are merely like reeds. When they argue, it is regarding [a width of] from three to four [handbreadths]. One master holds: Since they do not have the legal measure of a place [that can be considered a ceiling], we do not issue a decree. And one master holds: Since they depart from the legal status of <term>lavud</term> <gloss>the rule that gaps of less than three handbreadths are considered joined</gloss>, we do issue a decree. We learned in the Mishna: If one placed upon it a board that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid, provided that one does not sleep under it. It is well according to Shmuel, who said that the dispute concerns those that do not have four, but if they have four, everyone agrees it is invalid; that is why one should not sleep under it. But according to Rav, who said that the dispute is when they have four, but if they do not have four, everyone agrees it is valid, why should one not sleep under it according to Rabbi Judah? Do you think that the end of the clause is everyone's opinion? The latter part of the Mishna refers to Rabbi Meir. Come and hear: Two sheets join together.</meta>

<summary>This page discusses the laws of ritual impurity regarding handles of produce and debates whether boards used for Sukkah roofing are disqualified if they meet or exceed a width of four handbreadths.</summary>
<keywords>Sukkah, Ritual Impurity, Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Meir, Boards, Pitchfork, Prayer</keywords>

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>

They descend to the status of <term>tumah</term> <gloss>ritual impurity</gloss> by means of <term>machshavah</term> <gloss>intention/mental designation</gloss> but they do not emerge from their impurity except through a change in action <note>a physical alteration to the object</note>. <term>Ma'aseh</term> <gloss>a physical action</gloss> can override another action or a mental designation, but mental designation cannot override either an action or another mental designation. And if you should say: These words apply only to vessels, which are significant, but handles <note>stems or attachments of fruit</note> which are only for the purpose of eating are designated by thought and removed from their status by thought? But we have learned in a <term>Mishnah</term>: All handles of food that one crushed in the threshing floor are pure <note>they no longer transmit impurity to the food</note>, while Rabbi Yosei deems them impure.

It is well understood according to the one who says "crushed" means he untied their bundles. But according to the one who says "crushed" literally means crushed, what can be said? Here, too, it means he literally crushed them. If so, what is the reason for the <term>Acherim</term> <gloss>Others/Anonymous Sages</gloss> who rule like Rabbi Yosei? For we learned: Rabbi Yosei deems them impure. Why is this? It is well understood there that the reason of Rabbi Yosei is seen to follow the view of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork <note>the handles still serve a purpose even if crushed</note>. But here, what are they fit for? They are fit for when one dismantles <note>the Sukkah</note>, to be held by their husks.

The text itself states: All handles of food that one crushed in the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yosei deems them impure. What is the meaning of "crushed"? Rabbi Yochanan says: Literally crushed. Rabbi Eliezer says: He untied their bundles. It is well understood according to Rabbi Eliezer who said it means he untied their bundles, that is why Rabbi Yosei deems them impure <note>because the stalks are still intact</note>. But according to Rabbi Yochanan who says it means literally crushed, why does Rabbi Yosei deem them impure? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork.

Rabbi Eliezer said: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork <note>original: "עתר"</note>? To tell you that just as this pitchfork turns over the grain in the threshing floor from place to place, so too the prayer of the righteous turns over the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

### MISHNAH

One may cover <note>the Sukkah</note> with wooden boards <note>original: "נסרים"</note>, these are the words of Rabbi Judah; but Rabbi Meir forbids it. If one placed upon it a board that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid, provided that one does not sleep under it.

### GEMARA

Rav said: The dispute is regarding boards that have four <note>handbreadths of width</note>. For Rabbi Meir holds the Decree of the Ceiling <note>original: "גזרת תקרה"; a rabbinic prohibition against using boards that make the Sukkah look like a permanent house</note>, and Rabbi Judah does not hold the Decree of the Ceiling. But regarding boards that do not have four, all agree it is valid.

And Shmuel said: In a case where they do not have four, there is a dispute; but if they have four, all agree it is invalid.

<note>The Gemara analyzes Shmuel's view:</note> If they do not have four, even if they are less than three? But those are merely like reeds! Rabbi Pappa said: This is what he is saying: If they have four, all agree it is invalid. If they have less than three, all agree it is valid, for what is the reason? They are merely like reeds. When do they disagree? From three to four. One Master <note>Rabbi Meir</note> holds that since they have left the rule of <term>lavud</term> <gloss>the legal principle that gaps less than three handbreadths are considered closed</gloss>, we decree against them. And the other Master <note>Rabbi Judah</note> holds that since they do not reach the size of a significant place <note>four handbreadths</note>, we do not decree against them.

We learned in the Mishnah: If one placed upon it a board that is four handbreadths wide, it is valid, provided that one does not sleep under it. This is well understood according to Shmuel, who said that regarding boards that do not have four there is a dispute, but if they have four all agree it is invalid, and for that reason one may not sleep under it. But according to Rav, who said the dispute is regarding boards that have four, and that according to Rabbi Judah it is valid, why should one not sleep under it? Do you think the end of the Mishnah reflects everyone's view? The end of the Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir.

Come and hear: Two sheets join together...
<column-break/>
Two...
