text:
<meta>continues from previous page: ...He will see Him [as it is written] "when the Lord returns to Zion." And it is said, "The glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." The Father of mercy, He will have mercy on the burdened people, and He will remember the covenant of the steadfast <note>referring to the patriarchs</note>, and He will save our souls from the evil hours, and He will rebuke the evil inclination from those who are carried <note>meaning those who carry the burden of their own frailties</note>, and He will grant us grace for everlasting deliverance. And He will fulfill our requests with a measure of goodness, salvation, and mercy.</meta>

<note>Decorative ornament</note>

The Throne of the Prophets <note>referring to the verses recited when the Torah scroll is removed</note>... 

And this is the Torah which Moses placed before the children of Israel, by the mouth of the Lord, by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted. 
His glory is upon earth and heaven. He has lifted up the horn of His people, praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people close to Him. Hallelujah.

And it says, "His name endures forever," and it is written, "Lord, your name endures forever, Lord, your remembrance throughout all generations."
The Throne of the Prophets (The Ark, etc.).

And trust, and say, "Return, O Lord, to the tens of thousands of the thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength. Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy. For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed. For I have given you a good instruction; do not forsake My Torah. It is a tree of life to those who take hold of it, and those who support it are happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Bring us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old." Blessed are those...

For the Leader, a Psalm of David. May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you high. May He send your help from the sanctuary, and support you from Zion. May He remember all your meal offerings, and accept your burnt offering, Selah. May He grant you your heart's desire, and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your requests. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand. Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we will make mention of the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit that is upon you, and My words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever.

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to the other and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory. And they receive [the words] one from the other and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His might; holy forever and to all eternity. The Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His radiant glory. A spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a sound of great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place. And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great tremor, of those who praise and say: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His presence. The Lord is King forever and to all eternity. The Lord’s kingdom endures forever and to all eternity. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, keep this forever for the inclinations of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their hearts to You. And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; He frequently turns His anger away and does not arouse all His wrath. For You, O Lord, are good, and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your Torah is truth. You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, which You swore to our ancestors from days of old. Blessed be the Lord, day by day He bears our burden, the God of our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. O Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is our God who created us for His glory, and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our hearts to His Torah, and place in our hearts His love and His awe, to do His will and to serve Him with a whole heart, so that we do not labor in vain, nor bring forth for confusion. May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and that we merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing for the years of the days of the Messiah and for the life of the world to come. In order that glory may sing to You and not be silent, O Lord my God, I will thank You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and whose trust the Lord is. Trust in the Lord forever, for in God the Lord is a Rock of eternity. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. The Lord desires, for the sake of His righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord our Master, how glorious is Your name in all the earth.
Be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the Lord.

And now, I pray, let the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies and Your kindnesses, for they are from old.

Magnified and sanctified be His great name. In the world which He created according to His will, and may He establish His kingdom, and cause His redemption to sprout, and bring near [the time of] His Messiah. In your lifetimes and in your days and in the lifetimes of the whole house of Israel, speedily and at a near time, and say: Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised and glorified and exalted and elevated and honored and raised and extolled be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Above (far above) all the blessings and songs, praises and consolations which are uttered in the world, and say: Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and with favor our prayer. May the prayer and supplication of the whole house of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven, and say: Amen. May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be great peace from heaven and life for us and for all Israel, and say: Amen. My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His high places, He will make peace upon us and upon all Israel, and say: Amen.

A prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, and answer me, for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am pious; save Your servant, You my God, who trusts in You. Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to You I call all the day. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, O Lord, are good, and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, O Lord, and shall honor Your name. For You are great and do wondrous things; You alone are God. Teach me Your way, O Lord, that I may walk in Your truth; unite my heart to revere Your name. I will thank You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever. For Your kindness is great toward me, and You have delivered my soul from the lowest depths. O God, the insolent have risen against me, and a congregation of violent men have sought my soul, and they have not set You before them. But You, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Show me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because You, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
May the Lord our God be with us, as He was with our ancestors; may He not forsake us and not abandon us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His ordinances, which He commanded our ancestors. And let these words of mine, which I have supplicated before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is no other.

A Song of Ascents, by David: If it had not been the Lord who was for us, let Israel now say. If it had not been the Lord who was for us when men rose up against us. Then they would have swallowed us alive in the burning of their anger against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the torrent would have gone over our soul. Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare was broken, and we escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

text:
<meta>continues from previous page: ...He will see Him [as it is written] "when the Lord returns to Zion." And it is said, "The glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." The Father of mercy, He will have mercy on the burdened people, and He will remember the covenant of the steadfast <note>referring to the patriarchs</note>, and He will save our souls from the evil hours, and He will rebuke the evil inclination from those who are carried <note>meaning those who carry the burden of their own frailties</note>, and He will grant us grace for everlasting deliverance. And He will fulfill our requests with a measure of goodness, salvation, and mercy.</meta>

<note>Decorative ornament</note>

The Throne of the Prophets <note>referring to the verses recited when the Torah scroll is removed</note>... 

And this is the Torah which Moses placed before the children of Israel, by the mouth of the Lord, by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted. 
His glory is upon earth and heaven. He has lifted up the horn of His people, praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people close to Him. Hallelujah.

And it says, "His name endures forever," and it is written, "Lord, your name endures forever, Lord, your remembrance throughout all generations."
The Throne of the Prophets (The Ark, etc.).

And trust, and say, "Return, O Lord, to the tens of thousands of the thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength. Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy. For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed. For I have given you a good instruction; do not forsake My Torah. It is a tree of life to those who take hold of it, and those who support it are happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Bring us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old." Blessed are those...

For the Leader, a Psalm of David. May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you high. May He send your help from the sanctuary, and support you from Zion. May He remember all your meal offerings, and accept your burnt offering, Selah. May He grant you your heart's desire, and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your requests. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand. Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we will make mention of the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit that is upon you, and My words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever.

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to the other and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory. And they receive [the words] one from the other and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His might; holy forever and to all eternity. The Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His radiant glory. A spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a sound of great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place. And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great tremor, of those who praise and say: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His presence. The Lord is King forever and to all eternity. The Lord’s kingdom endures forever and to all eternity. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, keep this forever for the inclinations of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their hearts to You. And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; He frequently turns His anger away and does not arouse all His wrath. For You, O Lord, are good, and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your Torah is truth. You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, which You swore to our ancestors from days of old. Blessed be the Lord, day by day He bears our burden, the God of our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. O Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is our God who created us for His glory, and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our hearts to His Torah, and place in our hearts His love and His awe, to do His will and to serve Him with a whole heart, so that we do not labor in vain, nor bring forth for confusion. May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and that we merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing for the years of the days of the Messiah and for the life of the world to come. In order that glory may sing to You and not be silent, O Lord my God, I will thank You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and whose trust the Lord is. Trust in the Lord forever, for in God the Lord is a Rock of eternity. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. The Lord desires, for the sake of His righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord our Master, how glorious is Your name in all the earth.
Be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the Lord.

And now, I pray, let the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies and Your kindnesses, for they are from old.

Magnified and sanctified be His great name. In the world which He created according to His will, and may He establish His kingdom, and cause His redemption to sprout, and bring near [the time of] His Messiah. In your lifetimes and in your days and in the lifetimes of the whole house of Israel, speedily and at a near time, and say: Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised and glorified and exalted and elevated and honored and raised and extolled be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Above (far above) all the blessings and songs, praises and consolations which are uttered in the world, and say: Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and with favor our prayer. May the prayer and supplication of the whole house of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven, and say: Amen. May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be great peace from heaven and life for us and for all Israel, and say: Amen. My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His high places, He will make peace upon us and upon all Israel, and say: Amen.

A prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, and answer me, for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am pious; save Your servant, You my God, who trusts in You. Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to You I call all the day. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, O Lord, are good, and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, O Lord, and shall honor Your name. For You are great and do wondrous things; You alone are God. Teach me Your way, O Lord, that I may walk in Your truth; unite my heart to revere Your name. I will thank You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever. For Your kindness is great toward me, and You have delivered my soul from the lowest depths. O God, the insolent have risen against me, and a congregation of violent men have sought my soul, and they have not set You before them. But You, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Show me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because You, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
May the Lord our God be with us, as He was with our ancestors; may He not forsake us and not abandon us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His ordinances, which He commanded our ancestors. And let these words of mine, which I have supplicated before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is no other.

A Song of Ascents, by David: If it had not been the Lord who was for us, let Israel now say. If it had not been the Lord who was for us when men rose up against us. Then they would have swallowed us alive in the burning of their anger against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the torrent would have gone over our soul. Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare was broken, and we escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

14 All glorious is the princess within the chamber; her clothing is inwrought with gold. 15 She shall be led unto the king in raiment of needlework; the virgins her companions that follow her shall be brought unto thee. 16 With gladness and rejoicing shall they be led, they shall enter into the king’s palace. 17 Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou shalt make princes in all the land. 18 I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations; therefore shall the peoples give thee thanks for ever and ever.

-> XLVI. <-

1 For the Leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah; set to Alamoth <note>original: "עלמות", likely a musical term or soprano-like register.</note>. A Song. 2 God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. 3 Therefore will we not fear, though the earth do change, and though the mountains be moved into the heart of the seas. 4 Let the waters thereof roar and foam, let the mountains shake at the swelling thereof. Selah. 5 There is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High. 6 God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; God shall help her, at the approach of morning. 7 The nations made a tumult <note>continues into next page</note>

text:
<header>Emor</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion among the holy people, even more than all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss>, to receive the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. And a person ought to rejoice with the poor, because the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss> who are invited belongs to the poor. And he who dwells in all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss> and invites these supernal <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, the guests of faith, and gives them their portion, they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that that table which he prepared is his, and not the Holy One, blessed be He’s. Concerning him it is written:
> **Behold, I will rebuke your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, etc. The dung of your feasts, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person at the hour when those guests of faith stand up from the table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and to receive them at the table. Now that they have invited him, and all the righteous, and King David, and they do not give them their portion, that is more difficult than everything, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all rise and say: <term>Isaac</term> said:
> **And the belly of the wicked shall lack** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> said:
> **Your bread that you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And the rest of all the righteous said:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> said, and the laws of the destitute <note>or: oppression</note>, as it is written, and it was when the days were finished, and the Lord waved the... and they are speaking of the dead. Because David begged for the table and he was made a guest, but he did not seek, and did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. And like the crown and the right hand of King David, they judge the world, especially that person who closes his hand more than everything. Rabbi Eleazar said: The path of piety does not exempt a person, except by what he can, as it is written, according to the gift of his hand, etc. And not the board <note>or: tablet</note> of the poor, and the full and satisfied is the first, and what remains to give to the poor. Even the spirit of everything is that of the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, and he is given to the guests, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a friend with him, and for a blessing He calls upon him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This is what King David said, because all types of kings and those close to the King are entrusted into the hand of David. He who rejoices... in his portion, and his friend, etc. ...Jacob said to him... the rest of the righteous said... and the Lord shall satisfy you continually, etc. King David said, no weapon that is formed against you shall prosper, because he is entrusted with all types of types. And all the portion of a person who merits all this merit, the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, about them it is written:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

<column-break/>

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

**A commandment** this is, to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> properly on these days, and they are humble, and he adorns it, and the secret stands as we have established, "And you shall take," <term>Padirus</term> <gloss>a mystical term for taking/holding</gloss>, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time, for they are His. Likewise, they require the Holy One, blessed be He, in their portion, and delight in Him. And this is the first, this is the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss>, and it is fitting to take the mystery of the image of Man, and so below. It is done.

The creator, the blind to all in His mercies and in His laws, and also His deeds. All the creator, the blind, this is Man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls "the blind," as it is written, "And God created man in His image," and furthermore that which they seek in His name at the time when He is pure and distinct in the world, and they seek God, as it is written, "You shall not revile God," he called him in His name, as it is written, "And God created"

<column-break/>

"man in His image," and beautifully we have established it, as it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness**, at the time when the union was mentioned. And such is the intention of both, in "image" and "likeness," and one is of the male and female, and it went forth, "And God created man in His image." Like the crown that rises, we find that at the time of the union, it is found.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual responsibility of inviting the Ushpizin (guests) during Sukkot, emphasizing that failure to provide for the poor during this time is spiritually catastrophic, and concludes with a mystical exposition on the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, King David, Faith, Commandments, Lulav, Divine Image, Union, Creation, Righteousness</keywords>

text:
<header>Emor</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion among the holy people, even more than all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss>, to receive the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. And a person ought to rejoice with the poor, because the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss> who are invited belongs to the poor. And he who dwells in all of the <term>faith</term> <gloss>divine presence</gloss> and invites these supernal <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, the guests of faith, and gives them their portion, they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that that table which he prepared is his, and not the Holy One, blessed be He’s. Concerning him it is written:
> **Behold, I will rebuke your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, etc. The dung of your feasts, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person at the hour when those guests of faith stand up from the table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and to receive them at the table. Now that they have invited him, and all the righteous, and King David, and they do not give them their portion, that is more difficult than everything, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all rise and say: <term>Isaac</term> said:
> **And the belly of the wicked shall lack** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> said:
> **Your bread that you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And the rest of all the righteous said:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> said, and the laws of the destitute <note>or: oppression</note>, as it is written, and it was when the days were finished, and the Lord waved the... and they are speaking of the dead. Because David begged for the table and he was made a guest, but he [the host] did not seek, and did not invite him [David], and did not give him his portion. And like the crown and the right hand of King David, they judge the world, especially that person who closes his hand more than everything. Rabbi Eleazar said: The path of piety does not exempt a person, except by what he can, as it is written, according to the gift of his hand, etc. And not the board <note>or: tablet</note> of the poor, and the full and satisfied is the first, and what remains to give to the poor. Even the spirit of everything is that of the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>guests</gloss>, and he is given to the guests, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a friend with him, and for a blessing He calls upon him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This is what King David said, because all types of kings and those close to the King are entrusted into the hand of David. He who rejoices... in his portion, and his friend, etc. ...Jacob said to him... the rest of the righteous said... and the Lord shall satisfy you continually, etc. King David said, no weapon that is formed against you shall prosper, because he is entrusted with all types of types. And all the portion of a person who merits all this merit, the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, about them it is written:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

<column-break/>

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

**A commandment** this is, to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> properly on these days, and they are humble, and he adorns it, and the secret stands as we have established, "And you shall take," <term>Padirus</term> <gloss>a mystical term for taking/holding</gloss>, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time, for they are His. Likewise, they require the Holy One, blessed be He, in their portion, and delight in Him. And this is the first, this is the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss>, and it is fitting to take the mystery of the image of Man, and so below. It is done.

The creator, the blind to all in His mercies and in His laws, and also His deeds. All the creator, the blind, this is Man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls "the blind," as it is written, "And God created man in His image," and furthermore that which they seek in His name at the time when He is pure and distinct in the world, and they seek God, as it is written, "You shall not revile God," he called him in His name, as it is written, "And God created"

<column-break/>

"man in His image," and beautifully we have established it, as it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness**, at the time when the union was mentioned. And such is the intention of both, in "image" and "likeness," and one is of the male and female, and it went forth, "And God created man in His image." Like the crown that rises, we find that at the time of the union, it is found.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual responsibility of inviting the Ushpizin (guests) during Sukkot, emphasizing that failure to provide for the poor during this time is spiritually catastrophic, and concludes with a mystical exposition on the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, King David, Faith, Commandments, Lulav, Divine Image, Union, Creation, Righteousness</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page: ...the people of the world who see that the person who has a portion in the holy nation is superior in everything regarding faith, by receiving guests to rejoice in this world and the world to come.</meta>

A servant <note>of God</note> must cause the poor to rejoice, for the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>Holy Guests</gloss> whom he invites belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these supernal guests, the Guests of Faith, and gives them their portion <note>by feeding the poor</note>, all of them stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6; the Guests refuse the table of one who does not share with the poor</note>

It follows that such a table which he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One’s, blessed be He. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those Guests of Faith rise from his table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham all his days stood at the crossroads to invite guests and receive them at his table. Now that they <note>the supernal Guests</note> invite him and all the righteous, and King David, and people do not give them their portion <note>by neglecting the poor</note>, this is the most difficult thing of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the rest of the righteous say:
> **For all tables are full of filthy vomit, so that there is no place clean** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression, for it is written <unclear>as the lead of the days</unclear> <note>The OCR text here contains highly corrupted readings of verses and Aramaic idioms</note>. This refers to David, for he was a guest and no one invited him or gave him a portion. Since King David is the crown and the right hand that sustains the world, that person who harms him is excluded from everything. Rabbi Eleazar said: The Torah does not impose a burden on a person beyond what he is able to do, as it is written, *every man shall give as he is able* <note>Deuteronomy 16:17</note>. One should not say: "I will eat and satisfy myself first, and what is left I will give to the poor." Rather, the essence of the Guests is the priority. If he gladdens the Guests, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, and the verse calls him for a blessing:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac says over him:
> **No weapon formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David said this because all the weapons of the King and the battles of the King were entrusted into the hands of David. Happy is the man who rejoices in his portion. Jacob said of him: *Then shall your light break forth as the morning, etc.* <note>Isaiah 58:8</note>. The rest of the righteous said: *And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul, etc.* <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. King David said: *No weapon formed against you shall prosper*, for he is appointed over all types of weapons. All this portion is merited by a person through these merits. Of the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, it is written:
> **Your people shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

***

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulvav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is proper in these days, to be humble and armed with it. This is the secret we have established: *And you shall take* <note>Hebrew: *u-lekachtem*</note> suggests *padi-ros* <note>A wordplay implying "redemption of the head"</note>, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion and take refuge in Him. First is the Lulav, which is the secret of the <term>Diyokna</term> <gloss>image/form</gloss> of Adam, and so it is below.

<unclear>Regarding the corrupted OCR text regarding Samael and mercy</unclear>. This "Adam" is what the Holy One, blessed be He, called "Man," as it is written: *And God created man in His own image.* Furthermore, it was explored in the <term>Bamma</term> <gloss>high place/altar</gloss> at the time when truth and radiance went out into the world. It is written *Elohim* <gloss>God/Judges</gloss> *you shall not revile* <note>Exodus 22:27</note>, and it is written: *And God created*

---

*man in His own image.* And we have well established what is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness** <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. This was said at the time of the union <note>of the divine attributes</note>. This is the intention of both, "image" and "likeness," for from the union of male and female came forth: *And God created man in His own image.* When the King ascended, we find that He was present at the time of the union.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual necessity of giving charity to the poor during Sukkot to satisfy the supernal Guests (Ushpizin). It also begins a mystical discourse on the Lulav and the creation of man in the Divine Image (Tzelem).</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, Table, King David, Lulav, Divine Image, Tzelem, Likeness, Faithful Shepherd, Sukkot</keywords>

text:
<header>Emor</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion among the holy people sits in the shadow of faith to welcome the <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>holy guests</gloss> in order to rejoice in this world and the world to come. And yet, one must also rejoice with the poor. Why? Because the portion of these <term>Ushpizin</term> is truly that of the poor. And he who sits in this shadow of faith and invites these exalted guests—the guests of faith—but does not give them their portion, they all rise from him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of a man who is stingy, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that the table he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One’s, blessed be He. About him it is written:
> **And I will spread dung upon your faces, etc., the dung of your festivals** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

But not My festivals. Woe to that person at the hour when these guests of faith rise from his table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroad to invite guests and prepare tables for them. Now, when they invite him, and all the righteous, and King David, and one does not give them their portion, Abraham rises from the table and calls out:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all rise after him. <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **And the belly of the wicked shall lack** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **You shall vomit up the morsel you have eaten** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, without place** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> said and completed his judgments, as it is written: *And it came to pass after ten days, that the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.* What does he speak of? Because David asked Nabal, and he was made a guest for him, but he did not want to, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. And during those ten days when King David judges the world, that person who completes for him more evil than Nabal is judged. Rabbi Eleazar said: Therefore, the Torah does not burden a person more than he is able, as it is written: *A man according to the gift of his hand, etc.* And a person should not say, "I will eat and be satisfied and drunk first, and what remains I will give to the poor." Rather, the essence of everything is the <term>Ushpizin</term>. If one rejoices the <term>Ushpizin</term> and satisfies them, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, and Abraham calls out concerning him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls out concerning him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This is what King David said, because all the weapons of the King and the King’s battles are entrusted into the hand of David. But Isaac says: *His seed shall be mighty upon the earth, etc.; wealth and riches are in his house, etc.* Jacob says: *Then shall your light break forth as the morning, etc.* The other righteous ones say: *And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy, etc.* King David said: *No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper*, for he is entrusted with all the weapons of the world. Blessed is the portion of the person who merits all this; the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come is theirs. Concerning them it is written:
> **And your people are all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened: *Everyone who is called by My name, for My glory I have created him, I have formed him, yes, I have made him.* "Everyone who is called by My name"—this is man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls by His name, as it is written: *And God created man in His image.* Furthermore, he is called by His name at the time when He brings forth justice and judgment into the world, and he is called <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>God</gloss>, as it is written: *You shall not revile Elohim*. He called him by His name, as it is written: *And Elohim created man in His image*. And this is well established, as it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness**, at the time of the union <note>referring to the mystical union of the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine</note>. And so it is in the union of both: in image and likeness, male and female were brought forth. *And Elohim created man in His image.* In the book of King Solomon, we found that at the time of the union

<column-break/>

### The Faithful Shepherd

This is a **precept**: to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch, part of the Four Species for Sukkot</gloss> on that day with its species. This mystery we have established, and the companions established it, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes them to Israel on these days and rejoices in them. So, too, Israel takes Him, the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion and rejoices in Him. And this is the mystery of the <term>Lulav</term> and the species within it, which is the mystery of the image of man, and it has already been stated. Thus far.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual obligations of inviting the seven "Holy Guests" (Ushpizin) to the Sukkah, the consequences of failing to provide for the poor during the festival, and the mystical interpretation of man being created in the divine image.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Sukkot, Charity, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, King David, Lulav, Image of God, Faithful Shepherd</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page: He would sit a second time for the people of the world who see that he who has a portion in the holy people sits in the Shadow of Faith.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He who has a portion in the holy people sits in the <term>Shadow of Faith</term> <gloss>Zila de-Meimanuta</gloss> to receive guests, to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. Therefore, one must bring joy to the poor. Why? Because the portion of those guests whom he invites belongs to the poor. If a person sits in this Shadow of Faith and invites these supreme guests, the <term>Guests of Faith</term> <gloss>Ushpizin</gloss>, but does not give them their portion <note>by feeding the poor</note>, they all rise up and leave him, saying:
> **Do not eat the bread of a stingy man...** <note>Proverbs 23:6; literally "one with an evil eye"</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is not present at it. Regarding him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival offerings...** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

"Your festivals," but not "My festivals." Woe to that man at the moment when these Guests of Faith rise from his table! 

Rabbi Abba said: All his days, <term>Abraham</term> <gloss>the first patriarch, representing Loving-kindness</gloss> stood at the crossroads to invite guests and prepare tables for them. Now, when they invite him and all the righteous ones and <term>King David</term>, and they are not given their portion, Abraham rises from the table and calls out:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men...** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And all the others follow after him. <term>Isaac</term> <gloss>the second patriarch, representing Judgment</gloss> says:
> **...but the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> <gloss>the third patriarch, representing Beauty/Balance</gloss> says:
> **The morsel which you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of filthy vomit, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> <gloss>representing Kingship/Shekhinah</gloss> spoke and completed the judgment, as it is written: *And it came to pass about ten days after, that the Lord smote Nabal, and he died.* <note>1 Samuel 25:38</note> Why is this mentioned? Because David asked Nabal <note>for food</note> and would have become his guest, but Nabal did not want him, did not invite him, and gave him no portion. During those ten days when King David judges the world, judgment was passed upon that man <note>the stingy host</note>, for he is even worse than Nabal. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: Therefore, the Torah does not burden a person beyond his capacity, as it is written: *Every man shall give as he is able...* <note>Deuteronomy 16:17</note> Let a person not say: "I will eat and satisfy myself and drink first, and what remains I will give to the poor." Rather, the very first of everything belongs to the guests. If he makes the guests happy and satisfies them, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him. Abraham calls out concerning him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls out concerning him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper...** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Simeon said: King David said this last verse, because all the King's armaments and the King's wars are entrusted to David's hand. But Isaac says: *His seed shall be mighty upon earth... wealth and riches shall be in his house.* <note>Psalm 112:2-3</note> Jacob says: *Then shall your light break forth as the morning...* <note>Isaiah 58:8</note> The other righteous ones say: *The Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul in drought...* <note>Isaiah 58:11</note> King David said: *No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper,* for he is appointed over all the armaments of the world. Worthy is the portion of the man who merits all of this! Worthy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come; concerning them it is written:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous...** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

Rabbi Simeon opened: *Every one that is called by My name, for My glory I have created him, I have formed him, yea, I have made him.* <note>Isaiah 43:7</note> "Every one that is called by My name"—this refers to Man <note>Adam</note>, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, called by His own name, as it is written: *And God created man in His own image.* <note>Genesis 1:27</note> Furthermore, man is called by His name when He brings Truth and Judgment into the world and is called <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>God/Judge</gloss>, as it is written: *You shall not revile the judges <note>Elohim</note>.* He called man by His name, as it is written: *And God <note>Elohim</note> created man in His own image.* And we have already established this well, for it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness**—this was said at the time of union <note>the mystical union of the divine attributes</note>. So it is with the union of the two, in "image" and "likeness," and Man emerged from Male and Female. *And God created man in His own image.* In the book of King Solomon, we find that at the time of union

it is found

---

### The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

**This commandment** is to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch used on Sukkot</gloss> on that day with its specific species. We have established this secret, and the companions have established it: just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel in these days and rejoices in them, so too Israel takes the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion and rejoices in Him. This is the secret of the Lulav and the species within it, which is the secret of the form of Man <note>the Lulav represents the spine, the Myrtle the eyes, the Willow the lips, and the Etrog the heart</note>, as has been stated. Until here.

<summary>This page emphasizes the spiritual necessity of giving charity to the poor as a prerequisite for hosting the seven mystical guests (Ushpizin) in the Sukkah. It also begins a discourse on the creation of Man in the Divine Image and the mystical symbolism of the Lulav.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, Sukkah, King David, Abraham, Shadow of Faith, Image of God, Lulav, Divine Union, Nabal</keywords>

text:
# No. 20 (CBS 16023)

->In the name of Ṭardi daughter of Oni<-
(2) Hormisdar Ṭardi, AAAAAA, bound and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) that appear by night and appear by day, and that appear to Ṭardi daughter of [Oni...] (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah, Hallelujah, according to AAAAAA.

### Translation

Ṭardi daughter of Oni (2) Hormisdar Ṭardi. In the name of AAAAAA, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear (to) Ṭardi daughter of [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Hallelia, Selah. According to AAAAAA.

### Commentary

A charm against ghosts. The interest of this bowl lies in the figure decorating the center. It represents a demon with arms and legs manacled. On either side of the figures is an enclosed space, that on the figure’s right hand bearing the inscription <term>asura</term> <gloss>prohibition</gloss>, that on its left, <term>rsha</term> <gloss>permission</gloss>. In the lower part of the body on the former side is inscribed the names of the sorcerer’s client. The picture thus graphically presents the idea that the demon has no power over the lady in question. The picture is of better quality than the inscription, which is very illiterate. The spelling is most careless.

1. The connection of the proper names is uncertain, as also the character of the names themselves. For Hormisdar I might compare the Pahlavi <term>Ormazdyâr</term> <gloss>name of a Zoroastrian deity</gloss>, Justi, p. 10a.
2. For the repeated A, see p. 60.
3. <term>laṭana</term> <gloss>curse-spirit</gloss>: probably an artificial form; cf. <term>satana</term> <gloss>Satan</gloss>, <term>ṭalana</term> <gloss>shadow-spirit</gloss>, <term>shidana</term> <gloss>demon-spirit</gloss>.

<summary>This page presents an incantation text intended for a woman named Ṭardi, accompanied by a scholarly description of an illustration featuring a bound demon.</summary>
<keywords>Ṭardi daughter of Oni, Hormisdar, Aramaic incantation, CBS 16023, Liliths, Gabriel, Michael, Rophiel, Pahlavi, demonology</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
to finish in judgment and paved a way to receive their arrival. Regarding this, it is said: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, he <note>the Ancient One/Keter</note> fled to him, he fled to his attribute <note>Judgment</note> from the Word. Therefore, may He be blessed, at the time of the Small Judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for My sake, for My sake I will do it <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>, for how shall He be profaned? This occurs at the time of the Small Judgment. All of this generation consists of lines of "everything," and this is the secret of "all of it is turned white; he is clean" <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>. In this way, contemplate to understand the <term>Fear of Isaac</term> <gloss>the attribute of Judgment</gloss>, the strength and the Word, according to the sense that the Supreme <term>Keter</term> <gloss>Crown</gloss> is crowned, shining its face downward to the great Void, covered with Life to the lap of Mercy, according to the sense that the Supreme shines His face, becoming revealed from the covering. This is the secret: "God <note>YHVH</note> caused His face to shine and was gracious to you" <note>Numbers 6:25</note>.

Behold, I shall explain to you further through the Word: know that wherever you find "Light of the Face" above, it is a great secret. It is because the three attributes and the <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>Diadem/Shekhinah</gloss> are the face of the World, and they all cling to the <term>Fear of Isaac</term>. When the attribute of the Crown <term>Keter</term> shines its face, it is attributed to everything as Mercy and is grasped here as Mercy. This is the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light" <note>Psalms 118:27</note>. This is the order: "Happy is the people that knows the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance" <note>Psalms 89:16</note>. Thus, contemplate the secret: "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing" <note>Genesis 27:1</note>. Then you will grasp the secret of the blast <note>of the Shofar</note> in the secret of "God has gone up with a shout" <note>Psalms 47:6</note>, for the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that knows the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance" is that they will find mercy from the sound of the Shofar of the ram of Isaac. 

When you contemplate the meaning of "in the light of Your countenance they walk," which is our foundation, we say "He who remembers the visual-perceptions" <note>a liturgical phrase</note>. Through the secret of the "Back of the Word," you will understand what exists between "He who remembers the visual-perceptions" and "He who remembers the Back of the Word." For "Remembering the visual-perceptions" is drawn from the great Mercies of above, in the secret of "God is the Lord, and He has given us light." But the "Back of the Word" is drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, from the attribute of Judgment of which it is said: "and darkness was upon the face of the deep" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>, and "He remembered the secret and the kindness." Therefore, the attribute of the Lord <note>YHVH</note> shines below, included in the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, the place where the secret is in the head. This is the secret of "He caused His face to shine and was gracious to you." 

Understand this well, for the world stands upon these two attributes. Therefore, I inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name <note>YHVH</note>, may He be blessed, which is the decisive factor in the middle, and it is uniquely composed of His completeness. Like the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>YHVH as Elohim</note>, which stands in the middle, surveying the right—which is Kindness <term>Chesed</term>—and the left—which is Judgment <term>Din</term>—and they are all included in the middle from Kindness and Judgment. They are all called by the nicknames of Kindness in the middle, and they are called the nicknames of Mercy, and their elevation is in the middle, for the Mercy and the Crowns prevail. 

Behold, I explain through the Word: know that all the Holy Names and the nicknames and the words—whether they are called Kindness, whether they are called Mercy, or whether they are called Judgment—not one of them is pure Kindness or pure Judgment or pure Mercy unless there is a mixture in them, from that level and below. But from that level and above, everything is pure Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture in the world. 

Now, open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, like the principles of the steps of the Chariot and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>Divine Emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand a bit of how the <term>Sefirot</term> and the Names and the words are connected in the world. By His crowning, may He be blessed, you will understand the secret of the General Root of everything, may He be blessed and exalted. Know that the names of the Supreme Crown <term>Keter</term> are all simple names without any mixture of a thing. Just as the known Mercies that are adjacent to the name <term>Eheyeh</term> or the Kindness adjacent to the name <term>Eheyeh</term> are all completely simple, having no mixture of a thing. This is the secret of what is said: "but with great mercies will I gather thee" <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. And what are "great mercies" but...

to finish with judgment and to pave a path for their destruction. Regarding this it is said: And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, he fled from it, he fled from his attribute <note>the attribute of strict judgment</note>. Therefore, may He be blessed, at the time of harsh judgment, He has mercy on His world and returns for My sake, for My sake, I will do it <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>; for how could He be destroyed? This is the time of harsh judgment: All of it has turned white; he is clean <note>Leviticus 13:13</note>, and this is the secret of: All has turned, therefore he is clean. 

In this manner, contemplate and understand the Dread of Isaac <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>the attribute of severe judgment</gloss>. When it is crowned by the Supreme <term>Keter</term> <gloss>the Crown, the highest emanation</gloss>, it illuminates its face downward to the great abyss, covering it with Mercy. This is like the Supernal face illuminating and revealing itself from under the covering. This is the meaning of: The Lord cause His face to shine upon you <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. 

I shall now explain to you another secret. Know that wherever you find the "shining of the face" above, it is a great secret. It is because the three attributes <note>likely Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note> and the Crown <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>the Diadem or Shekhinah</gloss> are the face of the inwardness. They all cling to the Dread of Isaac, and when the attribute of the Crown <term>Keter</term> illuminates its face, it is attributed to the totality of Mercy and is perceived here as Mercy. This is the secret of: God is the Lord, and He hath given us light <note>Psalm 118:27</note>. 

This is the order of the verse: Happy is the people that know the joyful sound; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance <note>Psalm 89:16</note>. Contemplate the secret: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing. From this you will grasp the secret of "Sound the <term>Shofar</term> <gloss>ram's horn</gloss> on the New Moon" <note>Psalm 81:4</note>, for the sake of the day of our festival. The secret of "Happy is the people that know the joyful sound <term>Teruah</term>; they walk in the light of Thy countenance" means they will receive mercy from the ram of Isaac. 

When you contemplate the phrase "in the light of Thy countenance they walk," it is the foundation of what we say in prayer: He who remembers the binding <note>of Isaac</note>. From the secret of the "remembrance of the binding" you will understand the difference between "He who remembers the binding" and "He who remembers the ashes of the binding." "Remembering the binding" is drawn from the Great Mercy above, through the secret of: God is the Lord, and He hath given us light. "The ashes of the binding" are drawn from the attribute of God <term>Elohim</term>, from the attribute of the Judge <term>Dayan</term>, of whom it is said: For He shall look upon the face of the deep. Thus, the attribute of the Tetragrammaton <term>Y-H-V-H</term> shines below, included within the attribute of <term>Elohim</term>, which is the place of the foundation of the head. This is the secret of: He caused His face to shine upon you.

Stand firm in knowing these two attributes. Now I will inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term> which balances in the center and unites with its perfection. Like the image of a balance, <term>Y-H-V-H</term> stands in the middle, balancing the right side which is Kindness <term>Chesed</term> and the left side which is Judgment <term>Din</term>. They are both included in the center, between Kindness and Judgment. All the titles of Kindness in the center are called Titles of Mercy, and their ascent to the middle of the balance increases Mercy and closeness. 

I will now explain. Know that all the Holy Names, the Titles, and the Words—whether they are called Kindness, whether they are called Mercy, or whether they are called Judgment—none of them are pure Kindness, pure Judgment, or pure Mercy. Rather, they are all a mixture from the level of the Balance and below. However, from the Balance and above, everything is pure Mercy and pure Kindness, simple and without mixture at all. 

Now open your eyes and set your heart to these deep matters, which are like principles for the levels of the Chariot <term>Merkavah</term> and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand how the <term>Sefirot</term>, the Names, and the Words are tied together in the world. By His will, you will understand the secret of the general rule of everything. Know that the Names of the Supreme Crown <term>Keter Elyon</term> are all simple names without any mixture of anything. Even the known Mercies that are adjacent to the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> or the Kindness adjacent to the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> are all entirely simple and have no mixture. This is the secret of: But with great mercies will I gather thee <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. What are these "great mercies"? They are...

It explains that while lower emanations are mixtures of attributes, the highest Crown consists of pure, unmixed Mercy.</summary>
<keywords>Isaac, Keter, Chesed, Din, Teruah, Shofar, Binding of Isaac, Names of God, Balance</keywords>

Hosts in judgment, and the Holy God is sanctified through righteousness. And regarding this it is said, "And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old," and "his eyes were dim," meaning it speaks also of him and also of his attribute. And therefore the Lord, may He be blessed, at the time of harsh judgment, has mercy on His world and says, "For My own sake, for My own sake I will do it; for how should it be profaned?" And this is what they, of blessed memory, said: "The son of David will not come except in a generation that is entirely liable," etc. And this is the secret of "though they be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow." And according to this path, understand that the fear of Isaac <note>representing the attribute of severe judgment</note> has no power and dominion at the time when the supreme Crown <term>Keter</term> <gloss>the highest sefirah</gloss> illuminates its face downward, because its great light dims the light of the eyes of the fear of Isaac. And this is the secret of "The Lord make His face shine upon you, and be gracious unto you." What is "and be gracious unto you"? That if you are not worthy of mercy at the time that the supreme faces shine, He will give you a gift of grace. And this is the secret of "The Lord make His face shine upon you, and be gracious unto you." 

And behold, I am enlightening your eyes further, with the help of God. Know that in every place that you find the light of faces from above, it is a great secret. It is that there are three hundred and ten faces of wrath, and all of them are attached to the fear of Isaac. And when the attribute of the Crown illuminates its face and brings out the banner of mercy, which has inscribed upon it the attribute of God <term>El</term> <gloss>a name signifying mercy</gloss>, which is the secret of the tithes of the faces of wrath, then all the faces of wrath return to shine and are all turned into mercy. And this is the secret of "God <term>El</term> is the Lord <term>YHVH</term>, and He has given us light." And this is "Happy is the people that know the joyful shout; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance." 

And if so, contemplate the secret of "And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing." And then you will grasp the secret of "Blow the horn in the new moon, in the covering, for our feast day." And the secret of "Happy is the people that know the joyful shout; they walk, O Lord, in the light of Your countenance." And you will see what is the horn of the ram of Isaac. # The Gates of Light

And regarding this it is said: And it came to pass when Isaac was old and his eyes were dim <note>Genesis 27:1</note>; that is to say, it speaks both of him and of his specific attribute <gloss>the attribute of Judgment, Din</gloss>. Therefore, may the Lord be blessed, at the time of harsh judgment He has compassion on His world and says: For My own sake, for My own sake, I will do it, for how should My name be profaned? <note>Isaiah 48:11</note>. This is what our Sages of blessed memory meant when they said: The Son of David <gloss>the Messiah</gloss> will not come except in a generation that is entirely guilty, etc., and this is the secret of: It is all turned white, he is clean <note>Leviticus 13:13, a law regarding leprosy used here as a mystical paradox</note>.

By this path, contemplate that the <term>Pachad Yitzchak</term> <gloss>Fear of Isaac, the attribute of Judgment</gloss> has no power or dominion at the time when the <term>Keter Elyon</term> <gloss>Supreme Crown</gloss> shines its face downward, because its great light dims the light of the eyes of the Fear of Isaac. This is the secret of: May the Lord make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. What is "and be gracious to you" <note>Hebrew: ve-yichuneka</note>? That even if you are not worthy of mercy, at the time when the Higher Faces shine, He will give you a free gift <note>Hebrew: matnat chinam</note>. This is the secret of: May <term>YHVH</term> make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you.

Behold, I will enlighten your eyes further with the help of God. Know that in every place you find "the light of the Face" from above, it is a great secret. It is because there are three hundred and ten faces of wrath, and they are all attached to the Fear of Isaac. But when the attribute of the Crown shines its face and brings forth the banner of mercy, upon which is engraved the attribute of <term>El</term> <gloss>God/the attribute of Kindness</gloss>—which is the secret of the tithes <note>The numerical value of "El" (31) is a tenth of the 310 faces of wrath</note> of the faces of wrath—then all the faces of wrath return to shining and are all transformed into mercy. This is the secret of: <term>El YHVH</term>, and He has given us light <note>Psalm 118:27</note>. And this is: Happy is the people who know the joyful sound; <term>YHVH</term>, they walk in the light of Your face <note>Psalm 89:16</note>.

If so, contemplate the secret of: And it came to pass when Isaac was old and his eyes were dim from seeing. Then you will grasp the secret of: Blow the shofar at the New Moon, at the hidden time for our feast day <note>Psalm 81:4</note>. And the secret of: Happy is the people who know the joyful sound; <term>YHVH</term>, they walk in the light of Your face. You shall see what the shofar made from the ram of Isaac is. When you contemplate these matters, you will then enter into the secret of what we say in prayer: "Former of the luminaries" and "Creator of the fires of light." Then you will understand the difference between "Former of the luminaries" and "Creator of the fires of light."

For the "Formation of the luminaries" is drawn from the Great Mercies of above, in the secret of: <term>El YHVH</term>, and He has given us light. But the "Fires of light" are drawn from the attribute of <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>, from the attribute of darkness, of which it is said: And darkness was upon the face of the deep <note>Genesis 1:2</note>, and: Who forms light and creates darkness <note>Isaiah 45:7</note>. Therefore, the attribute of <term>El</term> illuminates the darkness that is included within the attribute of <term>Elohim</term>, which is the secret of the Fire. This is the secret of: May <term>YHVH</term> make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you.

Now that we have informed you of this regarding these two attributes, we must inform you of the secret of the attribute of the Name <term>YHVH</term>, may He be blessed, which tips the balance in the middle, and how He conducts His world. The designations of <term>YHVH</term>, may He be blessed, which stand in the middle of the row: to their right is <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Kindness</gloss>, and to their left is <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>, and they are comprised in the center of both Kindness and Judgment. These designations in the center are called the designations of Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>, and regarding them it is said: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses <note>Daniel 9:9</note>.

I shall now explain with the help of God. Know that among all the Holy Names, the designations, and the attributes—whether they are called Kindness, or Mercy, or Judgment—there is not one among them that is absolute Kindness, absolute Judgment, or absolute Mercy without having some mixture. All of this applies from the Name <term>EHYEH</term> <gloss>I Am/Keter</gloss> and below. But from Him and above, all is absolute Mercy and Kindness, simple and without any mixture in the world.

Now, open your eyes and set your heart to see deep matters that are like general principles for the arrangements of the Chariot and the connection of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>Divine Emanations</gloss>. When you see this, you will understand a little of how the Sefirot, the Names, and the attributes are tied to one another and receive from one another, and how they all become one union and one intention without any separation in the world. When you understand this, you will understand the secret of the Unity of the Creator of all, may He be blessed and exalted.

Know that the names of the Supreme Crown <term>Keter Elyon</term> are all simple names without any mixture of anything. How so? The known Mercies that are adjacent to the Name <term>EHYEH</term>, or the Kindness adjacent to the Name <term>EHYEH</term>, are all absolute and simple; they have no mixture of any other thing. This is the secret of what is said: And with great mercies I will gather you <note>Isaiah 54:7</note>. For what are "Great Mercies" if not...

<summary>This page explains how the supreme attribute of the Crown (Keter) illuminates and transforms the harsh judgment associated with Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak). It distinguishes between the "Luminaries" of mercy and the "Fires" of judgment, emphasizing that while lower emanations are mixtures of traits, the highest levels are pure mercy.</summary>
<keywords>Isaac, Keter, Mercy, Judgment, EHYEH, YHVH, Sefirot, Creation of Light, 310 faces of wrath</keywords>

of a sandal and the head-tefillin <note>phylacteries</note> when it is covered, and of the arm when it is rising and falling, and the ears of the cauldron, and the ears of the satchel. **4** These are the things that require water to enter them: the knot in the joints of the shoulder, and the rim of a coat of mail, and the head-tefillin when it is not covered, and that of the arm when it is rising and falling, and the stitches of a sandal, and the wings. They immersed them while covered until they were submerged, and they immersed them while uncovered until they bubbled, and they rested from bubbling. **5** All handles of vessels that are long, and he intends to cut them, are immersed up to the measured place. Rabbi Judah says: Until he immerses all of them. The chain of a large bucket is four handbreadths, and that of a small one is ten; they are immersed up to the measured place. Rabbi Tarfon says: Until he immerses the entire ring. A rope tied to a basket is not considered attached unless he sewed it. **6** The House of Shammai says: One may not immerse hot liquids in cold, nor cold in hot, nor clean in unclean, nor unclean in clean. The House of Hillel says: One may immerse a vessel that is full of liquids. If he immersed it, it is as if he did not immerse it. If it is full of urine, they view them as if they were water. If it is full of purification waters, [he must wait] until the water [of the immersion pool] exceeds the purification waters. Rabbi Yose says: Even if the vessel holds a <term>kor</term> <gloss>a large dry measure</gloss> and contains only a <term>revi'it</term> <gloss>a quarter-log measure</gloss>, it is as if he did not immerse it. **7** All foods combine to render the body <note>the hands</note> impure at a volume of half a <term>pras</term> <gloss>half a loaf</gloss>. All liquids combine to render the body impure at a volume of a <term>revi'it</term>. This is a stringency regarding one who drinks impure liquids, compared to one who eats, as he treats other liquids like water. **8** If he ate impure foods and drank impure liquids, he immersed and vomited. They are impure because they are not pure in the body. If he drank impure water, he immersed and vomited. They are pure because they are pure in the body. If he swallowed a pure ring, entered the tent of a corpse, and then learned and immersed and vomited it, it remains as it was. If he swallowed an impure ring, he immerses and eats of the <term>terumah</term> <gloss>priestly heave-offering</gloss>. If he vomited it, it is impure. And anything outside that is severed, like a person, when it is visible, it is an interposition; and if it is not visible, he immerses and eats of his <term>terumah</term>.
