continues from previous page <meta>continues from previous page: ...He established that everything emerges from there.</meta> **Rabbi Eleazar said:** Learn from this that Jacob emerged from the harsh judgment, for Isaac indeed held fast to the portion of harsh judgment. **Rabbi Shimon** said to him: This is so on its own, yet Isaac himself emerged from Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss>, and likewise all judgment emerges from mercy, and mercy from judgment. Abraham inherited the legacy of loving-kindness; Isaac emerged in judgment from within loving-kindness; Jacob emerged in mercy from within harsh judgment. Thus it is above, one from the other, and one draws from the other, until everything is recognized as being one, and from the one, all depend, and all are found to be one. Blessed be His name forever and to all eternity. **Rabbi Eleazar said:** It is recognized that there is no wholeness unless one holds to the other, and the one holds to both, in order to perfect everything, such as Jacob, and this is what is written:
> "He fled from end to end."

It is taught: This side is not called such except from this side, and from this side everything is recognized, for above, everything rises in one balance <term>metkala</term> <gloss>scale of judgment/balance</gloss>; it does not change and will not change, as it is written:
> "I, the Lord, have not changed."

**Rabbi Judah said:** All these are shining lights, from the One, and upon the One they depend, and these lights are one—everything—and they do not wish to be separated; and he who separates them is as if he had separated himself from the life of the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said, it is written:
> "And I will give youths to be their princes, and children shall rule over them."

This is what is written, "And you shall make two <term>keruvim</term> <gloss>cherubim</gloss> of gold," and it is written, "He who sits upon the cherubim," and it is written, "And He rode upon a cherub and flew." "He who sits upon the cherubim"—when He begins to be seated in wholeness, it is written "He who sits upon the cherubim" <note>alternatively: when He is found in wholeness</note>; "And He rode upon a cherub"—one, when the King is not seated upon His throne. "He who sits upon the cherubim" [implies] two. **Rabbi Yose said:** Woe to the world when one cherub turns its face away from its companion, for it is written:
> "And their faces shall be toward one another."

When there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac said:** We have learned, "You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father nor the nakedness of your mother." Woe to the one who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner, it is written concerning Jacob, "He fled from end to end." Fortunate is the portion of Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, boasts in their praises, as it is written:
> "Israel, in whom I will be glorified."

It is taught: **Rabbi Isaac said:** In the early days, a person would say to his companion, "Tell me one word and take a coin from me." Now, a person says to his companion, "Take a coin from me and occupy yourself with the Torah," and there is no one who pays attention and no one who inclines his ear, except for those few holy, exalted ones in whom the Holy One, blessed be He, boasts, as it is written:
> "And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified."

"Woe to the pillars and their rings of silver." **Rabbi Isaac** said, "Woe to the pillars"—I have already said, all those that are joined in the knots of the upper existences are called "woe to the pillars," and all those below depend upon those rings. What are the rings? Six within six, and they are joined and watered by the thread of the spine that stands upon them. And in the <term>Sefer de-Tzeni'uta</term> <gloss>Book of Concealment</gloss>, it is taught: rings above and rings below, and all rise in one balance. What is the concealment of the book? **Rabbi Shimon said:** There are five chapters that are included in the Great Palace and fill the entire earth. **Rabbi Judah said:** If they are included in this way, they are superior to all. **Rabbi Shimon said:** This is so for one who enters and exits, but for one who does not enter and exit, it is not so.

A parable for a person who lived among the mountains and did not know the dwellings of the town. He planted wheat <term>chittin</term> <gloss>wheat</gloss> and ate wheat in its raw form. One day he entered the town. They brought him good bread. He asked, "What is this?" They said, "It is bread, to be eaten." He ate and tasted it greatly upon his palate. He asked, "And from what is this made?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him cakes kneaded with oil. He tasted them and said, "And these, from what are they made?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him royal pastries kneaded with honey and oil. He said, "And these, from what are they made?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Certainly, I am the master of all these that I am eating, for the essence of all of these is wheat." And because of that...

<summary>This page explores the interplay between Mercy and Judgment through the symbolism of the Cherubim and the "rings and pillars" of the Tabernacle. It concludes with a parable of a villager who discovers that all refined food products are derived from wheat, illustrating the Zoharic concept of the underlying divine unity within diverse manifestations.</summary>
<keywords>Cherubim, Jacob, Mercy, Judgment, Balance, Torah, Wheat, Divine Unity, Tabernacle, Pillars</keywords>

text:
(XXVI)

->APPENDIX B.<-

For Hatred. I call upon you, evil spirit, and destructive spirit <note>original: "shada" <gloss>demon/spirit</gloss></note>, and spirit without mercy. I call upon you, evil spirit, you who dwell in the graveyard and take hold of the cloak of human beings. You shall go, tie a knot upon <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> <note>often abbreviated in manuscripts as "Ploni son of Ploni"</note> on his head, his eyes, his mouth, his tongue, his throat, and his entrails, and you shall pour filthy water into his belly. And if you do not go and pour water into his belly, I will send upon you evil ones: the angels Puziel, Guzael, Pasdiel, and Pruzael. I have summoned you and bound you <note>emending the text based on the note "ve-kiturei" <gloss>and bindings</gloss></note> so that you go immediately upon <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> and pour filthy water into his belly, and kill <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear>, for this is what I desire. A.A.S.

For Hatred. Write upon an egg laid that day, in the grave of a Christian <note>original: "Natzrani" <gloss>Christian/Nazarene</gloss></note>. I adjure you by the hidden things of heaven and earth: just as the heavens were separated from the earth, so shall you separate and divide <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> and <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and separate them one from another, as the living were separated from the dead, and as the sea was separated from the dry land, and the water from the river, and the mountain from the valley, and the night from the day, and the light from the darkness, and the sun from the moon. So shall you separate <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> from <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and separate them one from another, by the twelve hours of the day and three hours of the night, and the seven days of the week, and the thirty days of the month, and the seven years of release, and the fifty years of the jubilee, each and every day, in the name of the angel Tamtamiel, the satan, and in the name of the angel Ziabael, and in the name of the angel Darsamiel, and in the name of the angel Zahabuch, and in the name of the angel Da'af, and in the name of the angel Zehazmael, and in the name of the angel Sasniel, who is appointed over the pain, and over the <unclear>finitah</unclear> <gloss>uncertain term, perhaps affliction</gloss> and the <unclear>tzacha</unclear> and the <unclear>hadrozofa</unclear>. Separate <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> from <unclear>So-and-so son of So-and-so</unclear> his wife, and let them distance themselves, one from the other, and let them not be able to find comfort in one another, in a hurry and in pain. Complete.

<summary>This page contains two magical spells for inciting hatred and separation between individuals, utilizing demonic invocation and symbolic analogies of cosmic division.</summary>
<keywords>hatred, separation, demonology, Aramaic incantations, Puziel, magic rituals, sympathetic magic</keywords>

text:
# The Apostle

<meta>continues from previous page</meta> he began to speak: 12 And the priest of the god <note>The Hebrew text uses "אלדים" (Elohim), which in this context refers to the pagan deity Zeus.</note> who was outside the city brought bulls and wreaths to the opening of the house where they were staying, and he wished to offer a sacrifice to them. 13 When Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and leaped out to the gathering of the people, and they were shouting: 14 And they said, "Men, why are you doing this? We are also human beings just like you, and we feel just as you do. We tell you that you should turn away from these empty things and turn to the living God, He who made the heaven and the earth and the seas and everything that is in them." 15 He is the one who in previous generations allowed all the nations to go in the way of their own choosing. 16 Even so, He did not leave Himself without a sign, so that people would take heed of Him. He did good things for them from heaven and brought down rain for them, and He caused their fruits to grow in their seasons and filled their hearts with food and joy. 17 And since they spoke thus, the people saw them and said that no man should offer them any sacrifice. 18 And Jews came there from <term>Iconium</term> and from <term>Antioch</term> and stirred up the people against them, and they stoned Paul and threw him outside the city because they thought he was dead. 20 But the disciples gathered around him, and he rose and entered the city, and on the second day he left from there with Barnabas, and they came to the city of <term>Derbe</term>. 21 And when they had taught the people of that city and the number of their disciples had increased, they returned to the city of <term>Lystra</term> and to <term>Iconium</term> and to the city of <term>Antioch</term>. 22 And they strengthened the believers among themselves.

<summary>Paul and Barnabas reject the people's attempt to worship them as gods, urging them to turn to the living God. Despite being stoned by incited crowds, they continue their missionary journey.</summary>
<keywords>Paul, Barnabas, Lystra, Iconium, Antioch, Derbe, mission, faith</keywords>

text:
For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are a hint to the seven kingdoms. And likewise, what are these for <term>chariots</term> <gloss>the literal reading of the word used in the text</gloss>, the matter of their being alive for them.

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. In which the black horses go out toward the north country, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out toward the south country. And the strong ones went out, and sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth, and he said, 'Go, walk to and fro in the earth.' And they walked to and fro in the earth. Then he cried out to me, and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.'"

**And he answered.** These are the four spirits. Similar to the seven spirits. And likewise "he came to Jerusalem" as if [written] "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: for the seven, a black son as for a white son. And those similar to it. For the seven, the fourth part of the chariots, and they go out to the seven spirits of the heavens. As if to give authority to the seven kingdoms to rule in the seven spirits, each one in its time. As if for everything in the world, that which is the seven of strength. "Standing before the Lord of all the earth." As if in the mission of God, that He granted them power over this. Like "the sons of God came to stand before the Lord" <margin>Job 2</margin>. **In which.** The black ones. And he mentioned the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, which were in everything to destroy it, and after that they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. And the white ones, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them, for the kingdom is <unclear>broken</unclear>. That Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him and reigned, and after that [the] <term>Kuz</term> <gloss>unknown term</gloss> and <term>Kakhis</term> <gloss>unknown term</gloss> after him in all the world. **And the dappled ones went out toward the south country.** Which were a holy part, as it passed, for Rome is <unclear>different</unclear>, and Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece. And at the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern, and in all the lands the sons of Greece were reigning. And Caesar prevailed over them, and he transferred the kingdom from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans. **And the strong ones.** They are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael, which mustered itself to seek a kingdom to be a place that would be for <unclear>tranquility</unclear> for them, a spirit for them. And this is what he said, "And they sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth." **And he said.** Meaning, he gave them permission to walk to and fro and to conquer lands. **Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me, "**See, those that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country**," meaning the portion of the black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>This page provides a detailed symbolic interpretation of the four chariots and their horses, linking them to historical kingdoms including Babylon, Media and Persia, Greece, and Rome, while discussing the emergence of the kingdom of Ishmael.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four spirits, Babylon, Media and Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Alexander of Macedon</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
found that the kingdoms already seen were a hint to the seven kingdoms <note>likely referring to historical stages of the four major empires</note>. And so, "What are these, my lord?" is an inquiry into the nature of my life within them.

### Zechariah 6

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses goes out to the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out to the south country. And the strong went out and sought to go, to walk about the earth; and he said, 'Go, walk about the earth.' So they walked about the earth. Then he called out to me and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those who go out to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.'"

**And he answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like "to the four winds." Similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" means "to Jerusalem." Alternatively, "a white son of a black" <note>an idiomatic or grammatical comparison</note> is like "to a white son of black," and others like it. He divided the four chariots as going out to the four winds of the heavens. This was to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time. This refers to the whole world, as the language implies strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth": this means by the mission of God who gave them dominion over this, just as it is written <margin>Job 2</margin> "and the sons of God came to stand before the Lord."

**The one in which.** "The black." He mentioned the black ones because the time of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the north country, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white," which is the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them," for that kingdom was swift as lightning. Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he reigned, and after him his successors ruled throughout the whole world.

In the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks were ruling in all lands, but Augustus Caesar prevailed over them, and he transferred the kingdom from the Greeks and returned it to the Romans.

For I have already seen the visions that are a hint to the four kingdoms. If so, what are these? For what purpose did I see them?

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. In which the black horses go out to the north country, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the south country. And the strong ones went out and sought to go, to roam through the earth; and He said, 'Go, roam through the earth,' and they roamed through the earth. And He called out to me and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those that go out to the north country have set my spirit at rest in the north country.'"

**And he answered:** "These are four spirits," like "to the four spirits." And similarly, "And he came to Jerusalem" <note>meaning "to Jerusalem"</note>; "Son of Saul" <margin>II Samuel 4:1</margin> <note>meaning "to the son of Saul"</note>, and others like them. That is to say, these four chariots go out to the four spirits of the heavens, meaning to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each in its time; that is, in the whole world, which has four corners. "Standing before the Lord of all the earth," meaning in the mission of God, who sent them for this, as it is said, "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord" <margin>Job 2</margin>. **In which:** The black ones—and he did not mention the red ones because the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the north country, which is Babylon, to destroy it, and afterwards they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. And the white ones, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them, for their kingdom grew strong; for Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he and those who came after him reigned over the whole world. **And the dappled ones went out to the south country:** Which is the land of the south, because Rome is northern, and Julius Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight the kingdom of Greece, and at the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern, and in all the lands the people of Greece were reigning then. And this Julius Caesar overcame them, and he transferred the kingdom from the people of Greece and returned it to the Romans. **And the strong ones:** These are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael, who strengthened themselves of their own accord to seek a kingdom wherever it might be; therefore, no spirit was described for them, and this is what it says: "And they sought to go, to roam through the earth." **And he said:** Meaning, He gave them permission to roam and to conquer lands. **And he called out:** Meaning, He cried out to me with a loud voice and said to me, "**See, those that go out to the north country have set my spirit at rest in the north country,**" meaning these black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>This page continues the commentary on the vision of the four chariots in Zechariah, interpreting the colored horses as representations of the historical succession of the Babylonian, Medo-Persian, Greek, and Roman empires, with an added note on the kingdom of Ishmael.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, Four Kingdoms, Babylon, Media and Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Julius Caesar, Alexander of Macedon</keywords>

And the angel answered and said to me: "These are the four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses go out to the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out to the south country. And the strong went out and sought to go, to walk about through the earth; and he said: 'Go, walk about through the earth.' So they walked about through the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying: 'Behold, those who go out to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.'"

**And he answered:** "These are the four spirits" is like "to the four spirits." Likewise, "and he came Jerusalem" <margin>2 Chronicles 1</margin> is like "to Jerusalem"; "son of Saul" <margin>2 Samuel 4</margin> is like "to the son of Saul," and similar cases. He means that these four chariots go out to the four spirits of the heavens, meaning to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each one in its time; that is to say, in the whole world, which has four sides. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth" means by the mission of God who sent them for this, just as it says: "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord" <margin>Job 2</margin>.

**The one in which:** The black. He did not mention the red horses because the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the north country, which is Babylon, to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white," which is the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them" because their kingdom grew strong; for Alexander of Macedon <note>Alexander the Great</note>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he and those who came after him ruled afterward over the entire world.

**And the dappled went out to the south country:** Which is the land of the south <gloss>the Negev/Egypt</gloss>. This is because Rome is northern, and Julius Caesar, who ruled over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece. At the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern. At that time, the sons of Greece were ruling in all the lands, and this Julius Caesar overcame them; he transferred the sovereignty from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans.

**And the strong:** <term>Ha-amutzim</term> <gloss>the strong/determined ones</gloss>. These are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>the Arab/Islamic conquests</note> who strengthened themselves on their own to seek a kingdom in whatever place it might be. Therefore, he did not designate a specific direction <note>spirit/wind</note> for them. This is what is meant by "and they sought to go, to walk about through the earth."

**And he said:** Meaning, He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**And he cried out:** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me: **"Behold, those who go out to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the black horses who went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<note>original: "ראשו ונופל על פניו ועל צור יי' השר כשהוא רואה את"</note> head and falls upon his face. And when Zakufael, the Prince of the Lord <note>original: "יי' השר"</note>, sees <term>Zakufael</term> <gloss>the prince charged with recording the merits of Israel</gloss>, the Prince of the Lord who is appointed to write the merits of Israel that are performed before the Throne of Glory, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And when Zakfiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord who guards the keys of the palaces of the Arabot firmament, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Anafiel? Because the branch <note>original: "ענף"</note> of his splendor, his majesty, his crown, his radiance, and his brilliance covers all the splendors of the highest Arabot firmament like the Creator of the world. Just as of the Supreme Creator it is written, "His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise," so too does Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord, cover with his splendor and his majesty all the splendors of the highest Arabot. And when Anafiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Kotertashiel, the great, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Kotertashiel? Because he is appointed in purity over the four heads of the River of Fire <note>original: "נהר נור"</note> that is before the Throne of Glory. And every single prince who goes out and enters before the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss> does not go out or enter except by his authority, for the boundaries of the four heads of the River of Fire are entrusted to his hand. And not only that, but the majority of his height is seventy thousand myriads of <term>parsaot</term> <gloss>leagues/parasangs</gloss>, and he is the crown-prince <note>original: "כותרתשי"</note> of the River of Fire, and he goes out and enters before the <term>Shekhinah</term> to interpret the merits of all who enter the world, as it is written: "The court sat in judgment, and the books were opened." And when Kotertashiel, the Prince of the Lord, sees Shaqed-Hazyah, the great, mighty, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, he would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Shaqed-Hazyah? Because he weighs all merits on a pair of scales before the Holy One, blessed be He. And when Shaqed-Hazyah, the Prince of the Lord, sees Zephanuri, the great, mighty, awesome, and honored Prince of the Lord, and the splendor revered by all the heavenly host, he removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is his name called Zephanuri? Because he breathes into him in purity...

<summary>This page continues the liturgical description of the celestial hierarchy, detailing the ritual of bowing and removing crowns performed by various angelic princes before their superiors, specifically focusing on the roles of Anafiel, Kotertashiel, Shaqed-Hazyah, and Zephanuri.</summary>
<keywords>Hekhalot, Angelology, Divine Throne, Arabot, Prince of the Lord, Celestial Hierarchy, Shekhinah</keywords>

his head and falls upon his face. And Galitzur Y. <note>original: "יי'"</note> the prince, when he sees Zakzakiel Y. the prince—who is appointed to record the merits of Israel that they perform before the Throne of Glory—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And Zakzakiel Y. the prince, when he sees Anaphiel Y. the prince—who guards the keys to the palaces of Arabot <note>the seventh and highest heaven</note>—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. 

And why is he called Anaphiel? Because the branch <term>anaf</term> <gloss>branch</gloss> of his splendor, his majesty, his crown, his radiance, and his luminosity covers all the dwellings of the supreme Arabot, like the Creator of the world. For of the supreme Creator, it is written: "His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise." So too does Anaphiel Y. the prince cover with his splendor and majesty all the dwellings of the supreme Arabot. 

And Anaphiel Y. the prince, when he sees Soter-Ashiel Y. the prince—the great, the awesome, and the honored—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is he called Soter-Ashiel? Because he is appointed by decree over the four heads of the River of Fire <term>nahar denur</term> <gloss>river of fire</gloss> toward the Throne of Glory. And every prince who goes out or enters before the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss> does not go out or enter except by his authority, because the seals of the four heads of the River of Fire are entrusted to his hand. Furthermore, his stature is seventy thousand myriads of <term>parsa'ot</term> <gloss>leagues</gloss>, and he hides the fire of the River of Fire and goes out and enters before the Shekhinah to explain the writings of all who enter the world, in the matter of what is said: "The judgment sat, and the books were opened." 

And Soter-Ashiel Y. the prince, when he sees Shaqed-Hozai Y. the prince—the great, the mighty, the awesome, and the honored—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is he called Shaqed-Hozai? Because he weighs all merits on a balance scale before the Holy One, blessed be He. And Shaqed-Hozai Y. the prince, when he sees Zeh-Panori Y. the prince—the great, the mighty, the awesome, the honored, the majestic, the revered in the entire celestial retinue—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is he called Zeh-Panori? Because he rages <note>or "frowns" / "is wrathful"</note> at him.

<summary>This passage describes a ritual hierarchy of celestial princes in the seventh heaven (Arabot), where each prince removes his crown of glory and bows upon seeing his superior, detailing the specific titles and divine functions of figures like Anaphiel, Soter-Ashiel, Shaqed-Hozai, and Zeh-Panori.</summary>
<keywords>Hekhalot, celestial hierarchy, Arabot, Throne of Glory, Shekhinah, River of Fire, divine service, angelic princes</keywords>
